# Lua API reference

<!-- Generated by tools/apidoc.lua from the source's comments: do not edit. -->

Each public function of the `paw` modules, module by module, with the
comment from its source. [Scripts](scripting.md) and
[Extensions](extensions.md) tell how the functions work together. The
functions of the kernel (`paw.api`, plain data in and out) are at the end.
`runtime/types/paw.lua` contains the same data for editors (LuaLS).

## Module paw

- `paw.add_track(opts)`: A new track, last unless `opts.index` says where: `opts` as `paw.api.track_add` takes them (`name`, `volume`, `output` as a track or an id, ...). In a window inside a subproject, the track is made in that subproject unless `opts.nest` says another.
- `paw.bounce(track, opts)`: Render a track with its devices to audio, as one clip on a new track immediately below it, and mute the original. The new track sends its sound where the original sent it. It uses `paw.render`, so `render.before` runs. `opts.name` is the name of the new track ("<name> (bounced)" by default). `opts.tail` is the seconds rendered after its last clip (2). Returns the new track, or nil when the track has no clips.
- `paw.buftype(name, def)`: Make a buffer type. See `docs/reference/lua-views.md`.

  ```lua
  paw.buftype("notes", { create = function(target) return {} end, render = function(win, canvas, ctx) end })
  ```

  The fields are these. `create(target, buf)` gives the state of the buffer. `render(win, canvas, ctx)` draws (`ctx.buf` is the buffer, and `win.state` is the state of the window). `on_key(win, key)` gets keys with no mapping. Also `on_mouse(win, event)`, `title(buf)` and `bufname(target, buf)`. `options` is the options of the buffer at the start.

  `listed` false keeps its buffers off `:ls`, and forgets each buffer when no window shows it. Also `delete(buf)` and `time` (see `timebind`). `claims(name)` tells if a name is a target of the type by its form (`:vs paw://lane/3`). `window()` is the window to draw when no window in the tabs shows the type (one in a separate window of a graphical frontend). Map keys for its windows with `{ view = name }`.

  A type can also do all that a view can do, for each window. `grid(win)` is the cursor that the keymap moves, as the `grid` of a view. `describe(win)` is the text of `K`. `status(win, ctx)` is the `view` component of the status line. Also `subscope(win)`, `paint(win, g, ctx)` and `pointer(win, e)` (pixels in a graphical frontend), and `help`.

  It can also have the fields that `paw.layout.powers` maps: `keymaps`, `motions`, `textobjects` and `operators`. Their functions get `ctx.win` and `ctx.buf`.
- `paw.cancel(handle)`: Stop a timer: `handle` is what `paw.defer` or `paw.every` returned.
- `paw.clip(id)`: The clip of an id, as a `paw.Clip`.
- `paw.cmd(name, args, ctx)`: Run a command. `args` is a table of arguments. `ctx` adds fields such as `count`.
- `paw.defer(fn, ms)`: Run `fn` once, after `ms` milliseconds (or when the current turn ends).
- `paw.device(id)`: The device, clip or automation lane of an id, as an object.
- `paw.device_types()`: Descriptions of each kind of device that you can add to a track. A kind that an extension added (`paw.plugins.add_dir`) has its extension in `from`.
- `paw.emit(event, payload)`: Call each handler for `event` (a name, or a descriptor). paw reports a handler that fails, and goes to the next. Returns true, or false and the reason when a handler returned `false, reason`. So a handler refuses the request of an event (`edit.before`, `project.saving`, `key.pre`).
- `paw.every(ms, fn)`: Run `fn` every `ms` milliseconds. Returns a handle for `paw.cancel`.
- `paw.failure(err)`: What a user sees of an error: one line, without the list of calls. The place in the code (`paw/x.lua:12:`) moves to the end, where it does not hide what went wrong. The whole error goes to the log.
- `paw.flush()`: Send the change events for the edits made until now. The kernel does this at the end of each turn. Call `paw.flush()` to make handlers run sooner.
- `paw.import_audio(path, opts)`: Bring a sound file into the project: on a new track named after the file (or on `opts.track`), at the cursor (or `opts.start`). Returns the clip.
- `paw.inspect(value, indent, seen)`: Render any value as readable Lua-like text.
- `paw.is_audio_file(path)`: True if a path names a sound file, from its file ending.
- `paw.is_chain_file(path)`: True if a path names a chain file of devices: a `devices.json`.
- `paw.lane(id)`: The automation lane of an id, as a `paw.Lane`.
- `paw.notify(text, level)`: Show a message. `level` is "info" (default), "warn" or "error".
- `paw.off(id)`: Stop a listener: `id` is the value that `paw.on` or `paw.once` returned.
- `paw.on(event, fn, opts)`: Listen for an event: in Lua its name or a pattern as text, in Teal its descriptor (`paw.events.event`). Returns a handle for `paw.off`.
- `paw.once(event, fn)`: Listen for an event once: the handler is removed after its first call.
- `paw.open(path, opts)`: Open what a path names: a folder that is no project as a list of its files, a sound file as a new track, anything else as a project, with plugins offline as `opts` says (see `paw.loading.open`).
- `paw.open_chain(path)`: Open a chain file (a `devices.json`) alone, as a new project with no file: one track with its devices, and the device panel on it. `:w` writes the chain back to its file. Returns the track.
- `paw.redo`: the same as `paw.api.redo`.
- `paw.render_cancel()`: Stop the render in the background, and the renders that wait after it. paw does not write its file. Returns true if a render ran.
- `paw.render_status()`: The render in the background: `{ path, fraction, seconds, cancelling, stage, queued }`, or nil. `stage` is "rendering", or "encoding" when ffmpeg makes a lossy file from the render. Then `fraction` tells how far the encoding is.
- `paw.render_stems(dir, opts)`: Render each track on its own into a directory, one file per track named after it: stems. A track is rendered with what it passes through on the way to the master, as when it is soloed, so that the stems add up to the mix. `opts` is as for `paw.render`, plus `tracks` to choose which (all that are not muted, by default) and `format` ("wav", "flac", "mp3", "ogg" or "opus"). With `background`, they are rendered one after another. Returns the files.
- `paw.render_tags(set)`: What the project's rendered files are tagged with (`project.meta.tags`): `paw.render_tags()` gives `{ title, artist, album, track, year, genre, comment, cover }` as far as set; `paw.render_tags({ artist = "Me" })` sets those fields and keeps the others, an empty string takes one out. A relative `cover` is from the project's directory.
- `paw.restore_clip(snap, track)`: Add a clip from a snapshot to a track.
- `paw.restore_device(snap, track, index)`: Add a device from a snapshot to a track, at the end of the chain or at the 1-based `index`.
- `paw.restore_track(snap, index)`: Make a track from a snapshot, at a 1-based position in the track list.
- `paw.track(which)`: A track by id, or by name.
- `paw.tracks()`: Every track, in order, as `paw.Track` objects (the master is `paw.master`).
- `paw.try(fn, ...)`: Call a function. If it fails, show the error as a message and do not raise it. Returns true and the results of the function, or false and the error. The message is the first lines of the error (`paw.failure`). The log keeps the list of calls.
- `paw.undo`: the same as `paw.api.undo`.
- `paw.wait`: the same as `paw.api.wait`.

## Module paw.Clip

- `paw.Clip:add_note(note)`

  ```lua
  clip:add_note({ pitch = "E4", start = 1, length = 0.5, velocity = 90 })
  clip:add_note({ pitch = "G4", start = 2, attr = paw.attr.m2("11.A") })   -- pizzicato
  ```

  Returns the note's place among the clip's notes.
- `paw.Clip:add_notes(notes)`: Add several notes as one edit (as `add_note` takes each).
- `paw.Clip:controls()`: The events of the clip that are not notes: controller moves, the pitch wheel, pressure and program changes. Each is `{ start, type, value }`, with `start` in beats from the start of the clip. `type` is "cc" (with `number`), "bend" (-1 to 1), "pressure", "registered" or "assignable" (with `bank` and `index`), or "program" (with `program` and maybe `bank`). Values go from 0 to 1 at any resolution. With `key`, a move is for the note on that key only, as in MIDI 2.0: its own bend, pressure or controller.
- `paw.Clip:data()`: The data of a clip of a kind (`paw.clip_kinds.data`).
- `paw.Clip:duplicate(opts)`: Copy the clip. By default the copy goes right after the original.
- `paw.Clip:edit_notes(edit)`: Change, remove and add several notes as one edit. Every index is a note's place before the call:

  ```lua
  clip:edit_notes({ set = { { index = 3, start = 1 } }, remove = { 5, 6 }, add = { note } })
  ```
- `paw.Clip:exists()`: True if the clip is still in the project.
- `paw.Clip:get()`: Everything about the clip as plain data (`paw.api.clip_get`).
- `paw.Clip:note_at(pitch, beat)`: The note on a pitch that sounds at a beat of the clip, and its place in the notes of the clip. Nothing when there is no such note.
- `paw.Clip:notes(range)`: The notes of a MIDI clip: a list of { pitch, start, length, velocity }. `start` is in beats from the start of the clip. A note can have `meta`, a table of extension data such as a lyric. A note can also have `attr`, the MIDI 2.0 attribute of its note-on (`{ type, data }`, see `paw.attr`).

  With a range, only the notes that sound in it. The second value is then the place of each note in the whole list, for `set_note` and `remove_note`:

  ```lua
  local notes, at = clip:notes({ from = 4, to = 8, low = "C3", high = "C5" })
  ```
- `paw.Clip:peaks(n)`: The waveform of an audio clip: `n` { min, max, rms } entries. Each entry covers an equal part of the sound of the clip, scaled by its gain. It gives how far the wave goes each way (-1 to 1) and how loud it is there. paw keeps the result, so the code that draws can ask for it each frame.
- `paw.Clip:remove()`: Take the clip out of its track.
- `paw.Clip:remove_note(index)`: Remove the note at a place among the clip's notes (from 1).
- `paw.Clip:set_controls(controls)`

  ```lua
  clip:set_controls({ { start = 0, type = "cc", number = 64, value = 1 },
                      { start = 1, type = "bend", key = "E4", value = 0.02 } })
  ```
- `paw.Clip:set_data(data)`: Give a clip of a kind new data, as one undo step (`paw.clip_kinds.set`).
- `paw.Clip:set_note(index, fields)`: Change one note, by its place in the notes of the clip (from 1). The other notes do not change: `clip:set_note(3, { length = 2 })`. Returns the new place of the note, because notes stay in the order of their start. `attr = false` removes its attribute.
- `paw.Clip:set_notes(notes)`: Replace every note of the clip with `notes` (as `add_note` takes each).
- `paw.Clip:snapshot()`: The clip as plain data, for `paw.restore_clip`.
- `paw.Clip:track()`: The track the clip is on.

## Module paw.Device

- `paw.Device:automate(param)`: The lane for a parameter, made if there is none yet.

  ```lua
  synth:automate("cutoff"):add(0, 200)
  ```
- `paw.Device:automate_state()`: The device's state lane, made if there is none yet: a lane whose points each give the device one of the lane's states, from that point on.

  ```lua
  local lane = amp:automate_state()
  lane:set_state(16, lane:add_state(amp:capture("crunch")))
  ```
- `paw.Device:capture(name)`: The device's whole state now, as a state lane takes it: `{ name, state, params }`. The plugin's saved state, and the parameters set in the project.
- `paw.Device:close_editor()`: Close the plugin's own window.
- `paw.Device:exists()`: True if the device is still in the project.
- `paw.Device:get()`: Everything about the device as plain data (`paw.api.device_get`).
- `paw.Device:info()`: The description of this device: its name, category, format, and its parameters with their ranges. A plugin's parameters are those of this instance, which is the only place they are known.
- `paw.Device:lane(param)`: The lane for a parameter, if there is one.
- `paw.Device:lanes()`: The automation lanes of the device's parameters, as `paw.Lane` objects.
- `paw.Device:move(index, track)`: Move within the chain, or to another track: `device:move(1)`, `device:move(2, other)`.
- `paw.Device:open_editor()`: Show the plugin's own window.
- `paw.Device:remove()`: Take the device off its track.
- `paw.Device:restart()`: Show the window of the plugin. `device.editor` is "open", "closed", or nil for devices that have no window. Start the device again: for a plugin that stopped (`stopped` tells why) or did not load. It returns with the last state of it in the project.
- `paw.Device:set(name, value)`: Set one parameter, or several from a table.

  ```lua
  device:set("cutoff", 800)
  device:set({ cutoff = 800, resonance = 0.4 })
  ```
- `paw.Device:set_offline(on)`: Set the device offline, or online again. An offline device is not made (a plugin has no process), and the chain passes over it. Its state and parameters do not change.
- `paw.Device:set_output(pair, track)`: Play the output pair `pair` of the device (2 and more: the first pair plays on its own track) into a track, or nowhere with nil. `device.outputs` is a table of pair number to track id. `device.ports.outputs` names the pairs.
- `paw.Device:set_sidechain(track, opts)`: Listen to the sound of a different track as the side-chain of the device. With `comp:set_sidechain(kick)`, a compressor on the bass ducks under the kick. `{ pre = true }` takes the sound before the fader, pan and mute of that track. nil (or no track) removes the side-chain. `device.sidechain` is the id of the track.
- `paw.Device:snapshot()`: The device as plain data, for `paw.restore_device`. For a plugin, the data contains its state, which holds more than its parameters.
- `paw.Device:state_lane()`: The device's state lane, if it has one.
- `paw.Device:track()`: The track this device is on.
- `paw.Device:value_at(param, beat)`: The value of a parameter at a beat while the song plays. This is the value of the lane when the lane is on. If not, it is the value of the device.

## Module paw.Lane

- `paw.Lane:add(beat, value)`: Add a point. It replaces a point at the same beat. The value is in the units of the target: dB for volume and -1 to 1 for pan. For a parameter, it is in the range of the parameter.
- `paw.Lane:add_state(state)`: Add a state to a state lane, or replace the one of its name. Returns its index, from 0: the value of a point that gives it.
- `paw.Lane:clear()`: Remove every point of the lane.
- `paw.Lane:exists()`: True if the lane is still in the project.
- `paw.Lane:get()`: Everything about the lane as plain data (`paw.api.lane_get`).
- `paw.Lane:points()`: The points as a list of { beat, value }, sorted by beat.
- `paw.Lane:remove()`: Take the lane away, and the automation in it.
- `paw.Lane:set_points(points)`: Replace the points: `lane:set_points({ { 0, -60 }, { 8, 0 } })`. Points may also be written { beat = 0, value = -60 }.
- `paw.Lane:set_state(beat, which)`: Give the device a state of a state lane from `beat` on: a point that names the state by its name or its index.

  ```lua
  lane:set_state(16, "crunch")
  ```
- `paw.Lane:state_index(which)`: The index of a state of a state lane, by its name or its index. Nil when the lane has no such state.
- `paw.Lane:states()`: The states of a state lane: `{ name, state, params, call, program, bank }` each.
- `paw.Lane:track()`: The track the lane belongs to.
- `paw.Lane:value_at(beat)`: The value at a beat, when the lane is on and when it is off. Nil without points.

## Module paw.Track

- `paw.Track:add_clip(opts)`: Add a clip. With `file` it is an audio clip, otherwise a MIDI clip.

  ```lua
  track:add_clip({ start = 0, length = 4, notes = { { pitch = "C4", start = 0, length = 1 } } })
  track:add_clip({ start = 8, file = "take1.wav" })
  ```
- `paw.Track:add_device(kind, params, opts)`: Add a device to the end of the chain, or at the 1-based `opts.index`.

  ```lua
  track:add_device("synth", { cutoff = 800 })
  ```
- `paw.Track:automate(target)`: The lane for "volume" or "pan", made if there is none yet.

  ```lua
  track:automate("volume"):set_points({ { 0, -60 }, { 8, 0 } })
  ```
- `paw.Track:clip_at(beat)`: The clip that covers `beat`, if any. Where two clips overlap, the later clip wins.
- `paw.Track:clips()`: The track's clips, as `paw.Clip` objects.
- `paw.Track:device(which)`: The first device of a kind, or the device at a 1-based position.
- `paw.Track:devices()`: The track's devices in the order they process, as `paw.Device` objects.
- `paw.Track:duplicate()`: Copy the track with its devices, clips and automation, and put the copy after it.
- `paw.Track:exists()`: True if the track is still in the project.
- `paw.Track:get()`: A plain table with every field of the track, read once.
- `paw.Track:lane(target)`: The lane for "volume" or "pan", if there is one.
- `paw.Track:lanes()`: The automation lanes of the track, its devices' included.
- `paw.Track:meter()`: Peak level as linear `left, right`.
- `paw.Track:midi(event)`: Send a MIDI message to this track's devices now, outside the timeline: a controller, the pitch wheel, pressure, or with `key` one note's own.

  ```lua
  track:midi({ type = "cc", number = 1, value = 0.5 })
  track:midi({ type = "bend", value = -0.25 })
  track:midi({ type = "bend", key = "C4", value = 0.1 })
  ```
- `paw.Track:move(index)`: Move to a 1-based position in the track list.
- `paw.Track:note_off(pitch)`: Stop a note, or every note when `pitch` is left out.
- `paw.Track:note_on(pitch, velocity, attr)`: Start a note now, outside the timeline. `pitch` may be a name like "C4". With `attr`, a MIDI 2.0 attribute (`paw.attr`), the note carries it, and what the track's `attr_map` sends for it goes first.
- `paw.Track:play_note(pitch, velocity, ms, attr)`: Play a note for `ms` milliseconds (default 200), with `attr` if given.
- `paw.Track:remove()`: Take the track out of the project, with its clips and devices.
- `paw.Track:send(target, level, opts)`: Send some of this track's output to another track. `level` is in dB. With `{ pre = true }` the send is taken before the fader and pan, so it keeps its level when the fader moves: `vocal:send(reverb, -6, { pre = true })`.
- `paw.Track:snapshot()`: Everything about the track as plain data: its settings, devices (plugins with their state), clips and automation. `paw.restore_track` makes a track from it again, in this project or after the original is gone.
- `paw.Track:value_at(target, beat)`: The value of "volume" or "pan" at a beat while the song plays. This is the value of the lane when the lane is on. If not, it is the value of the track.

## Module paw.address

- `paw.address.children(uri)`: What an address holds, one level down.
- `paw.address.clip(id)`: A clip's address.
- `paw.address.device(id)`: A device's address, under its track's.
- `paw.address.edit(changes, label)`: Do a workspace edit. paw checks each change first, and does nothing unless it can do all changes. Then it makes all of them as one undo step with the label `label`. Returns true, or nil and the reason.

  ```lua
  paw.address.edit({ { uri = "paw://track/3", set = { volume = -6 } },
                     { uri = "paw://clip/7/note/41", set = { pitch = 62 } } }, "Lower the bass")
  ```
- `paw.address.find_note(clip, id)`: The note of a clip with an id, and its place in the clip (from 1).
- `paw.address.lane(id)`: An automation lane's address.
- `paw.address.location(uri, selector)`: A location: an address and, optionally, a part of it.
- `paw.address.marker(id)`: A marker's address.
- `paw.address.matches(pattern, uri)`: True if an address matches a pattern: `paw://track/*` (one level), `paw://track/**` (any depth), or an exact address.
- `paw.address.note(clip, id)`: A note's address: its clip, and the note's id there.
- `paw.address.of(object)`: The address of an object of the Lua interface (`paw.track(3)`, `paw.clip(7)`, a device), or of a table from `paw.api` (with its fields).
- `paw.address.param(device, key)`: A device parameter's address, by its key.
- `paw.address.parent(uri)`: The address that holds this one (a note's clip, a device's track), or nil.
- `paw.address.parse(uri)`: An address in parts: `{ kind = "note", track?, device?, param?, send?, clip?, note?, lane?, marker?, control?, number?, path?, segments }`, or nil when it is not one. The fragment (`#mix`) is kept as `fragment`.
- `paw.address.project()`: The addresses of the project, the tempo map, a track, a clip and a note. Also the addresses of a lane, a marker, a rendered file and a send, as `parse` reads them.
- `paw.address.render(path)`: A rendered file's address.
- `paw.address.resolve(uri)`: What an address names, as `paw.api` has it (a note also says its `place`; a parameter is `{ key, value, info }`), or nil when it is gone.
- `paw.address.scheme(name, spec)`: Add a kind of address, `paw://<name>/...`, for the data of an extension (the phrases of the vocal editor, the measures of a score). `spec.resolve(uri, parts)` gives the item or nil. The optional fields are `of(object)`, `children(uri, parts)` and `parent(uri, parts)`. For the quickfix list, `go(location, parts)` goes to an item and `where(location, parts)` names it in a few words. `edit(change, parts)` applies the change of a workspace edit to it. It must make its edits through `paw.api`, so the edits join the undo step.
- `paw.address.send(track, target)`: The address of a track's send to another.
- `paw.address.tempo()`: The tempo map's address.
- `paw.address.track(id)`: A track's address.
- `paw.address.track_of(uri)`: The track an address belongs to, if any.
- `paw.address.within(uri, ancestor)`: True if `uri` is `ancestor` or is inside it (a note inside its clip, a parameter inside its device and track). All addresses are inside the project.

## Module paw.annotation

- `paw.annotation.get(uri, exact)`: The labels on an address exactly (`exact`), or on it and what it holds.
- `paw.annotation.reset(namespace, doc)`: Forget the labels of a namespace, of one document or all. With no namespace, forget the labels of all namespaces.
- `paw.annotation.set(namespace, doc, list)`: Publish the labels of `namespace` in a document. They replace its old labels there.

## Module paw.attr

- `paw.attr.delay_of(track, attr)`: The milliseconds that a note with `attr` (nil for none) on `track` plays early (below 0) or late, from the `attr_map` of the track. So a library that speaks slowly still sounds on the beat. 0 without a map.
- `paw.attr.describe(attr)`: What an attribute is, for people: `{ code, tag, name, class, text }` (`code` and `class` only for articulations), where `tag` is a few letters for the piano roll and `text` one line for `K`. Nil for none.
- `paw.attr.m2(code, opts)`: An articulation's code as an attribute, or an attribute as its code (nil when it is not an articulation of M2-123). `opts` adds what a code leaves out: `variation` (0 to 15), `direction` ("down", "up", 1 or 2), `string` (1 to 7, highest first), `reset` (round robin).
- `paw.attr.parts(attr)`: The fields of an attribute's data, as M2-123 lays them out: `{ type, data, subclass, variation, direction, reset, string }`. Nil for none.
- `paw.attr.same(a, b)`: The same attribute: both none, or the same type and data.

## Module paw.audio

- `paw.audio.choices(track)`: All the possible inputs of a track, in order, under three headings (`group`). "audio" is none, each channel of the input device, and each pair of adjacent channels. "midi" is all ports, or one. "channel" is all MIDI channels, or one. Each is `{ group, label, checked, value }`. Give it to `M.choose`. A saved choice that is not available now is also in the list, marked as not found. So you can see it and change it.
- `paw.audio.choose(track, choice)`: Use a choice from `M.choices`. A track hears a MIDI port or channel only when it has no audio input. So a MIDI choice removes the audio input.
- `paw.audio.choose_engine(choice)`: Take a choice from `M.engine_choices`.
- `paw.audio.device()`: The input device's short name, or nil when there is none.
- `paw.audio.devices`: the same as `paw.api.audio_devices`.
- `paw.audio.engine_choices()`: The choices of the devices, under the headings (`group`) "output", "input", "block", "rate" and "backend" (the sound system). Each is `{ group, label, checked, value }` for `M.choose_engine`. The `info` lines are data that you cannot select.
- `paw.audio.label(t)`: What a track takes in, in a few words: `UR22mkII · 1/2` for audio, `MIDI · Keystation · ch 1` for MIDI from one port. Nil for a track that takes nothing in particular: no audio, and MIDI from everywhere.
- `paw.audio.level(t, levels)`: The level of the sound at the audio input of a track, 0 to 1. The track does not have to be armed or monitored. 0 for a track without an audio input.
- `paw.audio.levels`: the same as `paw.api.input_levels`.
- `paw.audio.load(cpu)`: How busy the engine is, 0 to 1, as the status line and all frontends show it. It is the load of its blocks, averaged over about one second, in steps of 2.5%. It changes only when the average leaves the step that shows. The load of one block changes all the time, more on a busy computer. If paw showed each change, the terminal would draw it again, and each window would draw a frame for it. `cpu` is the load that the caller read (`api.engine_get().cpu`), if the caller has it.
- `paw.audio.pick(track, groups)`: A picker of the inputs of a track (`I` on a track): monitoring first, then each choice of `M.choices`. With `groups` (`{ "midi", "channel" }`), only those choices: the MIDI input, as step input opens it.
- `paw.audio.short(name)`: The name of a device, made short enough for a track header. The name of the maker goes when a model number follows it, and a number at the end also goes.

  ```lua
  "Steinberg UR22mkII 0" → "UR22mkII", "Bose NC 700 HP" → "Bose NC 700 HP"
  ```
- `paw.audio.summary()`: The engine in a few words, for the transport bar: `pipewire · UR22mkII · 48 kHz`.
- `paw.audio.timing()`: Sample rate, block size and latencies in one line.
- `paw.audio.use(opts)`: Open other devices. `output` and `input` are a name or a part of a name (`"default"` for the default of the system). `buffer` is in frames (0 for the value of the device). `rate` is in Hz (0 for the value of the device). `backend` is the sound system (`"auto"`, `"pipewire"`, `"alsa"`, `"jack"`). The values that you do not give do not change. The choice is for this computer, and paw keeps it for the next run. A name that matches nothing is an error.

## Module paw.audition

- `paw.audition.builtin(track, at)`: A phrase for a track with nothing to play. For a drum track, it is a bar of a beat. For other tracks, it is the tonic chord of the key, held, then as an arpeggio up and down, in the range of the track. `{ notes, length, label }`.
- `paw.audition.file(path)`: Hear a sound file on its own, from its start, in place of whatever was.
- `paw.audition.has_instrument(track)`: True if a track has an instrument to play notes.
- `paw.audition.keep()`: Keep the trial's edits as one undo step.
- `paw.audition.midi_file(path, bars)`: Play the first `bars` bars of a MIDI file (2 when nil), at its own tempo, once: pitched parts through `player()`, its drums (channel 10) through a kit. Returns the label.
- `paw.audition.outline_lines(outline, width, rows, position, length)`: The outline of a sound file as `rows` lines `width` columns wide. The loudest part of each column goes up from the bottom. If `position` (seconds of `length`) is given, the column of that position is marked.
- `paw.audition.phrase(track, notes, opts)`: Play `notes` through a track, again each `opts.length` beats (or one time with `loop = false`). The notes are `{ pitch, start, length, velocity }`, with `start` in beats from the start of the phrase. The `track` of a note wins over the `track` of the phrase. `opts.label` tells what the phrase is. A phrase with the same `opts.key` as the phrase that plays continues and does not start again. So only the sound changes. `opts.tempo` is its tempo. If not given, it is the tempo of the project at `opts.at` (the cursor). paw plays nothing while the transport runs.
- `paw.audition.player(drums)`: A track to play notes through: the cursor's when it has an instrument, else one added as a trial (with the built-in synth, or drums) that `revert` takes away. `drums` asks for a drum kit.
- `paw.audition.quiet()`: Stop the sound of the audition (phrase and file). A trial does not change.
- `paw.audition.revert()`: Put the project back as it was before the trial, if there is one.
- `paw.audition.state()`: What you hear now: `{ kind = "phrase", label, track, notes, length, silent }`, `{ kind = "file", file, state, position, length, outline }` or nil. `trial` is true while the edits of a trial stay.
- `paw.audition.stop()`: Stop what is heard and take a trial back.
- `paw.audition.through(track)`: Play what a track plays around the cursor, through the track, again and again (`track_phrase`). So you hear a sound that you try on the track with its own notes. The loop continues while only the sound changes. Returns what you hear, in words.
- `paw.audition.track_phrase(track)`: What a track plays around the cursor, as a phrase. This is the bar of its MIDI clip at the cursor. If not, it is the last bar with notes before the cursor. If not, it is the first bar with notes. It is `builtin` when the track has no notes. `{ notes, length, label, at }`.
- `paw.audition.try(fn)`: Make the edits of `fn` as a trial, in place of the last trial. You hear and see them, and `revert` removes them with no trace. Returns the results of `fn`. If `fn` fails, paw removes the edits and raises the error.

## Module paw.autosave

- `paw.autosave.alternatives(path)`: The files that can replace the project file `path` when paw cannot open it. These are its `.bak` (the file before the last save) and the newest safety copy of it, newest first: { file, path, kind, time }.
- `paw.autosave.choices()`: Everything `:recover` offers: the stand-ins for a project that would not open, then the copies left by sessions that ended badly.
- `paw.autosave.copy(force)`: Write a copy now, if the project changed after the last copy (or with `force`, as when a take starts). Returns the written file, or nil.
- `paw.autosave.file()`: The file this session's copy of the project goes in: one per project file, or per session for a project that has no file yet.
- `paw.autosave.import_take(file)`: Import an orphaned take. It goes on the track that it was recorded for, if a track has the name that it starts with. If not, it goes on a new track. It goes at the start of the song.
- `paw.autosave.left_behind()`: The copies left by sessions that are gone: { file, path, name, time }.
- `paw.autosave.offer(path, err)`: Offer the alternatives to a project that would not open, if there are any: `:recover` lists them first. Returns how many there are.
- `paw.autosave.orphan_takes()`: Recorded takes in the `media` directory of the project that no clip uses, written after the last save of the project. A session that stopped during or after a take, without a save, leaves them. A take that you undid before a save is not one of them. { file, name }.
- `paw.autosave.recover(file, opts)`: Open a copy that a session left, as the project that it is a copy of. `opts.as_path` opens it under that file name (a `.bak`, which paw keeps). `opts.plugins_offline` opens it with all plugins offline, if a plugin possibly stopped the session.

## Module paw.bytes

- `paw.bytes.base64`: the same as `paw.api.base64_encode`.
- `paw.bytes.le16(n)`: Two bytes of an unsigned 16-bit number, little-endian.
- `paw.bytes.le32(n)`: Four bytes of an unsigned 32-bit number, little-endian.
- `paw.bytes.u16(data, at)`: The unsigned 16-bit little-endian number at `at` (from 1), or nil past the end.
- `paw.bytes.u32(data, at)`: The unsigned 32-bit little-endian number at `at` (from 1), or nil past the end.
- `paw.bytes.unbase64(text)`: The bytes of base64 text (either alphabet, padded or not, spaces and line ends passed over). Raises when the text is not base64.
- `paw.bytes.vst3_join(component, controller)`: A VST3 plugin's state as paw keeps it, from its component's part and its controller's part.
- `paw.bytes.vst3_split(raw)`: The component's part and the controller's part of a VST3 plugin's state as paw keeps it (each after its length, 32 bits, little-endian), or nil and why. A state without a controller part gives "" for it.

## Module paw.canvas

- `paw.canvas.back(name)`: Give the keyboard back to the main window from a view in a separate window. It goes to the window that had it before the view went there, else to the current window of the tab.
- `paw.canvas.button(g, hits, x, y, label, action, opts)`: A button: a rounded box with a label, painted with `g` and added to the hit list `hits` to run `action` (a function of the event, or a table as `Hits:add` takes) when pressed. `opts`: `width`, `height` (24), `fill`, `color`, `on` (lit, in `lit` or the selection's color), `size`. Returns where the next button goes to its right, and the width.
- `paw.canvas.cell_event(window, event, bare)`: A pointer event in pixels as the terminal gives it to the `on_mouse` of a view. It is in cells, with `kind` down, up, drag, `scroll_up` and other kinds, `button`, and `mods` ("C", "A", "S"). Nil for an event that the terminal cannot tell (the second click of a double click comes as down and up).
- `paw.canvas.close(name)`: Close the separate window of a view. The keyboard returns to the main window, where it was before. For a view docked in the layout, its window there closes, as `:close` does.
- `paw.canvas.dock(name)`: Put a view in a separate window back into the layout, with the keyboard. It goes where it was before it left the layout. If not, it goes where it docks. If not, it goes in a window split from the current window. paw does this when its separate window closes. `Ctrl-w d` in it does the same.
- `paw.canvas.draw(draw, px)`: The operations that a function draws on a painter of `px.w` by `px.h` pixels: what a strip shows (`buf:strip`). `draw(g, px)` gets the painter and `px`. If it fails, the error shows where it would draw.

  ```lua
  local ops = paw.canvas.draw(function(g, px) g:rect(0, 0, px.w, 2, { fill = "#ffffff" }) end, { w = 80, h = 40 })
  ```
- `paw.canvas.focus(name)`: Give a view in a window the keyboard, as a click in it does.
- `paw.canvas.glyph_outline(font, codepoint)`: A music font's glyph as commands and numbers in staff spaces from its origin, y down, from the fonts built into the kernel, or nil.
- `paw.canvas.hit_list()`: A list of places that the pointer acts on (see `view.hits`).
- `paw.canvas.image(bytes, w, h, format)`: Keep a picture of pixels for views to show (`g:image`, `buf:image`). `bytes` is a PNG file, or straight RGBA of `w` by `h` pixels row by row (`format` `"png"` or `"rgba"`; a PNG file is known without it). Returns its key, its width and its height. The key comes from the pixels: the same pixels have the same key, and a frontend that has the picture is not sent it again. paw keeps the pictures used last, up to 256 MB; keep a picture again to use it after a long time.

  ```lua
  local f = assert(io.open("cover.png", "rb"))
  local key, w, h = paw.canvas.image(f:read("*a"))
  f:close()
  ```
- `paw.canvas.key(name, keys)`: Keys typed in the window of a view. They go to the key mappings with that view focused (or to an open prompt), as when typed in the terminal. In its window, a view can give a key its own meaning, as other programs do (`view.window_keys`, for example Ctrl-A to select all notes). The terminal keeps the one rule of all views.
- `paw.canvas.leave(name, pane)`: A view that will show in a separate window leaves the layout, so it does not show two times. Its windows in the tabs close and keep their place. Returns the window that had the keyboard, to give the keyboard back to it. A view that a frontend draws itself (the arrange view, the mixer and other views) also stays where it is. The separate window is a second view of it. A view with a state for each window leaves only the pane `pane` that it goes out of: its other windows stay.
- `paw.canvas.open(name, opts)`: Show a view that paints in a graphical frontend, and give it the keyboard. When the view has a place in the layout (`paw.ui.dock`, or a window that shows it), it is docked, as the terminal shows it. If not, or with `window = true`, it is in a separate window. A view that is already in a separate window stays there. `opts`: `title`, `width`, `height` (the start size of a window), `window`.
- `paw.canvas.open_view(name, opts)`: Show a view in a window of a graphical frontend (the focused view when `name` is nil), and give it the keyboard. A view that paints is painted (`M.open`). Other views are drawn as the terminal draws them, in cells of the monospace font of the window, at the size of the window. A line below the view shows prompts, messages and its keys. A view that floats over the views of the terminal moves into the window. `opts`: `title`, `width`, `height` (in pixels).

  ```lua
  paw.canvas.open_view("undotree")
  ```
- `paw.canvas.openable()`: The views a frontend can offer to open in a window: those that take the keyboard, `{ name, title }` each, by title. A view keeps itself off the list with `window = false`. A view with a painted twin (`painted = "name"` of a view that has `paint`) is offered as that one.
- `paw.canvas.paint(name, width, height, opts)`: Paint a view at a size. Returns the drawing as a list of operations:

  ```lua
  { "r", x, y, w, h, fill, stroke, stroke width, radius }
  { "t", x, y, text, colour, size, bold (0 or 1), align, width }
  { "p", path commands, stroke, stroke width, fill }
  { "m", x, y, w, h, text, colour, background, attributes }
  { "g", x, y, size, codepoint, colour, font }   a music font's glyph
  { "cut", x, y0, y1 }                           where a slice may end
  { "layer", name }                              what follows is that layer
  ```

  The attributes are a sum of 1 bold, 4 italic, 8 underline and 32 strike. It also returns the title of the window, which a view can change.

  The options are these. `cell` is the size `{ w, h }` of a cell of the monospace font of the window (or of the terminal, for a surface). `fresh` is true when the window has nothing yet. `glyphs` is true when the frontend draws glyph operations itself. If not, they come as paths, without the markers.

  `surface` is true when the drawing goes into the cells of a terminal. Then the view does not draw its background and the data that the bars of the terminal show. `colors` is `{ fg, bg }`, the colors of the terminal.

  `bars` comes from a frontend that shows a view in a separate window, away from the bottom of its main window. The view then draws the status line and the command line below it. The `paint` function of the view gets these in its context, as `cell`, `surface`, `fg` and `bg`. A view that draws cells gives `{ same = true }` when nothing changes.
- `paw.canvas.paint_cells(name, window, width, height, opts)`: A view that draws cells, at a size in pixels: its snapshot (`paw.api.ui_view_snapshot`) as runs of text, one style for each run. paw draws it again only after a request for a redraw. It also draws it one time each second for the parts that change by themselves (times), and on each call while the song plays. The result is `{ same = true }` when the drawing is the same as the last drawing. `window` keeps the last drawing. The view in a separate window has a line below it for prompts, messages and the keys of the view. This is not so when the frontend draws a status line there itself (`opts.status`). paw sends the windows of a graphical frontend as scenes (`paw.ui.render_scene`).
- `paw.canvas.place(buf, x, y, w, h, key)`: Show the picture `key` over the cells `x, y, w, h` of `buf`: see `buf:image`. In a terminal that shows images and in a window, it is a strip (`buf:strip`) under the cells, and the result is true; elsewhere half blocks, two pixels a cell.
- `paw.canvas.pointer(name, event)`: Pass a pointer event from a frontend to a view, which then has the keyboard. It goes to its `pointer` function in pixels. For a view in cells, it goes to its `on_mouse` function, as from the terminal.
- `paw.canvas.shown(name)`: True if a graphical frontend shows a view. The view is in a separate window, or docked where the screen of the seat is the main area of a frontend. That is a frontend that told its size to `paw.panes`, or the frontend of the instance when there is no terminal.
- `paw.canvas.text_width(text, size)`: The width of a line of text in pixels, near enough, at `size` (12).
- `paw.canvas.view_pointer(view, e)`: Give a pointer event in pixels to a painted view: to its hit list (`view.hits`) first, then to its `pointer` function.
- `paw.canvas.windows()`: The windows that are open, for a frontend: `{ name, title, width, height, cells }` each, `cells` for a view drawn as the terminal draws it.

## Module paw.chords

- `paw.chords.offer(key, near)`: The chords to offer at the pencil, in this order: the diatonic triads and sevenths of `key`, then the common qualities on the pitch `near`. Each with its symbol, name, numeral and pitches.
- `paw.chords.parse(text, key, near)`: Read a chord symbol in `key` (paw.harmony's key, C major when nil) with its root nearest the pitch `near` (60 when nil). Returns the chord, or nil and why not.
- `paw.chords.quality(suffix, steps, name)`: Add a chord name: its suffix after the root (`"7#9"`) and its tones in semitones above the root. A name the reading does not know is written but not read.
- `paw.chords.stack(root, n, key)`: The chord of `n` notes (3 a triad, 4 a seventh) on `root`, a pitch, stacked in thirds from the scale of `key`: the diatonic chord.

## Module paw.clip_kinds

- `paw.clip_kinds.add(track, name, args, data)`: A new clip of the kind `name` on `track`: `data`, or what the kind's `create` makes of `args` (the words, and `name`, `start` and `length` of the clip). Its length is `args.length`, or the length the kind compiled, or a bar of 4 beats. One undo step.
- `paw.clip_kinds.compile(clip)`: Compile a clip of a kind again from its data (after something that it links to changed). One undo step.
- `paw.clip_kinds.data(clip)`: The data of a clip of a kind, by its kind's `deserialize`: nil for a MIDI or audio clip, and nil and why when the kind cannot read it. Without its kind, the plain data as it is stored.
- `paw.clip_kinds.define(name, spec)`: Define a kind of clip (see above). `name` is a lowercase word that is not a built-in kind (`midi`, `audio`): what a clip of the kind keeps. Defining a kind again replaces it. Clips of an older version of its data are migrated.
- `paw.clip_kinds.describe(clip)`: A few words on a clip of a kind, for `K`: `Film clip · intro.mp4`, or "film (no extension here defines it)". Nil for a MIDI or audio clip.
- `paw.clip_kinds.list()`: The names of the defined kinds, in the order they were defined.
- `paw.clip_kinds.look(clip, ctx)`: How a clip of a kind looks in the arrange view, by its kind's `look`: nil without the kind, or when `look` fails (said once per kind).
- `paw.clip_kinds.migrate(name)`: Move the clips of the kind `name` (of each kind when nil) whose data is of an older version to their kind's version, by its `deserialize`, and compile them again. Says how many moved; a clip whose migration fails stays as it was, with a message. Gives how many moved.
- `paw.clip_kinds.remove(name)`: Forget a kind: no new clips of it. The clips of it that the project has stay as they are, data and all, until something defines it again.
- `paw.clip_kinds.set(clip, data)`: Give a clip of a kind new data: the kind checks it and compiles it again, and the data, sound, signals and files change together, as one undo step. Refused without the kind, and for a clip that a newer version of the kind made.
- `paw.clip_kinds.slip(clip, by)`: What a clip of a kind holds when what it plays moves `by` beats later under it: by the kind's `slip` (given the new offset), or the same data with its offset moved.
- `paw.clip_kinds.spec(name)`: The kind `name` as defined, or nil. `D` is the record of its data.
- `paw.clip_kinds.split(clip, at)`: What the two halves of a clip of a kind hold when it is split `at` beats after its start, as `paw.api.clip_set_custom` takes it: by the kind's `split`, or (without it, or without the kind) the same data, with the right half starting where the cut is in it. The caller makes the halves.
- `paw.clip_kinds.trim(clip, from, to)`: What a clip of a kind holds when it is cut to the beats `from` to `to` after its start: by the kind's `trim`, or the same data with its offset moved to `from`. The caller moves the clip's start and length.

## Module paw.commands

- `paw.commands.about(text)`: A command that can be adjusted says the range it changed, as the panel of `<leader>.` shows it (`Quantize · 48 notes`). Call it from the handler.

  ```lua
  paw.commands.about("48 notes")
  ```
- `paw.commands.adjust(given)`: Run the last command that has `adjust` again with other parameters, in place of its undo step: `paw.commands.adjust({ grid = "1/8" })`, or positional ones, by the order of its `adjust`. The project goes back to before the command, the command runs again with its first parameters and these laid over them, and the undo step is the new result. It works only on the last change: after `undo`, or another change, it says so.
- `paw.commands.adjusting()`: The line `adjust a=1 b=2` that holds the parameters of the last command that can be adjusted, as they are now; nil when no command ran that can be adjusted. `<leader>.` puts it on the command line.
- `paw.commands.alias(alias, target)`: Make `alias` another name for `target`.
- `paw.commands.complete(line)`: What could finish a command line: a list of `{ text, label, desc }` with `text` the whole line it would become and `label` the part shown.

  ```lua
  paw.commands.complete("track.co")   --> { { text = "track.color", label = "track.color", desc = ... } }
  ```
- `paw.commands.define(name, run, opts)`: Define or replace a command.

  ```lua
  paw.command("track.mute", function(ctx) ... end, { desc = "Mute the track" })
  ```

  The handler gets `ctx` with `ctx.args` (positional and named arguments) and `ctx.count` (the number typed before a key mapping, or nil). With `opts.raw`, the command line gives its text as one string in `ctx.args[1]`. With `opts.range`, it accepts a range of bars before it (`:5,8name`) as `ctx.range`. See Ranges below.
- `paw.commands.exec(line, ctx)`: Run a command line, as typed after `:`, with a range in front if it has one.
- `paw.commands.get(name)`: The command of a name: `{ name, run, desc, ... }` as `paw.command` made it, or nil.
- `paw.commands.label(spec)`: What an undo step made by a command is called: its `label`, or the start of its description, before any example or alternative.
- `paw.commands.list()`: Every command, sorted by name.
- `paw.commands.main(name)`: What a bare extension name (`:notation`) stands for: its `.open` or `.show` command, where it has one.
- `paw.commands.owner()`: The extension that paw loads now, or whose code registers these commands and keys later. `:help` goes to its page for them, and an unload removes them.
- `paw.commands.panel()`: What the panel of `<leader>.` shows: the title, the parameters of the last command that can be adjusted, and their values now. Nil when there is no such command.
- `paw.commands.params(ctx)`: The parameters of the command that runs: what the user gave, by the names that its `adjust` lists. A parameter not given is not in the table.

  ```lua
  local p = paw.commands.params(ctx)  -- `:quantize 1/16 strength=50`: { grid = "1/16", strength = 50 }
  ```
- `paw.commands.parse(line)`: Split a command line into a name and arguments:

  ```lua
  `track.add Bass volume=-6` -> "track.add", { "Bass", volume = -6 }
  ```

  Quotes keep spaces together: `track.add "Lead Guitar"`, `name="Lead Guitar"`.
- `paw.commands.put(name, spec)`: Put a command back as `spec` (a command that `get` or `list` gave), or remove it with nil. An extension that unloads does this with the commands that it made.
- `paw.commands.range(line)`: Split a range from the start of a command line. Returns the range and the rest. The range is nil when there is no range. When the range names nothing, an error message replaces the rest.
- `paw.commands.run`: the same as `paw.cmd`.
- `paw.commands.unknown(name)`: What to say about a name that is no command: the commands that start with it, if there are any.
- `paw.commands.used(name)`: Count a use of a command selected by name (typed, or selected in a picker). Pickers then show the commands used most first. paw keeps the count in `paw.state`.
- `paw.commands.uses(name)`: The number of times that `used` counted a command.

## Module paw.complete

- `paw.complete.accept(next_only)`: Write the alternative that shows into the clip, as one edit. Write all of it, or with `next_only` only the notes of its first onset (a note, or the notes of a chord that start together). The rest continues to show. The cursor goes to the end of the accepted part. Returns true if it wrote notes.
- `paw.complete.audition()`: Play the alternative that shows through the track of the clip. It starts one bar before it, with the notes that are there, and the project does not change. Not while the transport runs.
- `paw.complete.cancel()`: Cancel the current request, and tell this to the sources that did not answer yet.
- `paw.complete.context(trigger)`: What a request is about: the clip open in the piano roll, where the suggestion starts and what is chosen there. Nil without an open clip.

  ```lua
  clip, track      ids
  start, length    where the clip is in the project, in beats
  at, pitch        where the suggestion starts (clip beats) and the cursor's pitch
  notes            the clip's notes, as `clip:notes()` gives them
  selection        the chosen notes, or nil
  grid, view, trigger ("manual" or "auto"), id
  key              `paw.harmony.key(at)` when there is such a module
  ```
- `paw.complete.current()`: What shows: `{ items, index, item, clip }`, or nil. A suggestion asked for by itself does not show while the transport plays or records.
- `paw.complete.dismiss()`: Hide what shows, and drop the request being answered.
- `paw.complete.list()`: The sources, highest priority first.
- `paw.complete.pending()`: True if a request waits for answers.
- `paw.complete.poke()`: Start the idle pause again: after an edit.
- `paw.complete.register(spec)`: Add a source, or replace the one of the same name.
- `paw.complete.request(trigger)`: Ask every source for this view at once. `trigger` is "manual" (a key, the default) or "auto". Returns the request's id, or nil when there is nothing to ask about or nobody to ask.
- `paw.complete.select(n, absolute)`: Show the next alternative (`n` 1), the previous (-1), or with `absolute` the alternative number `n`.
- `paw.complete.show(items, opts)`: Show items as ghost notes in the piano roll without being a source: a snippet's preview, what a fix would do. `opts.clip` is the clip they are for (the one open), `opts.keys = false` shows them only, without the keys that accept or step through them. Nothing, or an empty list, hides them.
- `paw.complete.tool()`: What the window's piano roll toolbar shows of completion: nil without sources.
- `paw.complete.unregister(name)`: Remove the source of a name.

## Module paw.controls

- `paw.controls.add(clip, start, kind, number)`: Add a move at `start` beats into the clip: of `kind` ("cc" with `number`, "bend", "pressure", "program"), at rest or 0. Returns it.
- `paw.controls.cells(clip, row)`: The text of each column of a row, by the names in `M.columns`.
- `paw.controls.chosen(clip)`: The places of the chosen moves of `clip`, in order.
- `paw.controls.clear(clip)`: Choose none of the clip's controller moves.
- `paw.controls.edit(clip, row, column, text)`: Change one cell of a row from text written as the list shows it. Errors say what is wrong.
- `paw.controls.fraction(kind, value)`: A move's value as a height in the strip, and a height as a value.
- `paw.controls.is(control, kind, number)`: True if a move is of the kind of the strip.
- `paw.controls.line(clip, kind, number, beat0, f0, beat1, f1, free)`: Draw a straight line of moves of the kind of the strip, from `beat0` at height `f0` to `beat1` at `f1`. It replaces the moves of that kind between them, with one move on each step of the grid (each 32nd of a beat when `free`), with the two ends. The new moves are then selected.
- `paw.controls.move(clip, dbeat, dfraction, free)`: Move the selected moves `dbeat` later and `dfraction` of the height of the strip up. The first move goes onto the grid unless `free`. The other moves keep their distance from it. No move leaves the clip or the strip.
- `paw.controls.remove(clip)`: Take the chosen moves away. Returns how many went.
- `paw.controls.remove_row(clip, row)`: Take a row away.
- `paw.controls.rows(clip)`: Every note and move of a clip, in time order, as rows of the list: a note `{ kind = "note", place, start, note }`, a move `{ kind = "control", place, start, control }`. Notes come before moves at the same time. Notes and moves hidden by a trim of the clip's edges are left out.
- `paw.controls.select(clip, place, mode)`: Choose one move by its place: `mode` "only", "add" or "toggle".
- `paw.controls.select_box(clip, kind, number, beat0, low, beat1, high, mode)`: Choose the moves of the strip's kind that a box touches: from `beat0` to `beat1` and from height `low` to `high`, in any order. `mode` as for `select`. Returns how many are chosen.
- `paw.controls.value(kind, fraction)`: A height in the strip, from 0 to 1, as a move's value.

## Module paw.cursor

- `paw.cursor.bounds()`: The time the cursor stays in: the current scope's.
- `paw.cursor.clip()`: The clip under the cursor, if any.
- `paw.cursor.index()`: 1-based position of the cursor track among the tracks of its place: the song's, or its subproject's (as `paw.api.track_move` counts).
- `paw.cursor.lane_id()`: The automation lane row of the cursor: a lane of the cursor track that shows as a row (see `paw.lanes`). Nil when the cursor is on the track.
- `paw.cursor.lens()`: Keys and commands typed in a pinned window act on its track: the track of "the cursor" is the window's while that window has the keyboard, or while paw draws it.
- `paw.cursor.line()`: 1-based row of the cursor among every row drawn, lanes included.
- `paw.cursor.master_reachable()`: True if a move of the cursor can go on from the last track to the master: a move of its own in normal mode, in the views that draw the master after the tracks. After an operator or in a selection, only tracks count.
- `paw.cursor.move_track(delta)`: Move by rows. In normal mode, the rows of open automation lanes count. After an operator or in a selection, only tracks count, as for `dj`. From the last track, a move down goes on to the master, and from the master a move up returns to the tracks.
- `paw.cursor.on_master()`: True if the cursor is on the master track: the row after the last track in the arrange view, the strip after the last in the mixer.
- `paw.cursor.over(old, new)`: Where the cursor goes when it moves from beat `old` to `new`: a beat inside a closed time fold is its start, or its end when the cursor moves on from its start, so that a motion takes a fold as one step.
- `paw.cursor.row()`: 1-based row of the cursor track among the tracks that are drawn: the same as `index` until a group is folded. On the master, the row after the last track.
- `paw.cursor.set_beat(beat)`: Put the cursor at a beat (not before 0, and in the scope's time).
- `paw.cursor.set_track(track, lane)`: Put the cursor on a track, or with `lane` on one of its lane rows.
- `paw.cursor.shift(track)`: For a track of a subproject shown in place under its return row: the beat of the window where the subproject's beat 0 is. Nil for any other track. The arrange view draws its clips that much later, and the cursor finds them there.
- `paw.cursor.snap(beat)`: Round a position to the arrange grid.
- `paw.cursor.track()`: The track the cursor is on, as a `paw.Track`, or nil.
- `paw.cursor.track_id()`: The id of the track of the cursor, or of the first track when that track does not exist now. Nil when the project has no tracks. 0 when the cursor is on the master track (`on_master`).

## Module paw.curves

- `paw.curves.copy(q)`: A copy of a point.
- `paw.curves.ease(shape, t, tension)`: Where a stretch is `t` of the way from one point to the next, 0 to 1, as the model plays it (crates/paw-core/src/model.rs, `smooth`).
- `paw.curves.fit(t, points)`: Points made ready for a curve: sorted. Each range with a shape that the curve does not have becomes short pieces of a shape that it has.
- `paw.curves.generate(wave, from, to, opts)`: A wave from beat `from` to beat `to`: `opts.rate` beats a cycle, `opts.depth` of the height, about `opts.centre` (a fraction, 0.5 when left out), turned into values with `opts.unfrac`. `opts.seed` makes a random one the same each time. Smooth shapes where `opts.smooth` (the curve has them), else many points.
- `paw.curves.is_curve(uri)`: True if a text names a curve: an address that `target` can read.
- `paw.curves.provide(name, fn)`: Make curves of your own addresses. `fn(uri, parts)` returns a target with `points`, `write`, `name`, `format`, `lo`, `hi` and the other fields, or nil to let other providers have the address (`docs/reference/lua-views.md`, Curves).
- `paw.curves.quantize(points, grid)`: Points moved onto the grid. When two points go to one step, the later point stays.
- `paw.curves.smooth(points, times)`: Softer moves: each value becomes the mean of its value and the values next to it, `times` times. The first and the last value do not change.
- `paw.curves.sorted(points)`: Points sorted by beat, those at the same beat kept in the order given.
- `paw.curves.splice(points, from, to, new)`: Replace the points from beat `from` to beat `to` (both included) with `new`, and keep the other points. paw does this when you draw over a range.
- `paw.curves.target(uri)`: The curve at an address, or nil and why not.
- `paw.curves.thin(points, tolerance, frac)`: Fewer points for the same curve: a point goes when the curve without it strays from it by less than `tolerance` (a fraction of the drawing's height, through `frac`). Points that hold or ease stay.
- `paw.curves.value_at(points, beat)`: The value of a point list at a beat: the nearest point's before the first and after the last, nil with no points.

## Module paw.curves.editor

- `paw.curves.editor.add(on_curve)`: Add a point at the cursor: at the cursor's value, or with `on_curve` at the curve's value there.
- `paw.curves.editor.automate(device_id, key)`: Automate a parameter of a device. paw makes its lane, with a first point at its current value at the beat of the arrange cursor. paw shows the lanes of the track as rows, with the cursor on the new lane, and tells you.
- `paw.curves.editor.climb(n)`: Move the cursor's value `n` steps up.
- `paw.curves.editor.current()`: The curve window the keyboard is in: the current window, or the one a graphical frontend shows.
- `paw.curves.editor.cycle_shape()`: The next shape for the stretch from the point under the cursor.
- `paw.curves.editor.gen_finish()`: Keep the wave as it is.
- `paw.curves.editor.gen_next(by)`: Select the next shape (`by` 1) or the previous shape (-1) while you generate a wave.
- `paw.curves.editor.gen_step(by)`: Step the current choice of the wave under way, or go to the next choice.
- `paw.curves.editor.gen_text()`: What the wave under way reads as on the bottom line.
- `paw.curves.editor.generate(wave, from, to, opts)`: Make a wave over a range of the curve, from beat `from` to `to`. `wave` is a name or a number in `paw.curves.waves`. `opts.rate` and `opts.depth` are numbers or places in their lists. You can then step through the choices until `<C-y>` or `<Esc>` keeps them.
- `paw.curves.editor.grid(factor)`: Make the editor's grid `factor` times as fine or as coarse.
- `paw.curves.editor.insert_finish()`: Write what was drawn, as one undo step.
- `paw.curves.editor.insert_mark()`: Put the cursor's beat and value among the points drawn.
- `paw.curves.editor.insert_start(on_curve)`: Start drawing at the cursor: from here, each move of the cursor puts a point where it lands, at its value. Nothing is written until insert mode is left.
- `paw.curves.editor.move(n)`: Move the cursor along the grid, `n` steps.
- `paw.curves.editor.nudge_point(n)`: Raise or lower the point under the cursor `n` steps.
- `paw.curves.editor.open(uri, opts)`: Show a curve. It shows in the window that shows it already. If not, it shows in a new window split below the current window (to the side with `opts.vertical`), or in this window with `opts.here`. With `opts.window`, it shows in a separate window of a graphical frontend. `opts.beat` puts the cursor there.
- `paw.curves.editor.paste(register, count)`: Put the points of a register at the cursor, over what is there.
- `paw.curves.editor.picture(g, px, t, points, s)`: The plot in pixels (a strip below the cells, `buf:strip`): the grid, the curve and the area below it, through `paw.plot`. A value is as high as the middle of the dot where the cells would put it (`s.sub` dots for each cell, as `paw.opt.curve_glyphs` sets them). So the points and the cursor, which paw draws in cells over it, are on the line.
- `paw.curves.editor.remove(n)`: Remove `n` points from the one under the cursor on.
- `paw.curves.editor.target(win)`: The curve a window shows, or nil and why not.
- `paw.curves.editor.tension(by)`: Bend the smooth stretch from the point under the cursor.
- `paw.curves.editor.to_end(dir)`: To the first (`dir` -1) or last point.
- `paw.curves.editor.to_point(dir, n)`: Go to the next point (`dir` 1) or the previous point, `n` times. The cursor takes its value.
- `paw.curves.editor.type_value()`: Type the value of the point under the cursor, or of a new one there.
- `paw.curves.editor.under_cursor(note)`: The curve of the item under the cursor in the focused view. In the arrange view, it is a lane row or the tempo lane. In the device panel, it is a parameter. In the piano roll, it is the controller of the strip (with `note`, only that of the note under the cursor). Nil and the reason when there is none.
- `paw.curves.editor.wave_menu(from, to, where)`: The wave menu, then the wave over a region.
- `paw.curves.editor.zoom(factor)`: Zoom the editor's window in or out by `factor`.

## Module paw.diagnostic

- `paw.diagnostic.about(d, uri)`: True if a diagnostic is about an address or an item in it. A note counts when a diagnostic of its clip names the note in its notes.
- `paw.diagnostic.actions(target, place)`: The fixes of the diagnostics about a place (as `get` takes its target and filter), as `{ title, diagnostic, fix, run }`, the most severe first. `actions(clip, place)` asks about one note of a clip.
- `paw.diagnostic.apply(d, fix)`: Do a fix of a diagnostic as one undo step. Returns true if it did the fix.
- `paw.diagnostic.config(opts)`: Change how paw shows diagnostics. Returns the options in use.

  ```lua
  paw.diagnostic.config({ virtual_text = false })
  ```
- `paw.diagnostic.count(target, filter)`: How many diagnostics of each severity (as `get` takes its target): `{ error = 1, warning = 2, info = 0, hint = 0, total = 3 }`.
- `paw.diagnostic.format(d)`: A diagnostic in one line: `warning parallel-perfect: Parallel fifths … [midi-lsp]`.
- `paw.diagnostic.get(target, filter)`: Diagnostics, sorted by kind and then by where they are. `target`: a clip id (those about it and its notes), an address (those about it or what it holds), or nil for all. `filter`: `namespace`, `severity` (a severity or `{ min, max }`, min the least severe), `note` (a place in the clip), `kind` (as `paw.diagnostic.kind`), `document`.
- `paw.diagnostic.goto_next(opts)`: Go to the next diagnostic, or `opts.count` on (`]d`).
- `paw.diagnostic.goto_prev(opts)`: Go to the diagnostic before, or `opts.count` back (`[d`).
- `paw.diagnostic.group(prefix, severity)`: The highlight group for a severity with a prefix: `Diagnostic` gives `DiagnosticWarn`.
- `paw.diagnostic.jump(dir, count)`: The next (`dir` 1) or previous (-1) diagnostic that the focused view can show, from its cursor, `count` times, round the ends. The cursor goes there. Returns the diagnostic, or nil when the view has none.
- `paw.diagnostic.kind(d)`: The kind of item that a diagnostic is about, to make groups: clip, track, device, time, project, render, or the kind of an extension.
- `paw.diagnostic.list(target)`: Every diagnostic (of `target`, as `get` takes it) in a picker, as the quickfix list, grouped by what they are about: Enter goes to one.
- `paw.diagnostic.marks()`: The marks of the window in other views. Each track (by id) has the worst severity about it, its devices or its sends, and the first message. The ranges of time are also marks.
- `paw.diagnostic.namespaces()`: The namespaces that published diagnostics.
- `paw.diagnostic.notes_of(d)`: The notes of a diagnostic as they are now.
- `paw.diagnostic.paint_part(p, id, offset)`: One clip's, `offset` beats from the roll's own.
- `paw.diagnostic.paint_roll(p)`: Mark the diagnostics of each clip that the piano roll edits, as one of its layers. Each note has a line below it in the color of its severity. The message comes after the last note while there is space, and a mark on the ruler shows where it starts.
- `paw.diagnostic.places(d)`: The current places of the notes of a diagnostic (from 1). The list does not contain a note that does not exist now.
- `paw.diagnostic.reset(namespace, doc)`: Forget the diagnostics of `namespace` about one document, or all of them. With a clip id, forget all its diagnostics about that clip. With no namespace, forget the diagnostics of all namespaces about that document, or all diagnostics.
- `paw.diagnostic.roll_marks(id)`: The marks of the window in its piano roll for a clip. These are the notes that diagnostics are about, by place from 0. Each has its worst severity, the messages about it and the titles of its fixes.
- `paw.diagnostic.set(namespace, doc, list)`: Publish the diagnostics of `namespace` about a document (a clip, or a string: the document URI of a server). They replace its old diagnostics of that document. An empty list clears them.
- `paw.diagnostic.setloclist(opts)`: The diagnostics in the current window's location list.
- `paw.diagnostic.setqflist(opts)`: Put the diagnostics in the quickfix list, as `vim.diagnostic.setqflist`: `opts` has `target`, `severity` (the least severe), `title`, `open`. `setloclist` puts them in the current window's location list.
- `paw.diagnostic.severity_of(value)`: A severity from 1 (error) to 4 (hint), from a number or a word.
- `paw.diagnostic.show(d)`: Put the cursor of the view that shows it best on a diagnostic, and say it.
- `paw.diagnostic.status()`: The status line's piece: `E1 W2` for the clip in the piano roll, or the whole project when none is open. Nil when there is nothing to say.
- `paw.diagnostic.where(d)`: Where a diagnostic is about, in a few words: `Lead › Synth · cutoff`, `chords 2.1.00`, `5.1.00–9.1.00`, `mix.wav`.
- `paw.diagnostic.worst(uri, filter)`: The worst severity said about an address or what it holds, or nil.

## Module paw.draw

- `paw.draw.bar_lines(from, span)`: The bars and beats from `from` for `span` beats, as the project counts them. `{ beat = b, bar = n }` is a bar line (n from 1), and `{ beat = b }` is a beat inside a bar. Bar lines come from `paw.time.bar_start`, so a change of time signature moves them.
- `paw.draw.beats(ruler, scroll, span, zoom, origin)`: Write the numbers of a ruler above a roll that shows `span` beats from `scroll`, at `zoom` columns for each beat. Bars have the numbers of the project (`origin` is the project beat of the beat 0 of the roll). Beats between them are ticks. Returns the positions of the lines, as `{ x, bar }`, for the rows below.
- `paw.draw.braille(bits)`: A braille character from its eight dots: bit k is dot k + 1.
- `paw.draw.chips(buf, x, y, list, gap)`: Small on/off marks side by side, each a letter on a cell of its own: `chips(buf, x, y, { { "M", on, "Mute" }, ... }, gap)`. Returns the columns used.
- `paw.draw.clear_peak(id)`: Put out a track's clip light and let its loudest of late fall.
- `paw.draw.curve(buf, y, rows, value, style)`: Draw a curve as a thin line over `rows` rows of a buffer, from row `y` down. `value(i)` gives the height, from 0 at the bottom to 1 at the top, at point `i`, with two points for each column. The function changes only the cells on the line. It uses sextants (a connected line), braille dots or lines at three heights a row, as `M.curve_glyphs()` tells.
- `paw.draw.curve_glyphs()`: How paw draws curves in cells: "sextant", "braille" or "line", from `paw.opt.curve_glyphs`. `paw.opt.braille = false` and `paw.opt.ascii` both mean "line". `paw.opt.ascii` wins over all, and uses ASCII characters.
- `paw.draw.db_cell(db, width)`: Where on a meter `width` cells long a level in dB falls, from 0.
- `paw.draw.db_text(db)`: A volume in dB as few cells as it can: `-4.0`, `-inf`, `+2.5`.
- `paw.draw.hold(key, peak)`: Peaks held for some time, by key. `hold(key, peak)` gives the loudest peak of the last two seconds, which falls after that time.
- `paw.draw.hue(colour)`: Highlight groups in the shades of one color (`#rrggbb`), made the first time that a caller asks for the color:

  ```lua
  fg                  the colour itself, on whatever is behind it
  title, body         a clip's name row and the rows under it
  title_cur, body_cur the same for the clip under the cursor (or chosen)
  title_off, body_off the same for a muted clip
  lane_sel            the background of the selected track's lane
  note, note_soft, note_faint   notes, loud to quiet
  pill                dark text on the colour
  plate               a name plate: light text on a deep shade
  ```
- `paw.draw.jump_scroll(target, scroll, span, zoom, jumped)`: Where a view scrolls to for a move of its cursor to `target`, a beat, or nil when the move leaves the scroll to the caller. A step (`jumped` is false) is left to the caller, which scrolls just enough. A jump (it went into the jump list) to a target that is off screen, or in the last quarter of the view, puts the target at the left margin (`paw.opt.jumpview` "left", `paw.opt.jumpmargin` columns) or in the middle ("center"). `span` is the beats shown, `zoom` the columns a beat.
- `paw.draw.keys(buf, x, y, entries, width, groups)`: A row of keys and their actions, for a line of hints: `{ { "o", "new track" }, ... }`, with a faint dot between them. `? keys` is always the last when it is in the list. Returns the columns used. The entries that do not fit are not shown.
- `paw.draw.level(peak)`: How far up a meter a linear peak reaches, from 0 to 1 over 60 dB.
- `paw.draw.meter(buf, x, y, width, peak, hold)`: A level meter `width` cells wide for a linear peak: a thin rail, lit from the left, green then yellow then red. With `hold` (a linear peak), the loudest of late is marked.
- `paw.draw.miniroll(notes, width, rows, zoom, from)`: Notes as a small piano roll of `rows` text rows, each `width` columns. A row holds two pitches, drawn with half blocks. `notes` have `start`, `length` and `pitch`. A column covers `1 / zoom` beats from `from`.
- `paw.draw.mix(a, b, t)`: A color between two colors: `t` 0 gives `a`, 1 gives `b`.
- `paw.draw.nearest256(hex)`: The nearest of the 256 colors to `#rrggbb`, from the 6x6x6 cube (16 to 231) or the grays (232 to 255). A color with little hue gets a gray. Returns its index and the color that the index shows.
- `paw.draw.note_style(hue, velocity)`: The shade of a note by how hard it is played.
- `paw.draw.pan(buf, x, y, width, pan, style)`: A pan from -1 to 1 as a bar that is `width` cells wide (an odd number is best). It is a rail with a mark at the position of the sound, `───┃───` in the middle.
- `paw.draw.pan_text(pan)`: Where a pan from -1 to 1 points, in a few cells: `L30`, `C`, `R100`.
- `paw.draw.piano_key(buf, row, pitch, cursor, width, name)`: One row of a keyboard on its side, `width` cells wide, for the left edge of a piano roll. Black keys are short. The Cs have their names, and the pitch of the cursor has its name too.
- `paw.draw.reset()`: Forget the shades made until now. Call it after the palette changes.
- `paw.draw.sextant(bits)`: The character for a set of sextants (U+1FB00 to U+1FB3B, two columns by three rows): bits 1 to 32 are top left, top right, middle left, middle right, bottom left, bottom right. The patterns that are not in that block are a space, the left half, the right half and the full block.
- `paw.draw.slider(buf, x, y, width, fraction, on, off)`: A slider `width` cells wide with its knob `fraction` of the way along.
- `paw.draw.stereo_meter(buf, x, y, width, left, right)`: The two sides of a stereo level in one row that is `width` cells wide. The left side is in the upper half of each cell, the right in the lower.
- `paw.draw.term_def(def, truecolor)`: A highlight definition as this terminal can show it. On a terminal without 24-bit color, each `#rrggbb` becomes the nearest of the 256.
- `paw.draw.trace(width, samples, y, sub, kind)`: A connected line over a grid of cells, for a curve. `y(sx)` gives the row of the line from the top, in `sub` rows for each cell (3 for sextants, 4 for braille). `sx` counts from 0, with two samples for each cell. `y(sx)` gives nil for no line, and there are `samples` of them. The function fills a jump from the last row to this row, to keep the line connected. Returns `{ [row * width + col] = bits }`, the bits as `M.sextant` or `M.braille` take them.
- `paw.draw.track_colour(track, index)`: The color of a track: its own color if it has one. If not, a color of the theme, by the place of the track in the track list.
- `paw.draw.track_hue(track, index)`: The hue of the color of a track, from 0 to 360.
- `paw.draw.track_peak(id)`: The meter of a track as the mixer shows it, in a terminal and in a window (`scene.live`). It gives the two sides and the loudest recent peak. It also tells if the track reached full scale after the last `clear_peak` for it.
- `paw.draw.truecolor()`: True if the terminal shows 24-bit color. `paw.opt.termcolors` is "true" or "256". With "auto" (the default), the environment tells: COLORTERM of truecolor or 24bit, or a TERM that ends in -direct.
- `paw.draw.use_glyphs()`: Take the glyphs `paw.opt.ascii` asks for into `paw.draw.g`.
- `paw.draw.vmeter(buf, x, y, height, peak, hold)`: A level meter `height` cells tall, lit from the bottom, with the peak held (`hold`, linear) marked by a line over its cell.
- `paw.draw.wave_reach(a)`: How far a sample of size `a` (0 to 1) goes up a waveform, 0 to 1. With `paw.opt.wave_scale` "linear", the size does not change, and a kick shows over a hat. With `"db"`, the scale is in decibels from -48, and quiet sounds show.
- `paw.draw.waveform(peaks, rows)`: Peaks (`{ min, max }` pairs from -1 to 1, one for each column) as a waveform of `rows` text rows. Each column goes from its lowest to its highest sample around the middle of the rows, in eighths of a row. Returns the rows as text. It also returns, for each row, its runs `{ column, text, mark }` of cells with the same mark. The column counts from 0. The text of a run has the style of the mark, `nil` for none. "flip" is for cells whose upper part is the wave. Such a cell is an eighth block in reverse video, because blocks only grow from the bottom. "clip" is for a column that reaches full scale, and `clipflip` for both.

## Module paw.events

- `paw.events.emit`: the same as `paw.emit`.
- `paw.events.event(name)`: The descriptor of an event whose payload is a `P`: Teal checks the handlers that `paw.on` is given for it, and what `paw.emit` sends.

  ```lua
  local changed: paw.events.Event<OptionChanged> = paw.events.event("option.changed")
  ```
- `paw.events.handlers()`: Every handler, by its handle: `{ pattern, fn }`.
- `paw.events.listened(name)`: True if a handler listens for `name` by its name or its family (not `*`). Use it for events that are expensive to make.
- `paw.events.off`: the same as `paw.off`.
- `paw.events.on`: the same as `paw.on`.
- `paw.events.once`: the same as `paw.once`.
- `paw.events.pattern(pattern)`: The descriptor of a pattern of events (`track.*`, `*`): its handlers read nothing of the payload without a cast.

## Module paw.ex

- `paw.ex.address_of(item)`: The address of an item, for the quickfix list and for going to it.
- `paw.ex.apply(changes, remove)`: Make the changes `{ item, change }` and remove the items in `remove`, as one edit per clip.
- `paw.ex.change(item, sets, pattern)`: What a replacement makes of one item: the fields that change, as `paw.api` keeps them.
- `paw.ex.complete_pattern(line)`: Field names as they are typed in a pattern: `:%s/ve` offers `vel`.
- `paw.ex.complete_range(line)`: What could finish a range being typed: marks after `'`, tracks after `t/`. Nil when the line is not in the middle of one.
- `paw.ex.describe(r)`: What a range covers, in words: "bars 5 to 8 on 2 tracks".
- `paw.ex.exec(line, ctx)`: Run a command line, as typed after `:`, with a range in front if it has one. A line with a range, or an Ex command, is one undo step named after the line (a line typed after `:` always is).
- `paw.ex.field(name, spec)`: A field that `:s` and `:g` patterns can name (`lyric:la`): `level` (note, clip or track), `type`, `get(item)`, `set(item, value, change)`.
- `paw.ex.go(r)`: Move to where a range starts, as `:5` does in Vim.
- `paw.ex.item_of(uri)`: The item an address names, or nil.
- `paw.ex.items(r, kind)`: The notes, clips or tracks (`kind`) a range holds, in the order they come in the song.
- `paw.ex.label(item)`: An item in a few words: "C4 vel 100 at 5.1.00 in Verse".
- `paw.ex.mark(state, item, change)`: Remember an item for the views: lit, and with its change as a ghost.
- `paw.ex.pattern(text)`: Read a pattern: `{ text, level, test(item), names = { substrings of names it looks for } }`.
- `paw.ex.preview(text)`: Show what a line typed so far would do: called by the command line as it changes, and with nil when it closes. Returns a few words for the command line, and "error" when they say what is wrong.
- `paw.ex.range(line)`: Split a range from the start of a command line. Returns the range and the rest. The range is nil when there is no range. When the range names nothing, the third value is an error message, and there is no rest.
- `paw.ex.replacement(text, pattern)`: Read a replacement for what `pattern` matches: a list of changes, or an empty list, which removes what matched.
- `paw.ex.selection_range()`: The last selection of the focused view as a range of the song.
- `paw.ex.show(item)`: Put the cursor on an item, in the view that shows it.
- `paw.ex.shown()`: What the views show now, for frontends and tests: `{ from, to, tracks, matches, notes, clips, current }`, or nil.
- `paw.ex.split(rest)`: Split what follows a range into the command's name, the text after it, and how many times a `>` or `<` was typed.
- `paw.ex.substitution(r, pattern, replacement, flags)`: What a substitution would do: the matches, the ones it changes, and for each its change (false to remove it).
