- `paw.ex.view(name, spec)`: Tell how a view of your own maps its columns to the beats of the song, and which clips it edits, for ranges. See `docs/reference/lua-commands.md`.

## Module paw.ext

- `paw.ext.bundled()`: The names of the bundled extensions, loaded or not, sorted.
- `paw.ext.bundled_dir()`: The directory of the extensions that come with paw: `$PAW_HOME/extensions`, or `extensions` under the current directory in a source tree. Nil when there is no such directory.
- `paw.ext.caller()`: The loaded extension whose code called the function this is called from, or nil for the core's or the user's.
- `paw.ext.list()`: Loaded extensions, sorted by name.
- `paw.ext.load(path)`: Load one extension from a directory or a file (`.lua`, or `.tl` or the extension of another language of `paw.lang`). One the program was built with is not loaded again from elsewhere: the configuration that names the source tree's copy gets the packaged one.
- `paw.ext.load_bundled(name)`: Load a bundled extension by name. A name that is loaded does not change. Returns the entry, or nil and the problem.
- `paw.ext.load_dir(dir)`: Load everything in a directory of extensions.
- `paw.ext.load_packaged(dirs)`: Load the extensions the program was built with: `dirs` is a list of their directories separated by `:` (`$PAW_EXTENSIONS`, which the flake's `paw.withExtensions` sets).
- `paw.ext.manifest(path, name)`: An extension's manifest: `manifest.lua` in its directory. A one-file extension has none. Returns the table (with `name` filled in), or nil and what is wrong with it.
- `paw.ext.parse_version(text)`: The numbers of a version: "1.2.3" gives { 1, 2, 3 }. A part that is not there is 0. Nil for text that is not a version.
- `paw.ext.provides(name)`: What a loaded extension registered: a list of `{ kind, title, items }`, each item a short label, in the order of `paw.ext.registries`.
- `paw.ext.satisfies(version, want)`: True if `version` agrees with `want`. `want` is comparisons with spaces or commas between them. Each is `>=1.2`, `>1`, `<=2`, `<2.0`, `=1.2.3`, `^1.2` (the same first number, at least 1.2), `~1.2` (the same first two numbers) or a version alone, which means `^`. `*` or nothing is any version.
- `paw.ext.unload(name, opts)`: Unload an extension. paw removes all that it registered (while it loaded, and later from its handlers and timers). paw puts back what it replaced (a command or key of the core that it mapped again). Its options go with their values, and its timers stop. paw stops to offer the devices written in Lua and the plugin directories that it added. paw forgets its modules, so a new load runs them again.

  While a track contains one of its devices, paw does not unload it (as Neovim does not delete a buffer with changes). With `opts.force`, it unloads, and the devices stay and play until you remove them. paw cannot find them when you open the project again without the extension. Returns true (with `opts.force`, the devices that stay on tracks, in words), or nil and the reason.

## Module paw.external

- `paw.external.act()`: Act on the changes as the option says: called when paw gets the focus, or at the next key after them.
- `paw.external.asking()`: True if paw asks now what to do with the changes.
- `paw.external.keep()`: Keep paw's version of the project.
- `paw.external.reload()`: Read the changed files again, as one undo step.

## Module paw.files

- `paw.files.buffer_name(dir, tree)`: The name of the buffer that lists a folder, as a tree or not.
- `paw.files.cd(dir)`: Set the folder for relative names, as `:cd` does: `dir` is relative to the folder now; `-` is the folder before; nil is the home folder; false returns to the default (beside the project). Returns the folder, or nil and why not.
- `paw.files.cwd()`: The folder that `:cd` set, or nil when there is none.
- `paw.files.here()`: The folder that a relative name in a command goes to: the folder that `:cd` set; else the folder of the project's file; else the folder that paw started in.
- `paw.files.is_dir(path)`: True if a path is a folder.
- `paw.files.open(dir, opts)`: Show a folder: in this window (`opts.here`), or split beside (a tree by default). `opts.tree`, `opts.filter` ("unused") and `opts.hidden`.
- `paw.files.path(name)`: The full path of a name that the user typed: `~` is the home folder, and a relative name is in `paw.files.here()`.

  ```lua
  paw.files.path("mix.wav")  -- "/home/me/songs/mix.wav" in the folder of the project
  ```
- `paw.files.project_path(name)`: The full path of a project's name that the user typed, as `:w` takes it: as `path`, but a relative name goes beside a project folder, not into it.

  ```lua
  paw.files.project_path("take2")  -- "/home/me/songs/take2" beside songs/song
  ```
- `paw.files.sound_info(path, stat)`: What a sound file's header says: `{ rate, channels, seconds }`, or nil for a file that is not one that can be read.
- `paw.files.watch()`: Start to watch the cursor, when a files buffer exists.

## Module paw.folds

- `paw.folds.all(on, win)`: Close every fold of a window, every group too (`zM`), or open them all (`zR`).
- `paw.folds.at(id, win)`: The fold at a track (the cursor's by default), in a window: the largest closed one, which its row stands for, else the smallest. Nil when the track is in none.
- `paw.folds.clear(win)`: Delete every fold of a window, as `zE`. Returns how many there were.
- `paw.folds.close(id, win)`: Close the fold at the cursor, as `zc`; on a closed fold, the one around it. Returns it, or nil and the reason.
- `paw.folds.collapse(rows, win)`: The rows that a window draws, from the rows of its tracks without its folds of tracks: each closed fold of tracks keeps its first row, which stands for all of it.
- `paw.folds.count(f)`: How many tracks of a fold are there.
- `paw.folds.delete(id, win)`: Delete the fold at a track (the cursor's by default), as `zd`: the fold goes, its tracks stay, drawn as before. Returns it, or nil and the reason.
- `paw.folds.describe(f)`: What a fold holds, in words: `3 tracks`, `8 bars`.
- `paw.folds.group_closed(group, win)`: True if a group is folded into its row in a window (the one a view shows by default).
- `paw.folds.level(delta, win)`: Close one more level of regions in a window (`zm`, `delta` -1: the deepest open level first), or open one (`zr`, 1), as the `foldlevel` option of Vim. The regions that `za` or `zf` opened or closed follow the level again. Returns the level: how many levels stay open.
- `paw.folds.list(win)`: The folds of a window that a view shows (the one being drawn, else the current one). Empty when it has none.
- `paw.folds.make(spec, win)`: Make a fold of what a scope covers (`zf{motion}`), closed, in a window: a group folds into its row (`zfag`), tracks into one row named `Fold 1` (`Vjjzf`). Returns it, or nil and the reason.
- `paw.folds.name(f)`: The name a fold shows: its own, else its group's.
- `paw.folds.open(id, win)`: Open the fold at the cursor (the one its row stands for). Returns it, or nil and the reason.
- `paw.folds.over`: the same as `paw.cursor.over`.
- `paw.folds.reveal()`: The cursor does not stay on a track that is folded away: it goes to the row that stands for it.
- `paw.folds.row(id, win)`: The closed fold of tracks that the row of a track stands for in a window (the one a view shows by default), or nil: the track is the first row of that fold.
- `paw.folds.set_group(group, on, win)`: Fold a group into its row, or open it, in a window: `on` nil flips it.
- `paw.folds.time_at(beat, win)`: The closed time fold that a beat is on (`from` up to `to`), in a window.
- `paw.folds.time_map(zoom, win)`: The map from beats to the places of a view at `zoom` columns a beat, with the closed time folds of a window (the one a view shows by default). Each folded span takes the columns of its label and two more.
- `paw.folds.time_spans(win)`: The closed time folds of a window (the one a view shows by default), in order of time: the outermost of folds inside each other, and folds that overlap as one. A fold that holds all the time of the window's scope is open there.
- `paw.folds.toggle(id, win)`: Toggle the fold at a track (the cursor's by default), as `za`. Returns it, or nil and the reason.

## Module paw.formats

- `paw.formats.export(path, opts)`: Write the project with the format of a file. Says what it did.
- `paw.formats.extensions(side)`: The extensions of the files that a side takes, for lists and completion.
- `paw.formats.for_path(path, side)`: The format that takes `path` for `side` ("import" or "export"): one whose `detect` says yes, else one of the file's extension. Nil when none does.
- `paw.formats.get(name)`: The format of a name, or nil.
- `paw.formats.help_text()`: The page of `:help formats`, in Markdown: what each format reads and writes, and how to add one.
- `paw.formats.import(path, opts)`: Bring a file in with its format: `opts.merge` adds to the project, else it opens in place of the project. Says what it did; returns what the format returned, or nil when it could not.
- `paw.formats.list()`: The formats, by name: `{ name, desc, extensions, project, import, export }` each.
- `paw.formats.register(spec)`: Register a format of files (see the top of paw/formats.tl). A format of the same name is replaced. Returns the name.
- `paw.formats.split_args(line)`: The path at the start of a command line and the `key=value` words at its end: `song.rpp instrument=synth` is `"song.rpp", { instrument = "synth" }`.
- `paw.formats.unregister(name)`: Take a format away again.

## Module paw.freeze

- `paw.freeze.freeze(track, opts)`: Freeze a track or a group: render it, and play the file from now on. `opts.tail` is the seconds rendered after the song's end (2). One undo step. Returns the file.
- `paw.freeze.frozen(track)`: What a frozen track was frozen to, `{ file }`, or nil.
- `paw.freeze.holder(track)`: The frozen track a track sounds through, if any: the one whose file holds its sound.
- `paw.freeze.render_opts(track, opts)`: The render options of a freeze: the whole song from its start, the track alone before its fader, as 32-bit float. So the file plays what the track did.
- `paw.freeze.state(track)`: "frozen", "held" (its sound is in a frozen track it feeds), or nil.
- `paw.freeze.unfreeze(track)`: Play a frozen track's clips and devices again. The file stays where it is, as undo can bring the freeze back.

## Module paw.frontend

- `paw.frontend.band_state()`: The bands that have entries, as rows from 0 below the marker band: `{ rows, entries }`. Each entry has its `row`, its `band` and `index` (for `act.band`), `beat`, `length`, `name`, `color`, `active` and `hint`.
- `paw.frontend.choose_clips(set)`: Choose a set of clips (`{ [id] = true }`), as visual mode's selection: what `:select` does.
- `paw.frontend.choose_notes(clip, places)`: Choose notes of `clip` by their places (`{ [place] = true }`), as the pointer would: what `:select` does.
- `paw.frontend.chosen_clips()`: The ids of the chosen clips, in order.
- `paw.frontend.chosen_notes(clip)`: The places of the selected notes of `clip`, in order. None if the notes of the clip changed after the selection.
- `paw.frontend.chosen_refs()`: Every chosen note of the clips the roll edits, as `{ clip, place }`.
- `paw.frontend.chosen_text(clip)`: The chosen notes of `clip` (and of the clips edited with it) in words, for a toolbar: `3 notes · 5.1.00 – 5.3.00`, or "" with none chosen.
- `paw.frontend.closing()`: Tells if paw would lose data if it closes now: { modified, name, path }.
- `paw.frontend.completions(prompt)`: The candidates of a prompt, as the terminal shows them above the line. These are the candidates in view around the selected one, as `{ label, desc }`. `chosen` is the place of the selected candidate among them (0 for none).
- `paw.frontend.content_key(clip)`: What changes exactly when what a clip shows inside does: its notes and controller moves (fetch `M.preview` again then), or its waveform (fetch `M.peaks` again then). Nil for a MIDI clip with no notes yet.
- `paw.frontend.dialog_info()`: The data that the window needs to open the file dialog of the desktop. `native` tells if it must use that dialog (the option). When it is off, the dialogs are those of the kernel. `dir` is the folder to start in: `paw.files.here()`, as in the list picker. `name` is the file name of the project, for "Save as". `render` is the file endings that a render can write.
- `paw.frontend.engine_menu()`: The menu where the audio devices are chosen: `info` (lines to show), `output`, `input`, `block`, `rate` and `backend`, each a list of `{ label, checked }`. `act.choose_engine` takes one by heading and place.
- `paw.frontend.float(width, height)`: The float that is open (help, a list, a picker), drawn as text `width` columns wide: its title and its lines. Nil when there is none.
- `paw.frontend.format_value(param, value)`: A parameter's value as text in its unit (see `paw.params.format`).
- `paw.frontend.input_menu(track)`: The menu of the input of a track: the choices of `paw.audio.choices` under their headings, `audio`, `midi` and `channel`. It also gives the MIDI output of the track: `midi_out`, `midi_out_channel` and `midi_out_form`. Each is a list of `{ label, checked }`. `act.choose_input` takes one by heading and place.
- `paw.frontend.lane_name(lane)`: What a lane moves, in words: `Volume`, `Pan`, `Synth · cutoff`.
- `paw.frontend.lane_span(lane)`: The stretch of a lane's range that the drawing covers: a fader's travel for volume, the whole range for anything else.
- `paw.frontend.layout_get()`: How the window was left (its size, the zoom, the heights of rows and of the piano roll, if the mixer shows): a table, empty when nothing was kept. It belongs to the machine, so it is kept here, where a window attached to this kernel finds it too. (`M.layout_path` names another file, for tests.)
- `paw.frontend.layout_set(layout)`: Keep the window's layout (see `layout_get`).
- `paw.frontend.menu(kind, args)`: Menu `kind` for `args`, as plain data for a window to show.
- `paw.frontend.outputs_menu(device)`: The menu of the other output pairs of a device. For each pair, it gives `{ label, choices }`. The label names the pair and where it plays. The choices (`{ label, checked }`) are "Nowhere" and the tracks that it can play into. `act.route_pair` takes one. `act.spread_outputs` makes a track for each pair that plays nowhere.
- `paw.frontend.peaks(clip, points)`: The waveform of an audio clip at `points` points (`M.peak_points` without), as one flat list { min1, max1, rms1, min2, max2, rms2, ... }. It gives how far the wave goes each way and how loud it is, which is its body. It is not in `state`, which paw sends again each time the cursor moves. So a frontend gets each waveform only one time for each width.
- `paw.frontend.preview(id)`: A MIDI clip's notes for the small picture inside it: one flat list { start1, length1, pitch1, start2, ... }, at most `M.preview_notes` notes. Fetched when the clip's `stamp` in `state` changes.
- `paw.frontend.recent_menu()`: The recent projects the File menu lists: `{ label, path }` each.
- `paw.frontend.refresh()`: Make the frontend get the state of the project again, when nothing in the project changed. This is for data that an extension adds to the state.
- `paw.frontend.render_dialog()`: The start values of the render dialog. These are the file that a render would write, and the ranges that paw can render (`{ name, label }`: the song, the loop, the selection, each region). They are also the sample rate of the engine, and the lossy formats that ffmpeg can make here (`formats`: `{ mp3 = true, ogg = false, ... }`).
- `paw.frontend.routing(track)`: Where a track's sound goes, for a frontend to show and change:

  ```lua
  output   the name of the track it plays into ("Master" without one)
  targets  the tracks it could play into or send to, `{ id, name }` each;
           the master is first, with id 0
  sends    `{ target, name, level, pre }` each, levels in dB
  ```

  A track cannot play into itself or into a track that plays into it.
- `paw.frontend.save_as(after)`: Save the project under a new name: type it at a prompt that starts with the name of the project. A relative name goes where `:w name` puts it (`paw.files.here()`), `..` and `~` go elsewhere, and Tab completes. `after` runs once it is saved.
- `paw.frontend.send_list(track)`: A track's sends as `{ name, level }`, the level in dB.
- `paw.frontend.sidechain_menu(device)`: The menu of the side-chain of a device: "None" first, then the tracks that it can listen to. The last item tells if it takes the sound before their fader. Each is `{ label, checked }`. `act.choose_sidechain` takes one by place.
- `paw.frontend.state(known)`: The data that paw sends to a graphical frontend: transport, tracks, clips, devices and the modal state, as plain data. `known` is a list of the data that the frontend has already.
- `paw.frontend.take_preview(id, take, points)`: What take `take` of a clip plays, for the picture in its take lane. For sound, this is a waveform as `M.peaks` gives it, at `points` points. For MIDI, it is the notes as `M.preview` gives them. It repeats as a looped clip repeats. The waveform of the take that plays is the waveform of the clip, stretched. The waveform of a different take is its file, made shorter or longer in time as the clip stretches it.
- `paw.frontend.take_rows(clip)`: The takes of a clip as its take lanes show them: `{ name, key }` each. `key` changes exactly when the sound of the take changes. Nil for a clip without takes, which has nothing in the lanes.
- `paw.frontend.vca_words(id)`: What a track is in VCA terms, for a strip: a VCA's members by name, a member's VCAs by name, joined by commas.
- `paw.frontend.window_renderer_set(info)`: The window tells which OpenGL renderer draws it (see `paw.frontend.window_renderer`). One that draws on the processor is told once, in a line that says what to do.

## Module paw.fx

- `paw.fx.add(track, kind, opts)`: Add a device as a person does, from the device picker, the "Add a device" box of the window or `:device.add`. It works as `track:add_device`. Then a plugin with a window shows its window (`paw.opt.editor_on_add`), as REAPER does. Some instruments make no sound until their window opens one time.
- `paw.fx.added(device, kind, opts)`: The second half of `add`, once the device is there: remembered as used, its window shown.
- `paw.fx.card_params(d)`: A device's own parameters in the order its card shows them: the ones chosen, the one last touched, then the rest. `d` is `api.device_get`'s.
- `paw.fx.current(device)`: The name of the preset the device was last set to, if any.
- `paw.fx.default_preset(kind)`: The preset new instances of a kind start from, if the user marked one.
- `paw.fx.delete(kind, name)`: Delete a preset of a kind of device, by name.
- `paw.fx.device_line(info)`: The line that lists a device: a star for a favorite, then its name and vendor. Then the extension that it came with, if any, its format, and if it is an instrument or an effect.
- `paw.fx.device_list(wanted)`: Every device that can be added: favourites first, then the ones used last, newest first, then the rest (the kind `wanted` first, see `preferred`; built-in ones first, by name).
- `paw.fx.factory_presets(device)`: The device's own presets: a plugin's, or a built-in device's from `paw.fx.factory`. `{ name, category, id }`, in the order the plugin gives.
- `paw.fx.focus_param(id, key)`: Put the device panel's row on one parameter of a device.
- `paw.fx.hide_param(device, key)`: Take a parameter off the device's card in the window.
- `paw.fx.interactive()`: True if a person uses paw: a terminal UI is attached, or a graphical frontend asked for the state recently. Scripts (`-l`) and a kernel that nobody looks at do not count.
- `paw.fx.is_favourite(kind)`: True if a kind of device is a favorite.
- `paw.fx.learn(device, param)`: Learn a controller for a device's parameter: the next one moved moves it.
- `paw.fx.library()`: What is kept about kinds of device across sessions (`favourites`), read once.
- `paw.fx.load(device, preset)`: Load a preset into the device by name (the user's first), or one from `paw.fx.presets(device)`. One undo step.
- `paw.fx.note_used(kind, query)`: Note that a device was chosen, after `query` was typed if anything.
- `paw.fx.pick(device)`: Choose a preset of the device in a picker and load it.
- `paw.fx.pick_param(device)`: Select one of the parameters of the device: type a part of its name. It shows first on the card of the window, and it is selected in the device panel.
- `paw.fx.place(track, kind, opts)`: The first half of `add`: the device on the track, set to the preset new ones start from. What the device picker tries out before it is chosen.
- `paw.fx.preferred(track_id)`: The kind of device that a track probably needs next. "instrument" is for a track that makes sound from MIDI and has no instrument yet. "effect" is for the other tracks (a track with an instrument, the master, a track of audio).
- `paw.fx.presets(device)`: Every preset of the device: the user's first, then the factory's.
- `paw.fx.presets_dir()`: Where presets are kept: `paw.opt.presets_dir`, or `presets` in the data directory.
- `paw.fx.rank(info, query, line, wanted)`: How well a device matches the typed text, or nil when it does not match. The `@` words filter. The other words must match the whole line. A match in the name alone counts for more than a match that needs the vendor. The device selected last time for the same words comes first. A device of the category `wanted` (see `preferred`) comes before the others.
- `paw.fx.reload_library()`: Forget what was read, for tests that change the file underneath.
- `paw.fx.save(device, name)`: Save the device as it is now as a user preset. Returns the file's path.
- `paw.fx.search(query, limit, wanted)`: The devices that match `query`, best first, at most `limit`. The "Add a device" box of the window shows this list.
- `paw.fx.select(id)`: Put the device panel's row on a device of the cursor track.
- `paw.fx.set_default(kind, name)`: Mark the preset that new instances of `kind` start from, or none.
- `paw.fx.set_gain(device, db)`: A device's own gain after its effect, in dB.
- `paw.fx.set_wet(device, percent)`: How much of a device's effect is heard, in percent.
- `paw.fx.setup()`: Define the commands for devices. The runtime calls this once at start.
- `paw.fx.show_param(device, key)`: Show a parameter first on the card of the device. The device keeps this setting.
- `paw.fx.shown(device)`: The keys of the parameters the user chose to show for a device.
- `paw.fx.step(device, step)`: Load the next (`step` 1) or previous (-1) preset of the device's list.
- `paw.fx.target()`: The device the preset commands act on: the one selected in the device panel (its row stays where it was when another view has the keys).
- `paw.fx.toggle_favourite(kind)`: Make a kind of device a favorite, or not. Returns true if it is a favorite now.
- `paw.fx.user_presets(kind)`: The user's presets for a kind of device, by name: `{ name, path }`.

## Module paw.grep

- `paw.grep.entries(records)`: Records as quickfix entries: `lyric: la`.
- `paw.grep.fields()`: The fields text can be found in, for completion.
- `paw.grep.matcher(pattern, mode)`: A test of text: `mode` "regex" (`paw.regex`), "exact" (the words, each anywhere) or "fuzzy" (as the pickers match). Raises an error for a bad regular expression.
- `paw.grep.reader()`: The records of `records` read in slices, for a picker (`paw.slices`): each call of the function gives the records found in about `ms` milliseconds, and true when all are read.
- `paw.grep.records()`: Every record of every source, in the order the sources were added. A source that fails is passed over and logged.
- `paw.grep.search(pattern, opts)`: The records whose text matches `pattern`. `opts.mode` is as `matcher` takes it. `opts.fields` is a set of fields to search (all without it).
- `paw.grep.source(name, fn)`: Add a source of text, or replace the one of that name.
- `paw.grep.vimgrep(line, opts)`: What `:vimgrep` does: search, fill the list, go to the first place found unless the flags hold `j`. `opts.loc` the window's location list, `opts.add` adds to the current list. Returns the records found.

## Module paw.groups

- `paw.groups.add(track, group)`: Put a track into a group: it then sounds through the group, unless it was sent somewhere of its own.
- `paw.groups.depth(track)`: How many groups a track is inside.
- `paw.groups.dissolve(group)`: Undo a group: its members go up a level and the group, if it holds nothing of its own (no clips, no devices), goes away.
- `paw.groups.fold(group, on)`: Fold a group away, or open it, in the current window: `on` nil flips it. View state: no undo step (paw/folds.tl).
- `paw.groups.folded(group)`: True if the tracks of a group are folded and hidden, in the window a view shows (paw/folds.tl).
- `paw.groups.gather(group)`: Put a group's members right under it, in the order they are in.
- `paw.groups.hidden(track, top)`: True if a track is hidden: inside a folded group. Inside group `top` (the group of a narrowed tab), only the groups inside it count. `top` itself is open there.
- `paw.groups.is_group(track)`: True if a track is a group.
- `paw.groups.link(group, on)`: Link the faders of a group's members, or let them go: `on` nil flips it.
- `paw.groups.linked(group)`: True if the faders of the members of a group are linked. When one moves, the others move by the same number of dB. This is separate from the routing, which a group also has.
- `paw.groups.make(tracks, name)`: A new group that contains `tracks` (ids or tracks), above the first of them. Returns the track of the group.
- `paw.groups.members(group)`: The tracks that belong to a group, in the order of the track list.
- `paw.groups.of(track)`: The group a track belongs to (its id), or nil.
- `paw.groups.remove(track, stay)`: Remove a track from its group, up one level. It sounds where the group sounds, and it is in the parent group of the group, if any. It moves out of the rows of the group, unless `stay`.
- `paw.groups.rows(opts)`: The tracks that are drawn, in order: all but those folded away in the window (`paw.folds`), and in a scope only those of the scope (`paw.scope`). Rows of the arrange view and of a graphical frontend are places in this list. With `{ lanes = true }`, every row: `{ track = id }` for a track and `{ track = id, lane = id }` for an automation lane shown under it (see `paw.lanes`).
- `paw.groups.under(row)`: The tracks to draw under a row that is open in place, or nil (`paw.groups.rows` asks for each row).

## Module paw.harmony

- `paw.harmony.at(beat, latest)`: The chord that sounds at `beat`, or nil. With `latest`, of the reading as it stands, without waiting for a new one.
- `paw.harmony.builtin(from, to)`: The built-in provider: chords and keys read from the notes.
- `paw.harmony.chord_name(chord, key)`: A chord's symbol: "G7", "F/A", "Bbmaj7", spelled as `key` writes it.
- `paw.harmony.chord_roman(chord, key)`: The Roman numeral of a chord in `key`, counted from the tonic as in the major scale ("bVII", "vi", "V7", "ii°"). The name shows an inversion as "V7/B".
- `paw.harmony.chords(from, to, latest)`: The chords that sound between `from` and `to` (project beats; all of them when nil), in time order. With `latest`, of the reading as it stands, without waiting for a new one.
- `paw.harmony.degree(key, pitch)`: A pitch as an absolute scale degree (0 is the root in octave -1) and the semitones it lies above that degree (non-zero for notes outside it).
- `paw.harmony.degree_pitch(key, degree)`: The pitch of an absolute scale degree.
- `paw.harmony.draw(buf, scroll, span, zoom, origin, how)`: Draw the chords on a row of cells. `buf` is one row high, and shows `span` beats from `scroll` at `zoom` columns for each beat. Beats count from `origin` (the start of a clip, or 0 for the song). Each symbol starts on the left edge of the cell where its chord starts. It stops where the next symbol starts. The labels are as `paw.opt.chords` (or `how`) tells. It draws the reading as it stands: after an edit, the one before it until the new one lands.
- `paw.harmony.fresh()`: True if the reading agrees with the project, so `key` and `chords` answer immediately. A view that paw draws on each key asks this first, because to read a long song again takes some time.
- `paw.harmony.in_key(key, pitch)`: True if a pitch (or pitch class) is in a key.
- `paw.harmony.invalidate()`: Forget the reading: a provider whose answer changed calls this.
- `paw.harmony.is_drums(track)`: True if the harmony does not use a track: a drum track (a drum map in its meta, as the drums extension keeps it, or a drum device or name).
- `paw.harmony.key(beat, latest)`: The key at `beat` (the start when nil): the last key marker at or before it (`mk`, `key D minor`), or the key of a region over it, else the project's when one is set, else the one read there, else C major. `{ tonic, mode, name, ... }`. With `latest`, the key of the reading as it stands, without waiting for a new one: what a view that is drawn on each key asks.
- `paw.harmony.key_name(key)`: "D minor", "Bb major": the tonic spelled as its key writes it.
- `paw.harmony.keys()`: The keys over the song, `{ at, length, tonic, mode, name }` each: the key markers and the keys of regions, then the key of the project when it has one (over all of the song), else the keys read from the notes.
- `paw.harmony.label(chord, how)`: A chord's label as `paw.opt.chords` (or `how`) asks: its name, its numeral, or both ("G7 V7").
- `paw.harmony.marked_key(beat)`: The key that the user wrote for `beat` (a key marker, or a region's key), or nil. It is the one that `key` gives before the project's key.
- `paw.harmony.next(beat)`: The first chord that starts after `beat`.
- `paw.harmony.notes()`: Each note of the pitched tracks, in project beats, each with `track` and `clip`. The list does not contain muted clips and tracks, or notes that a trim of the edges of the clip hides. paw keeps the list until the project changes. This is what sounds, for the reading and for snippets. The context notes of the piano roll, `paw.roll_clips.context`, are what the roll shows, in its own beats, and only of the tracks selected to show.
- `paw.harmony.parse_chord(text)`: A chord from its symbol: "G7", "F#m7b5", "C/E", "Bbmaj7". Nil when it is not one.
- `paw.harmony.parse_key(spec)`: A key from a name ("D minor", "F# dorian", "Bb") or a table (`{ root = "D", scale = "minor" }`, `{ tonic = 2, mode = "minor" }`, or a key). A key is `{ tonic, mode, name, root = tonic, scale = mode, steps }`.
- `paw.harmony.pc_name(pc, key)`: The name of a pitch class: spelled as `key` writes it (sharps or flats), else the names most often written (C#, Eb, F#, Ab, Bb).
- `paw.harmony.pitch_class(name)`: A pitch class (0..11) from a name such as "C", "f#", "Bb", or a number.
- `paw.harmony.prev(beat)`: The last chord that starts before `beat` and is not the one at it.
- `paw.harmony.project_key()`: The key set for the project, or nil when none is.
- `paw.harmony.provide(name, fn, priority)`: Add a provider. `fn(from, to)` returns chords and keys, or nil to let the next provider answer. The lists have the shapes that `chords` and `key` give. `root`, `quality`, `at` and `length` are enough for a chord. `at`, `length`, `tonic` and `mode` are enough for a key. The highest `priority` (default 50) answers first. A new provider with the same name replaces the old one. `fn` nil removes it.
- `paw.harmony.provider()`: The provider the current reading came from.
- `paw.harmony.range(track)`: The range of a part for a track, `{ low, high, name }`. This is the range of the track (`track.meta.range = { low, high }`). If not, paw guesses it from the words of its name and the names of its devices. If not, it is C3 to C6.
- `paw.harmony.scale_names()`: Names of the known scales, sorted.
- `paw.harmony.schedule()`: Some time after the project changes, paw makes the reading again, in slices of a few milliseconds (the job `harmony`). So `harmony.changed` comes even when nothing asks.
- `paw.harmony.set_key(spec)`: Set the project's key (one edit), or clear it with nil. Returns the key.
- `paw.harmony.snap(key, pitch, dir)`: The pitch of the key nearest to `pitch`: `dir` "nearest" (the default; halfway between two goes up), "up" or "down". Stays within 0..127.
- `paw.harmony.step(key, pitch, n)`: Move a pitch by `n` scale degrees. A pitch outside the key keeps its distance from the scale note below it.
- `paw.harmony.tones(root, quality)`: The pitch classes of a chord of `quality` on `root`, root first.

## Module paw.harmony.read

- `paw.harmony.read.bar_part(run, offset, from, to, h)`: Add to `h` how long each pitch class of `run`, `offset` beats later, sounds from `from` to `to`.
- `paw.harmony.read.chords(notes, opts)`: Chords over notes in project beats, from `from` to `to` (the notes' span when nil), in windows of `step` beats (0.5). Each chord: `{ at, length, root, quality, bass, tones }` with pitch classes 0..11.
- `paw.harmony.read.correlate(h, profile, tonic)`: How well a histogram of pitch classes fits a key's profile from `tonic`, from -1 to 1 (Pearson's correlation).
- `paw.harmony.read.decode(windows, bar, pause, rows)`: The chords of a run of windows (`finish` makes each, one after another with no gap): a chord holds across windows unless the next is better by more than what a change costs. Silence of `bar` beats ends a chord. `pause`, if given, is called after each 64 windows, so that a reading in slices can stop there (paw/harmony/song.tl). `rows`, if given, keeps the work rows for the next call: a caller that decodes often gives its own.
- `paw.harmony.read.finish(p, at, length, step, beat, old)`: One window of the chord reading from what sounds in it (`p`, a part): from `at`, `length` beats long, with windows of `step` beats. `beat` gives the part of the window's whole beat, when the window needs it. `old`, a window that no one reads any more, gives its lists to the new one.
- `paw.harmony.read.fit(w, bass, total, root, q)`: How well the chord `root` `quality` fits weights `w` with `bass` and `total`.
- `paw.harmony.read.key_path(notes_hist, bars, chords, pause)`: The keys from the pitch classes of each bar (`hist`, as `bar_part` gives them, which it leaves as they are) and the chords, as `keys`. `pause`, if given, is called after each 16 bars, as `decode` does.
- `paw.harmony.read.keys(notes, bars, chords)`: Keys over notes in project beats, bar by bar. `bars` is a list of bar starts, with the end after the last bar. When `chords` (as `chords` gives them) are given, their roots and basses count two times. The harmony tells more about the tonic than the notes of a melody. Each key is `{ at, length, tonic, mode }`, with mode "major" or "minor".
- `paw.harmony.read.merge(parts)`: The parts of one stretch of time, or of stretches side by side, as one part: the weights add up, and the lowest pitch over time is the lowest of theirs. One part that sounds gives that part.
- `paw.harmony.read.part(run, offset, from, to)`: What the notes of `run`, `offset` beats later, sound from `from` to `to` (a `Part`). A note counts for how long it sounds there, a short note off the beat half; the lowest pitch over time is cut where a note starts or ends.
- `paw.harmony.read.run(notes)`: Notes as a `Run`: `notes` sorted by start, in their order.

## Module paw.harmony.voice

- `paw.harmony.voice.candidates(tones, opts)`: Each voicing of the chord in the range of the options, `{ pitches, style }`.
- `paw.harmony.voice.distance(a, b)`: How far voices move from `a` to `b`. When the chords have the same number of voices, it measures voice by voice. If not, it measures each note to the nearest note of the other chord, in the two directions, and halves the sum.
- `paw.harmony.voice.voice(tones, opts)`: The best voicing of `tones` (pitch classes, root first). The options are `low` and `high` (48 and 84), `count` (the number of voices, by default the number of tones) and `style` ("smooth"). `prev` and `next` are the pitches of the chords around it, to lead from and into. `bass` is the pitch class that must be the lowest. `center` is a pitch to stay near when there is no chord before. Nil when nothing fits the range.

## Module paw.health

- `paw.health.check(names)`: Run the checks named (all when none), each a result of `run`.
- `paw.health.executable(name)`: An executable on the PATH, or at a path: where it is, or nil.
- `paw.health.lines(results)`: Results as lines of text with their styles, for a page.
- `paw.health.names()`: The names of the checks, sorted.
- `paw.health.register(name, fn, opts)`: Register a check under `name`. It replaces a check with the same name. `fn(h)` reports through `h`. `opts.desc` tells in a few words what it checks.
- `paw.health.run(name)`: Run one check: `{ name, desc, items }`, each item `{ level, text, advice }`.
- `paw.health.worst(results)`: The worst level among results: "ok", "warn" or "error".

## Module paw.help

- `paw.help.add(path, opts)`: Add a page of help: a Markdown file in any folder. `opts.tag` is its tag and the start of the tags of its headings (the name of the file by default). `opts.ext` is the extension that it is about, and `opts.dir` is the folder of that extension. The page shows a note while the extension is not loaded. You do not add the README.md and doc/*.md of an extension.

  ```lua
  paw.help.add("/path/to/mine/notes.md", { tag = "mine-notes" })
  ```
- `paw.help.back(n)`: Back along the tags followed (`Ctrl-t`).
- `paw.help.complete(rest)`: What `:help` completes: the tags, ranked as `:help` ranks them.
- `paw.help.ex_name(line)`: The command an Ex line runs: `:%s/a/b/g` runs `s`, `:5,8co 17` `co`.
- `paw.help.excerpt_for_map(map, width, rows)`: The section of help that `for_map` would go to, as at most `rows` lines `{ text, style }` wrapped to `width`. It is for a pane next to a list of keys. The name of the page comes first. Nil when there is no help for the key.
- `paw.help.find(given, limit)`: The tags that a topic finds, best first, in the order of the `:help` of Vim. First the tag itself, then the tags that start with it, the tags that contain it, and the tags that contain its letters in order. You can write keys in the two ways: `<C-w>o` finds `Ctrl-w o`.
- `paw.help.follow()`: `Ctrl-]`: follow the link under the cursor, or find the code or the word there.
- `paw.help.for_command(name)`: The help for a command (what `Ctrl-]` does in the commands picker).
- `paw.help.for_map(map)`: The help for a key mapping: of its keys, else of the command it runs (what `Ctrl-]` does in the keys picker).
- `paw.help.grep(given)`: `:helpgrep`: every line of help that holds the words, in the quickfix list.
- `paw.help.index()`: What help knows: `{ sources, tags = name -> { name, source, row, col }, list }`.
- `paw.help.is_help(buf)`: True if a buffer is a page of help.
- `paw.help.jump(tag)`: Go to a tag: remember where from (for `Ctrl-t` and `Ctrl-o`) and show it.
- `paw.help.keyword()`: `K`: find the word under the cursor in help. It works in a page of help and in other text.
- `paw.help.lookup(topic)`: The tag a topic goes to, or nil.
- `paw.help.manual_sources(docs)`: The pages of the manual: each Markdown file under docs/. The kind of a page is the kind of its folder (docs/reference/...). If not, it is the section of docs/README.md that lists it, or the README of its folder. The name of a page is its base name (`help://options.md`, tags `options`). When two kinds have pages with the same name, the kind comes before the name (`how-to/x.md`, `how-to-x`). A page in a separate folder has its path in its kind as name (`course/05-grammar.md`). Its tags come after the folder: `course` for the README of the folder, and `course-5` and `course-grammar` for a numbered page.
- `paw.help.normalize(path)`: A path without `.` and `..`, made absolute from the current directory.
- `paw.help.open(topic)`: `:help topic`: go to the best tag for it, or say there is none.
- `paw.help.owned(index, topic, exact)`: The tag a topic an extension owns goes to: its place in the owner's pages (where `exact` is not already), else the owner's first page.
- `paw.help.owners(topic)`: The extensions that own what a topic names: the command's (`:name`), or a key's when only extensions map it (a key the core maps is the core's). A list, empty for the core's.
- `paw.help.prepare()`: Make the index of help at idle, in slices. A page that did not change since the last build is not made again.
- `paw.help.preparing()`: True while paw makes the index of help at idle.
- `paw.help.roots()`: The directories that can be a copy of the source tree, with the manual and the bundled extensions in it. These are `$PAW_HOME` (where an installed program keeps them), the parent of the runtime (`--runtime`), the tree of a loaded extension, and the current directory.
- `paw.help.show(source, row, col)`: Show a page at a row. It shows in the help window, or in a window split from the current window (as the `:help` of Vim splits). In a graphical frontend, it shows as a docked pane (`gw` moves it to a separate window). Returns the window.
- `paw.help.slug(text)`: A heading's words as a tag: `Ex: ranges, :s and :g` is `ex-ranges-s-and-g`.
- `paw.help.sources()`: Each page of help, in order: the contents, the manual (reference, how-to guides, explanation, tutorials), the extensions (each with a flag that tells if it is loaded) and the added pages. A page is `{ path, name, aliases, prefix, group, ext? }`. `name` is the name of its buffer (`help://name`). `aliases` is its tags (its title shows the first). `prefix` is the start of the tags of its headings. `group` is the kind of page in the manual, or `extensions` or `added`.
- `paw.help.tags_of_code(text, first)`: The tags that a piece of code names. A command line names its command, and `:set x` also names the option. A Lua name names itself and its modules. An address, an option, the name of a command and a key name themselves. With `first`, the code is where an item is described (the first column of a table), so each short word in it is a tag.
- `paw.help.topic_of(view)`: The topic of help for a view, for the key line: its `help` field, a section of the manual, or the page of its extension.

## Module paw.hooks

- `paw.hooks.key(key)`: Before a key is dispatched: `key.pre` sees it first. False when a handler took it, and the keymap is not to have it.
- `paw.hooks.note(name, payload)`: Count an event of this turn as a part of the edit of the turn. Undo, redo and the open of a project are not edits (`restored`).
- `paw.hooks.selection()`: The current selection: the visual selection of the focused view and the clips selected with the pointer. Also the selected notes of the clips that the piano roll edits.
- `paw.hooks.turn()`: The end of a turn, after its events are delivered: the kernel's `settle`.
- `paw.hooks.views_shown()`: The names of the views on screen.

## Module paw.insert

- `paw.insert.add(key, spec)`: Add a key, or put a new kind in place of the one on it. It goes into `paw.opt.insertkeys` (unless `hidden`), so it works at once.

  ```lua
  paw.insert.add("M", { kind = "midi", desc = "A 4-bar clip", length = "4 bars" })
  ```
- `paw.insert.back()`: `<BS>`: take back the last thing inserted, and the cursor with it.
- `paw.insert.count()`: The count typed so far in insert mode, or nil.
- `paw.insert.describe()`: What `K` says in insert mode: each key and what it inserts.
- `paw.insert.digit(d)`: A digit typed in insert mode: a count for the next key.
- `paw.insert.get(key)`: What a key inserts, or nil.
- `paw.insert.insert(key, count)`: Insert what `key` inserts at the cursor, as if typed in insert mode (`count` times).
- `paw.insert.list()`: The keys that work, in the order of `paw.opt.insertkeys`, each with what it inserts.
- `paw.insert.open()`: `<CR>`: open what was inserted last, and end insert mode; with nothing inserted, enter notes at the cursor, in a new clip if there is none.
- `paw.insert.remove(key)`: Take a key away, and out of `paw.opt.insertkeys`.
- `paw.insert.set(key, patch)`: Change what a key inserts, a built-in key too: only the fields of `patch` that are given. With `key`, the kind moves to that key (in the same place of `paw.opt.insertkeys`). The key gets a changed copy.

  ```lua
  paw.insert.set("r", { name = "Verse %d", length = "marker" })
  paw.insert.set("m", { length = "1 bar", key = "n" })
  ```
- `paw.insert.start()`: Start insert mode in the arrange view.

## Module paw.keymap

- `paw.keymap.after_next(fn)`: Run `fn` after paw gets and does the next whole command. Insert mode uses it for Ctrl-o, to return to insert mode after one command.
- `paw.keymap.all(view)`: Every mapping that can be typed while `view` has focus, each once: normal mode, then what only a selection, an operator or insert mode takes. Each comes with `kind`: "key", "motion", "operator", "object", "visual" or "insert".
- `paw.keymap.change(n)`: Go to where an earlier edit happened (`n` back, a negative `n` forward again). The first step from the place of the last edit goes to the one before.
- `paw.keymap.changed()`: Record a change that is not an edit of the project (the lines of a text buffer). Then `.` repeats the command that made it.
- `paw.keymap.changes(view)`: The places edits happened in a view, oldest first.
- `paw.keymap.classic(lhs, rhs, opts)`: A mapping as it was before the key rule. paw makes it when `paw.opt.keys` is "classic", now or later. It goes over the mapping that the rule gives the same keys. paw removes it again when the option changes back. A false `rhs` removes the keys.

  ```lua
  paw.keymap.classic("j", "track.volume by=-1", { view = "mixer", desc = "Volume down 1 dB" })
  ```
- `paw.keymap.del(lhs, opts)`: Remove a mapping: `opts.mode` and `opts.view` as `set` took them.
- `paw.keymap.delmarks(spec, all)`: Remove marks from every view, as Vim's `:delmarks` does: `spec` lists letters and ranges (`"a b"`, `"a-d"`), and `all` removes every lowercase one. Returns how many were removed, or nil and what is wrong.
- `paw.keymap.dispatch(key)`: Handle one key as if the user typed it. The kernel calls this. Scripts use `feed`.
- `paw.keymap.each(fn)`: Call `fn(map, mode, scope, keys)` for each mapping, in no order, with `keys` joined as `put` takes them. It is `every` without the sort.
- `paw.keymap.escape_hint()`: After an Escape that had nothing to cancel: a second one within two seconds outside the arrange view says how to leave.
- `paw.keymap.every()`: Every mapping in every mode and scope, sorted by scope, mode and keys. What checks the key rules walks (`tests/keys_constitution.lua`).
- `paw.keymap.expand(lhs)`: Write `<leader>` and `<localleader>` as the keys the options name.
- `paw.keymap.feed(keys)`: Type keys as if from the keyboard: `paw.keymap.feed("jj<Space>")`.
- `paw.keymap.first(mode, test, view)`: The first mapping of `mode` (in `view`, then global) that `test(map)` is true for, in the order of `list`, with no list made and sorted.
- `paw.keymap.getreg(name)`: What a register holds (the unnamed one when `name` is nil).
- `paw.keymap.goto_mark(name)`: Move to a mark. With `'` or a backtick as the name, return to the start of the last jump. With `.`, go to the place of the last edit.
- `paw.keymap.group(prefix, name, opts)`: Give a name to a prefix that only leads to more keys. The hints after it then show `+mix`, not the number of keys after it.

  ```lua
  paw.keymap.group("<leader>m", "mix")
  ```

  With `opts.view`, the name applies only while that view has focus.
- `paw.keymap.group_name(keys)`: The name given to a prefix with `group`, if any.
- `paw.keymap.groups()`: The names given to prefixes with `group`: scope -> keys -> name.
- `paw.keymap.has(mode, map)`: True if a mapping with the same keys and scope is also made in `mode`.
- `paw.keymap.hints()`: The keys that can come after the typed keys, when the user stops to type: a list of { key, desc }, and a title. Nil when there is nothing to show.
- `paw.keymap.human(keys)`: Keys as a person writes them: `<A-h>` is `Alt-h`, `<leader>at` is `Space at`, `<localleader>d` is `\d`, `<C-w>o` is `Ctrl-w o`, `<CR>` is `Enter`. Takes an `lhs` or a list of keys.
- `paw.keymap.jump(n)`: Return through the places of the jumps (with a negative `n`, go forward again).
- `paw.keymap.last_selection()`: The last selection made in the focused view, as `'<,'>` names it: the one open now, or the one visual mode last closed. Nil if there is none.
- `paw.keymap.list(mode, view)`: Mappings that apply in `mode` for `view`, the view's own first.
- `paw.keymap.mark(name)`: Set mark `name` (a letter) at the cursor of the focused view.
- `paw.keymap.marks(view)`: The marks of a view: name -> position.
- `paw.keymap.normal(keys)`: Type keys from inside a mapping, as `:normal` does. The keys run as a part of the current command, not as a separate command.
- `paw.keymap.on_next_key(fn)`: Run `fn` once, before the next key is handled: for what waits until the person is back at the keyboard (a file changed outside paw).
- `paw.keymap.operator(lhs, fn, opts)`: Define an operator: `fn(region, ctx)` acts on a region of the focused view. A region has `r0`, `r1` (rows, inclusive), `c0`, `c1` (beats, the end not included) and `kind`: "char" for a stretch of time, "line" for whole rows, "block" for a rectangle.

  ```lua
  paw.keymap.operator("gl", function(region) ... end, { view = "arrange", desc = "Loop" })
  ```

  With `count = "operator"`, the count typed before the operator is its own, as `ctx.op_count`. It tells how far or how many times: `3gUib` is three steps up over a bar. `ctx.count` is the count of the motion or object alone.
- `paw.keymap.parse(lhs)`: Split `gg<C-x>` into { "g", "g", "<C-x>" }, and expand `<leader>` and `<localleader>`.
- `paw.keymap.pending()`: The keys typed for a command that is not complete, for display: `"a2d3`.
- `paw.keymap.play(name, n)`: Play the keys in a register `n` times. `@` as the name plays the last register again.
- `paw.keymap.push_jump()`: Remember where the cursor is before it goes somewhere far away.
- `paw.keymap.put(mode, scope, keys, map)`: Put a mapping back as `map` (a mapping that `every` gave), or remove it with nil. The mapping is found by its mode, scope and joined keys (`table.concat(map.keys)`). An extension that unloads does this with the keys that it mapped.
- `paw.keymap.record(name)`: Start recording keys into a register, or stop with no name.
- `paw.keymap.recording()`: The register being recorded into, if any.
- `paw.keymap.repeat_as(keys)`: Make `.` repeat `keys` (a list of keys), not the keys typed for the command that runs now. `:adjust` does it, so that `.` does the adjusted command again.
- `paw.keymap.repeat_last(n)`: Do the last change again, with `n` in place of its count if given.
- `paw.keymap.scopes()`: Where paw finds mappings, first to last. First comes the part of the focused view that has the cursor, if the view has such parts (`view:subscope()`). For example, "arrange.lane" on an automation lane row, or a list of parts, the first part first. Then comes the view, then all views.
- `paw.keymap.search(text, dir)`: Search the focused view for `text`, forward (`dir` 1) or back (-1).
- `paw.keymap.search_next(dir, n)`: Move to the next (`dir` 1) or previous (-1) thing in the focused view that matches the last search. Views say what matches through `grid.search`.
- `paw.keymap.selection()`: The region selected in the focused view, or nil outside visual mode. It goes from the cursor to the start of the selection. Both ends are included when the view tells the size of the item under the cursor (`grid.extent`). A selection that did not grow covers one grid step. While a command runs with `:'<,'>`, it is the selection that the command names.
- `paw.keymap.set(lhs, rhs, opts)`: Map keys.

  ```lua
  paw.keymap.set("M", "track.mute", { desc = "Mute track" })
  paw.keymap.set("<leader>mz", function(ctx) ... end, { desc = "Check the mix" })
  ```

  `ctx` has `count`, `register` and, for mappings made with `char = true`, the key typed after the mapping as `char`.

  The options are `mode` (one mode or a list, default "n"), `view` and `desc`. `motion = true` is for a mapping that only moves the cursor. Such a mapping also works in visual mode and after an operator.

  `linewise = true` is for a motion across rows. `jump = true` keeps the position of the cursor for `<C-o>`. With `repeatable = false`, `.` does not repeat the mapping. `nowait = true` makes a key that also starts longer mappings run at once, without the wait for more keys.

  Each key with `role` "second+" or "second-" (the `[` and `]` of a view) does so. The same key again is a second press. Another key soon after it that makes a longer mapping (`]g`, `]q`) takes back its change and runs that mapping. On a selection, the selection opens again for that mapping.
- `paw.keymap.set_mode(mode)`: Change mode. When visual mode stops, the selection closes. `gv` opens it again.
- `paw.keymap.setreg(value, name, yank)`: Put a value in a register: the unnamed register, and `name` if given. With `yank` and no name, it also goes to `"0`, which a delete never changes. A value is a table with a `kind`. The code that yanks and pastes it decides what else it contains. `"_` discards.
- `paw.keymap.shada_project()`: What belongs to a project, for `paw.shada`: the marks, the jump lists (without where `<C-o>` is) and the places of the edits, each by view.
- `paw.keymap.shada_set_project(data)`: Put back what `shada_project` gave, in place of the marks and places now.
- `paw.keymap.shada_set_user(data)`: Put back what `shada_user` gave.
- `paw.keymap.shada_user()`: What belongs to the user, for `paw.shada`: the last search and the registers (as a table of registers by name).
- `paw.keymap.textobject(lhs, fn, opts)`: Define a text object: `fn(ctx)` returns a region, or nil when there is nothing of that kind at the cursor.

  ```lua
  paw.keymap.textobject("ic", function() ... end, { view = "arrange", desc = "The clip" })
  ```
- `paw.keymap.visual_restore()`: Open the last selection again.
- `paw.keymap.visual_start(kind)`: Start a selection from the cursor: "v" a range of time, "V" whole rows, "b" a rectangle. The same kind again stops visual mode.
- `paw.keymap.visual_swap()`: Swap the cursor with the selection's other end.
- `paw.keymap.with_selection(region_, fn, ...)`: Run `fn(...)` with `region` as the selection, the way `:'<,'>` runs a command: anything that asks for the selection meanwhile gets it.

## Module paw.keyrule

- `paw.keyrule.broken()`: Every mapping that breaks the rule, as "scope mode keys: why", sorted. Insert mode is left out (its keys enter material), and so are keys made with `prompt = true`, which answer a question on the screen.
- `paw.keyrule.lost_groups()`: Named groups of keys that lead to no key, as "scope keys (name)".

## Module paw.lanes

- `paw.lanes.any_open()`: True if a track has its lanes open.
- `paw.lanes.edit(lane_id, fn)`: Change the lane's points with `fn(points)`, which edits the list in place.
- `paw.lanes.format(lane, value)`: A value of a lane as its target shows it: "-6.0 dB", "L30", "800 Hz".
- `paw.lanes.is_open(track)`: True if the lanes of a track show as rows.
- `paw.lanes.lines()`: Every row of the arrange view in order: each track drawn, then its lanes when they are open.
- `paw.lanes.name(lane)`: What a lane is called: Volume, Pan, or its device and parameter.
- `paw.lanes.open(track, on)`: Show a track's lanes as rows, or hide them (`on` false).
- `paw.lanes.param_of(lane)`: The parameter a lane moves: its name, and the parameter's description for a device's lane.
- `paw.lanes.point_at(lane_id, beat, reach)`: The point at a beat, within `reach` beats: its index in the lane's points, and the point { beat, value }.
- `paw.lanes.shown(track)`: The lanes shown under a track: none when they are closed.
- `paw.lanes.step(lane)`: How far `+` and `-` move a point: a dB, 5% of pan, one choice, or a hundredth of the parameter's range.
- `paw.lanes.toggle(track)`: Show the automation lanes of a track, or hide them. Returns true if they show.
- `paw.lanes.value_at(lane, beat)`: What a lane's target is at a beat: the curve's value, or with no points yet the target's own value.

## Module paw.lang

- `paw.lang.add(ext, spec)`: Add a language whose files end in `.<ext>`. `spec.compile(source, path)` returns the Lua for the text of a file, or nil and an error. Or `spec.command` is a shell command that writes the Lua to its output, with `%s` for the file. `spec.name` names the language in errors, and `spec.version` goes into the cache's key: change it when the compiler changes what it makes.

  ```lua
  paw.lang.add("fnl", { name = "fennel", command = "fennel --compile %s", version = "1.5" })
  ```
- `paw.lang.cache_dir()`: The directory the compiled Lua is kept in: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/paw/lang`.
- `paw.lang.check(files, opts)`: Check the types of `.tl` files, as `tl check` does with the source tree's tlconfig.lua. `opts.include` adds directories to look for modules in. Returns a list of `{ file, line, col, msg, kind }`, kind "error" or "warning", sorted by file and line: empty when all is well.
- `paw.lang.compile(path, source)`: The Lua of a file in a registered language, compiled or from the cache. `source` is the file's text when it is read already. Returns the Lua, or nil and an error that names the file.
- `paw.lang.extensions()`: The extensions a source file may have: "lua" first, then each registered one, sorted.
- `paw.lang.find(base)`: The first file that is there of `base` with each extension of `paw.lang.extensions()`: `find("init")` gives init.lua, or init.tl when there is no init.lua. Nil when there is none.
- `paw.lang.loadfile(path)`: Load a file of Lua or of a registered language as a function, as `loadfile` does. Its errors and `debug.getinfo` name the file itself, so an extension written in another language owns what it registers.
- `paw.lang.of(path)`: The extension of `path` when a registered language has it, else nil.
- `paw.lang.searchpath(name, path)`: The file of module `name` in a registered language along `path` (by default `package.path`): each `?.lua` template with the language's extension. Nil and the files it tried when there is none.
- `paw.lang.tlconfig(root)`: The Teal configuration of the source tree (tlconfig.lua): the directories with declarations and modules (`include_dir`), and the file that declares the global names (`global_env_def`).

## Module paw.layout

- `paw.layout.alive(id)`: True if a window of this number is in a tab of the seat, or is a window in no tab (`M.loose`) that is still in use.
- `paw.layout.all_windows()`: Every window of every tab, as `{ win, tab }`.
- `paw.layout.alternate(win)`: Show again what a window (the current one) showed before what it shows now: Vim's alternate buffer, `Ctrl-^` and `:b#`.
- `paw.layout.as_tabs(spec)`: A layout as `M.restore` takes it, from any of the forms a configuration writes: a view's name (`"notation"`), a tree (`{ dir = "h", "roll", "notation" }`), a list of tabs, or what `M.capture` gives.
- `paw.layout.back()`: Give the keyboard to the window that had it before the current one (`Ctrl-w p`), else to another window of the tab. Returns false when the current window is the only one.
- `paw.layout.bind(win)`: Put the state of `win` in the table of its view, and keep the state of the window before. A window new to the view starts from that state (`fresh`). Nothing happens for a view with one state.
- `paw.layout.border_at(rects, x, y)`: The border between two windows at a cell of an arrangement (`paw.ui.arrange`). This is the rule between windows side by side, or the top row of a window below a different window.
- `paw.layout.bound(name)`: The window whose state the table of a view holds now, if any.
- `paw.layout.buf_create(type_name, target)`: A buffer of a type for a target, made if there is none. A view's type has one buffer, whatever the target.
- `paw.layout.buf_delete(buf)`: Delete a buffer (`:bd`): its windows close, and a buffer of a type that has more than one is forgotten. A view's buffer stays, as the view does.
- `paw.layout.buf_of(win)`: The buffer a window shows.
- `paw.layout.buffer_names()`: Names to complete after `:b`, `:e`, `:sp`, `:vs`: every buffer's and every view's that can be shown.
- `paw.layout.buffers_list()`: The buffers to list (`:ls`), by number: the views' that are in the layout or docked, and every other made since and not deleted.
- `paw.layout.buftype`: the same as `paw.buftype`.
- `paw.layout.capture(scopes)`: The tabs and windows as plain data: what `:layout save` writes. With `scopes`, the windows' scope stacks too (what the project keeps).
- `paw.layout.clip_named(target)`: The clip a name of a window's thing stands for: an id (`7`), an address (`paw://clip/7`) or the name of a clip, the first in the order of the tracks. Nil if there is none.
- `paw.layout.close(win)`: Close a window. The window of a view keeps its place, hidden. Other windows go. The last window of a tab closes the tab. The last window of all does not close. Returns true if it closed.
- `paw.layout.conceal(name)`: Hide the windows of a view in each tab, but the last window of a tab, which stays. Returns true if one that was on the screen went.
- `paw.layout.copy_tabs(tabs)`: A copy of a seat's tabs for a new seat: the windows keep their places and options, and start from that seat's state.
- `paw.layout.current()`: The window that has the keyboard, in the current tab. This is the last window entered, or the window of the focused view when paw gave focus by the name of the view.
- `paw.layout.default_tree()`: The tree that paw starts with when the configuration names no start layout (`paw.ui.start_layout`): the arrange view, and the panels' places next to it, closed. Nothing else depends on it: any view can be alone in a tab.
- `paw.layout.dock(name, opts)`: Dock a view in the current tab and remember the place for other tabs. See `paw.ui.dock`.
- `paw.layout.drag_border(border, rects, x, y, opts)`: Move a border to the position of the pointer. If one of the two sides has its own size, it keeps a size. If not, the first side gets a size. A graphical frontend lays the tree out in pixels (paw/panes.tl): `opts.unit` is its cell `{ w, h }`, and `opts.map` takes each node of its arrangement to the node of the tree. Sizes stay in cells.
- `paw.layout.drop_dead()`: Close the windows of buffers whose target is gone, as when another project is opened (a window with `paw://lane/9` in it): a type says so with `alive(buf)`. A window that cannot close, the last one, is left empty.
- `paw.layout.enter(win)`: Make a window the current one and give it the keyboard.
- `paw.layout.equalize()`: Give every window of the current tab an equal share, but strips that do not take the keyboard.
- `paw.layout.exchange(count)`: Exchange the current window with the next window next to it, or with the window number `count`, in their row or column. When it is the last window, use the previous window. The next window can be a split of several windows.
- `paw.layout.export(node, scopes)`: A tree of windows as plain data, for `paw.layouts` and to save. With `scopes`, each window's scope stack too: the project's screen keeps them, a named layout does not (its tracks are another project's).
- `paw.layout.find(root, name, on_screen)`: The window of a view in a tree, one on screen first: the window with the keyboard, else the one whose state the view holds, else the one that had the keyboard last. With `shown`, only one on screen.
- `paw.layout.find_id(root, id)`: The window of an id in the tree under `root`.
- `paw.layout.focusable_windows()`: The windows of the current tab that take the keyboard.
- `paw.layout.get(id)`: A window by its number, and the tab it is in.
- `paw.layout.hand_over(from, to)`: Give the state of the window `from` to the window `to` of the same view, in place of its own: a view in a window of its own that returns into its pane takes what it showed there.
- `paw.layout.import(spec)`: A node as saved, or as a configuration writes it: `"roll"` or `{ view = "roll", size = 20 }` for a window, `{ dir = "h", "arrange", "roll" }` (or with `children`) for a split. Windows of views that are not there (an extension not loaded) are left out.
- `paw.layout.layout_names()`: The names of the layouts there are: the configuration's and those saved.
- `paw.layout.leaf(view, fields)`: A new window that shows `view`, with fields such as `size` or `hidden`.
- `paw.layout.load(name)`: Put back layout `name`: the configuration's, else one saved.
- `paw.layout.loose(name, from)`: A window in no tab for the view `name`: a view in a window of its own of a graphical frontend. It starts from the state of the window `from` (the pane that it leaves), else of the window whose state the view holds now. It keeps its own state from then on.
- `paw.layout.maximize()`: Give the current window the whole tab, or put the others back.
- `paw.layout.move_to_edge(edge)`: Move the current window to an edge of the tab ("H", "J", "K", "L"), the whole height or width of it.
- `paw.layout.neighbour(dir, count)`: The window next to the current one in a direction ("h", "j", "k", "l"), `count` steps on.
- `paw.layout.one_window(name)`: True if a view is shown in one window at a time: a view without a state for each window. A buffer type is not.
- `paw.layout.only(win)`: Close every window of the current tab but one.
- `paw.layout.parent_of(node, target)`: The split that contains `target` in the tree under `node`, and its place there.
- `paw.layout.powers(scope, def, wrap)`: Map the items that `def` declares in key scope `scope` (the name of a view, or a part of a view: see `paw.keymap.scopes`). So a buffer type or a kind of text buffer declares its keys where it is made:

  ```lua
  keymaps     = { ["<localleader>r"] = fn or "command line" or { fn, desc = "...", mode = ... } }
  motions     = { ["]p"] = fn }      -- also after operators and in visual mode
  textobjects = { ip = fn }          -- fn(ctx) returns a region
  operators   = { gq = fn }          -- fn(region, ctx)
  ```

  `wrap(fn)`, if given, makes each function that the keymap calls. It can add to the `ctx` of the function (the first argument).
- `paw.layout.project_screen()`: The tabs and windows that the project keeps: `{ default, seats }`, `seats` the layout of each kind of seat (`paw.seats.kind`), each in the form `M.capture` gives. Nil when it keeps none. A project saved with one layout gives it as the default.
- `paw.layout.resize(win, axis, n, relative)`: Resize a window (the current one): `axis` "height" or "width", to `n` cells, or by `n` with `relative`. It is the window's row or column in the split along that axis that changes. Returns false when nothing can.
- `paw.layout.resolve(name)`: The type and the buffer of a name. The name is the name or the number of a buffer, or the name or the short name of a view (`roll`). It can also be a type with a target (`type://target`). Nil when the name is not known.
- `paw.layout.restore(saved)`: Put back tabs and windows from `M.capture()`'s data, or from a list of tabs as a configuration writes them:

  ```lua
  { { name = "Edit", layout = { dir = "h", "arrange", "roll" } }, { name = "Mix", layout = "mixer" } }
  ```

  Returns false when it holds no window.
- `paw.layout.reveal(name, go)`: Put a view's window on screen in the current tab: where it was, else where it docked. With `go`, a view on screen in another tab is gone to instead. Returns the window, or nil for a view that has no place (one that floats).
- `paw.layout.rotate(back)`: Rotate the windows of the current window's row or column: each moves one place on (`back`: one place back).
- `paw.layout.save(name)`: Write the tabs and windows as layout `name`, in the state directory.
- `paw.layout.scope_chain(levels)`: A scope stack from its plain data: the innermost level, each naming its parent.
- `paw.layout.scope_levels(s)`: A window's scope stack as plain data, outermost first.
- `paw.layout.set_option(win, name, value)`: Set a window option (`timebind`) on a window (the current one).
- `paw.layout.set_size(node, axis, size)`: Set the size a node takes along its parent: a panel whose size is an option (`devices_width`) has it set there.
- `paw.layout.settle()`: After a window drew or took the pointer: each view's table holds the state of its window in the current tab that had the keyboard last, so that keys and commands act there.
- `paw.layout.setup()`: Make the empty buffer type, the commands and the keys. Run once the default commands are there, as some of these take over their short names.
- `paw.layout.show_in(win, name, buf, target)`: Show a buffer in a window instead of the one it shows. A view on screen in another window moves here. `target` is what the view opens there (`roll://7`: clip 7).
- `paw.layout.shown(node)`: True if a node takes space: a window that is not hidden, or a node with such a window.
- `paw.layout.split(opts)`: Split a window (the current one) and show a buffer in the new half, which gets the keyboard. `opts`: `vertical` (side by side), `view` (the type; "empty" by default), `buf` (a buffer of a type that has more than one), `target` (what the view opens there, as in `roll://7`), `win`. Returns the new window, or nil and why not.
- `paw.layout.start()`: Lay out the screen as the configuration starts it: `paw.ui.start_layout = "notation"` in init.lua (any form `M.as_tabs` takes), or a named layout, `paw.opt.layout = "edit"`. Without either, the screen is the default tree. paw does this once its configuration has run.
- `paw.layout.tab()`: The current tab.
- `paw.layout.tab_close(i)`: Close tab `i` (the current tab). The last tab does not close.
- `paw.layout.tab_copy(name)`: Make a tab with the same windows as the current one, after it, and go to it, the keyboard in the same kind of window. Views shown in a window of each show the same state in both.
- `paw.layout.tab_go(i)`: Go to tab `i`.
- `paw.layout.tab_move(to, i)`: Move tab `i` (the current tab) to place `to` among the tabs: 1 is the first. The current tab stays the current tab.
- `paw.layout.tab_new(name, view, win, buf, target)`: Make a tab after the current tab, and go to it. It shows a buffer (the name of a view; `buf`, a buffer of a type with many) or the window `win`. Without them, it shows an empty window, the start page. `target` is what the view opens there (`roll://7`).
- `paw.layout.tab_step(n)`: Go `n` tabs on (back, when negative), round the end.
- `paw.layout.tab_title(t)`: What a tab is called: its name, else the buffer of its current window.
- `paw.layout.tidy(root)`: Merge splits of one child and splits the same way as their parent.
- `paw.layout.time_follow(lead, win)`: Call it after paw draws the main window. The other windows take its time.
- `paw.layout.time_lead()`: Before the windows are drawn: the current window, if it is time bound, leads the others that are. Returns the window to draw first and the set of windows that follow it.
- `paw.layout.title(buf)`: What a buffer is called on screen.
- `paw.layout.to_tab()`: Move the current window to a tab of its own.
- `paw.layout.view_named(name)`: The view a name or a short name (`roll`) stands for, or nil.
- `paw.layout.window_fields(name, tbl, keys, fresh, key)`: Keep fields of a view's table for each window: `keys` names them, `fresh` the ones a new window starts without (caches, what drawing measures). A new window starts with the others as they are.
- `paw.layout.window_keep(name, get, set, fresh, key)`: Keep some state of a view for each window. `get()` gives it (one value), `set(value)` puts it back, `fresh(value)` gives what a new window starts with from the value of the window it is split from. `key` names it: the same key again (a module loaded again) replaces it.
- `paw.layout.windows(root, all)`: The windows of a tree in order, the hidden ones too with `all`. A window made by code that only gave it a view gets what a window has.
- `paw.layout.within(win, fn, ...)`: Run `fn(...)` with the state of `win` in its view's table, then put back the state that was there.

## Module paw.learn

- `paw.learn.bind(source, target)`: Bind a controller to a target, in place of whatever moved that target before. `source` is { cc = 74 }, { bend = true } or { pressure = true }, or for a button { note = 36 }, with `channel` (1 to 16) or without for any channel. Returns the binding.
- `paw.learn.bindings()`: The bindings: { { source, channel, number, track, target, device, param }, ... }.
- `paw.learn.bound(target)`: What moves a target: its binding, or nil.
- `paw.learn.cancel()`: Stop the wait for a controller to learn.
- `paw.learn.clear()`: Forget every controller binding.
- `paw.learn.is_trigger(target)`: True if you press a target, and do not move it.
- `paw.learn.source(event)`: The source of a `midi.in` event that can move something, or nil: { source, number, channel, value } with the value from 0 to 1.
- `paw.learn.source_name(b)`: A controller as text: "CC 74 ch 1", "pitch wheel ch 2", "note 36 ch 10".
- `paw.learn.start(target)`: Wait for the next controller move and bind it to `target` (or to what was moved last).
- `paw.learn.target_for(word)`: The target a word names on the selected track: "volume", "pan", or a parameter of one of its devices by key or name.
- `paw.learn.target_name(t)`: What a binding moves, as text: "Lead › volume", "Lead › Filter › Cutoff".
- `paw.learn.trigger(name, spec)`: Add a kind of target that a button or a pad presses: `spec` has `press(binding, down)` (down is false when it is let go), `name(target)` (the text of `:learn.list`), and optionally `check(target)` (an error for a target that is not right), `words` (the words of `:learn` that name it), `target_for(word, track)` (the target of a word, or nil) and `under_cursor(focused)` (the target under the cursor of a view, or nil). A target can keep a number in `slot`, such as a row.
- `paw.learn.unbind(which)`: Take a binding away: by its place in `bindings()`, or everything that moves a target. Returns how many went.
- `paw.learn.under_cursor()`: What the keyboard is on, if that is something a controller can move: the parameter under the device panel's cursor, the mixer's fader.

## Module paw.limit

- `paw.limit.call(name, fn, ...)`: Call `fn(...)` with the time limit as `guard` does, but give its error to the caller and do not report it. Use it for a call whose caller must know the problem, for example a request on the control socket.
- `paw.limit.extend(ms)`: Give the current call more time, as `:lua` does: `ms` from now.
- `paw.limit.guard(name, fn, ...)`: Call `fn(...)` under the time limit for Lua (`paw.opt.lua_limit`). paw stops a call that runs too long, and reports it as `name`. paw reports errors and does not raise them. Returns the results of `fn`.
- `paw.limit.named(name, fn, ...)`: Name what runs inside the limited call, for the error should it run away: `paw.limit.named("command `x`", fn, ...)`.
- `paw.limit.timed(name, fn, ...)`: Call `fn(...)` against the budget of a callback (`paw.opt.budget_ms`): if it takes longer, paw names it as `name` once in `:messages`. A nil `name` is a timer, named by where `fn` is in the code. Returns what `fn` returns.
- `paw.limit.unhurried(fn, ...)`: Run `fn(...)` with its time not counted, for work that is known to be long and to end: `paw.limit.unhurried(synthesise, phrase)`. Callbacks the kernel makes meanwhile (timers during a wait) get a limit of their own.
- `paw.limit.untrusted(fn)`: Mark a function that the runtime did not write. Where the limit can stop compiled code, this does nothing. Where it cannot, the JIT compiler does not compile the function and each function made inside it. So the limit can stop their loops (unless `paw.opt.lua_limit = 0` disables the limit before paw loads the code).
- `paw.limit.within(ms, name, fn, ...)`: Call `fn(...)` with at most `ms` milliseconds, as `call` does: its error goes to the caller. Inside a limited call, the shorter of the two limits holds, and the rest of the outer one goes on after. Use it for code of an extension that must be fast, as a kind of clip's `compile` (`paw.opt.clip_kind_limit`).

## Module paw.loading

- `paw.loading.memory(path)`: What is remembered of a project's plugins: `stopped` maps device ids (as strings) to `{ kind, name, reason }`.
- `paw.loading.offline()`: Set every plugin offline, devices written in Lua too. Returns how many.
- `paw.loading.online()`: Bring every offline device up. Returns how many.
- `paw.loading.open(path, opts)`: Open a project, offline as `opts` says (`plugins_offline`, or `offline`, a list of device ids), and with the devices that could not be loaded last time offline as well.
- `paw.loading.project_dir(path)`: The directory the program keeps things about a project in, outside the project file: one per project file.
- `paw.loading.suggested(path)`: The devices of the project at `path` that could not be loaded last time, as a list of `{ id, kind, name, reason }`.
- `paw.loading.toggle(device)`: Set one device offline, or back online.

## Module paw.lsp

- `paw.lsp.actions_at(location, cb)`: Ask each server that gives actions, and contains the location, for the actions there. `cb(actions)` gets `{ { title, source, edit | run } }`.
- `paw.lsp.adapter(name, spec)`: Add a dialect: how a kind of server is spoken to (see paw/lsp/standard.tl for the functions an adapter has; any it leaves out are the standard ones).
- `paw.lsp.attach(which, address, keep, subject)`: Make a server keep a subject of an address open, when paw would send it and when it would not (`keep` false releases it). A clip id names its clip.
- `paw.lsp.attaches(which, address, subject)`: True if a server is attached to an address (for its subject, or for any subject).
- `paw.lsp.cancel(which, id)`: Tell a server to forget a request that it did not answer yet.
- `paw.lsp.clients()`: The servers that were enabled, as `{ name, status, error, transport, subjects, capabilities, server, pid, documents, client }`.
- `paw.lsp.code_actions(location)`: Pick a fix or an action for a location (by default what is under the cursor of the focused view; off a note in the piano roll, the diagnostics where the cursor is), and carry it out as one undo step.
- `paw.lsp.command(ctx)`: `:lsp [info|start|stop|restart|log] [name]`.
- `paw.lsp.command_complete()`: What `:lsp` completes to: its words and the configured servers.
- `paw.lsp.complete(ctx, done)`: A completion source over each server that runs and suggests, in the shape that `paw.complete.register` takes. `ctx` names the `clip` and the start of the suggestion (`at`, beats from the start of the clip), with an optional `selection` (a note set of the clip) and `controller`. paw calls `done(items)` one time.
- `paw.lsp.complete_cancel()`: Forget the completion requests still out (a newer one replaced them).
- `paw.lsp.config(name, config)`: Say how to start a server and what to show it, as `vim.lsp.config`. A second call changes only the fields it gives.

  ```lua
  cmd          the program and its arguments (or a function giving them)
  server       instead: a Lua table of handlers, run in this process
  kind         "oneshot": `cmd` is run once per version of each subject
               (placeholders `{file}`, `{input}`, `{uri}` and the settings),
               with `timeout_ms`, `accepts(doc)` (whether to run on it),
               `input(doc)` (what it is given, the subject by default)
  ```
