  ```lua
               and `diagnostic(finding, doc)` (a location, fixes)
  framing      "lines" (newline-delimited JSON, the default) or "headers" (Content-Length)
  adapter      the dialect, by name or as a table (LSP's own by default)
  attach       { subjects = { "clip", "mix", ... }, where = { focus, tracks = { "Flute*" }, drums } }
  settings     sent at initialize and with `workspace/didChangeConfiguration`
  init_options sent once, as `initializationOptions`
  restart      { max = 3, within_s = 60 }: restarts after it dies (none by default)
  env, cwd     for the process
  ```
- `paw.lsp.document(which, uri)`: The document a server holds under a URI, or nil.
- `paw.lsp.enable(name, on)`: Start a configured server (`on` false stops it).
- `paw.lsp.has(which, feature, lane)`: True if a server that runs (a client or its name) gives a feature: "hover", "completion", "actions", "diagnostics", "analysis", or "completion" with a lane: `has(name, "completion", "velocity")`. LSP's names (`hoverProvider`, `completionProvider`) are taken too.
- `paw.lsp.hover(id, pitch, beat, cb)`: Ask about a place in a clip (`pitch` and `beat` from its start), as before addresses: the same as `hover_at` on the note there.
- `paw.lsp.hover_at(location, cb)`: Ask each server that hovers, and contains the location, for its text there. `cb(sections)` gets `{ { client, lines } }` when all servers answer.
- `paw.lsp.info_lines()`: What `:lsp info` shows: each server, its transport, state, what it is attached to and can do, and what it holds.
- `paw.lsp.log_path(name)`: Where a server's errors are written.
- `paw.lsp.notify(which, method, params)`: Tell a server something that has no answer.
- `paw.lsp.request(which, method, params, cb)`: Send a request to a server. paw calls `cb(err, result)` with its answer. Returns the id of the request, or nil when the server is not there.
- `paw.lsp.restart(name)`: Stop a server and start it again.
- `paw.lsp.settle(ms)`: Wait in a script until each server started and answered all requests, and each one-shot run is complete. Stop after `ms` (10 s by default). Returns true if all of this happened.
- `paw.lsp.show_hover(id, pitch, beat)`: Show what is known about a location (by default what is under the cursor of the focused view): the diagnostics about it and what it holds, then each server's hover, in a float.
- `paw.lsp.show_lines(location, lines, sections)`: The hover float itself: the diagnostics' lines, then each server's.
- `paw.lsp.stop(name)`: Stop every server, or the one named.
- `paw.lsp.subject(name, spec)`: Add a subject (see paw/lsp/subjects.tl).
- `paw.lsp.sync()`: Update each server now. Open the documents that it is attached to, send the changes, and close the documents that it is not attached to now. Requests call this first, so they are about the current state.

## Module paw.lsp.document_module

- `paw.lsp.document_module.beats(ticks)`: Beats from the clip's start for a tick of its document.
- `paw.lsp.document_module.build(id, hash)`: The document for a clip, as `midi/didOpen` and `midi/didChange` send it, under `hash` (from `key_of`). Nil when the clip is gone.
- `paw.lsp.document_module.clip_of(uri)`: The clip a URI names, or nil.
- `paw.lsp.document_module.key(beat)`: The project's key at a beat as `{ root = 0..11, scale = "major" }`, as `paw.harmony.key` gives it.
- `paw.lsp.document_module.key_of(id)`: A value that changes each time the data that paw would send about a clip changes, and that is fast to make. It contains the notes of the clip, its position, the tracks around it, the tempo map and the key. Nil when the clip does not exist.
- `paw.lsp.document_module.tick(beats)`: Beats as ticks of `M.PPQ` a beat, the language server's unit.
- `paw.lsp.document_module.uri(id)`: The URI that names a clip: `paw://clip/12`.

## Module paw.luadev

- `paw.luadev.add_dir(dir, rank)`: Look for devices in `dir` too. `rank` (default `M.RANK_EXTENSION`) says whose script wins where two directories have one of the same name.
- `paw.luadev.check()`: Look at every script again: those that changed are loaded, and the devices made from them start again with the parameters they had. Returns what `paw.api.lua_devices_rescan` found.
- `paw.luadev.kinds_in(dir)`: The kinds of the scripts found in `dir`.
- `paw.luadev.remove_dir(dir)`: Stop to find scripts in `dir`. paw stops to offer the devices of its scripts (a script with the same name in a different folder takes their place). The devices that exist continue to work. Returns the kinds of the scripts that were there.
- `paw.luadev.watch()`: Look at the scripts' files every `paw.opt.lua_devices_watch` ms (0 for never). Started by itself once a directory is added.

## Module paw.markdown

- `paw.markdown.inline(s, style, link, out)`: The runs of a line of Markdown, each with the style and link given.
- `paw.markdown.parse(text)`: Markdown as a list of blocks (headings, paragraphs, lists, code, tables) for `render`.
- `paw.markdown.plain(s)`: The text of runs without their marks: a heading as it reads.
- `paw.markdown.render(blocks, opts)`: The blocks as lines `opts.width` wide (78 by default). `opts.heading_tag(block)` gives the tag that shows at the right of a heading (as the help of Vim shows `*tag*`). Returns `{ lines, anchors }`. An anchor is `{ row, kind = "heading" | "tags" | "code" | "lead", ... }` ("lead": the bold words at the start of a paragraph).
- `paw.markdown.width(s)`: How many cells a string takes.

## Module paw.markers

- `paw.markers.add(beat, name, opts)`: Add a marker at a beat. With `opts.length`, add a region from there; its `opts.key` (such as "E minor") is the key of the harmony over its time. Returns it.
- `paw.markers.around(beat, level)`: The region a beat is in: the innermost of those that hold it, or nil. With `level` 2, the region around that one, and so on out (the outermost when there are fewer).
- `paw.markers.at(beat, reach)`: The marker or region start nearest a beat within `reach` beats (half a grid step by default), or the region the beat is inside.
- `paw.markers.children(id)`: The regions one level inside a region, in order of time; with no id, the regions at the top.
- `paw.markers.default_name()`: A name for a new marker that has none: "Marker 3" for the third.
- `paw.markers.depth(id)`: The level of a region: 1 at the top, 2 inside one region, and so on. Nil for a marker.
- `paw.markers.find(which)`: The marker or region of a number (its place in the song), of an id given as `{ id = n }`, or of a name. Nil if there is none.
- `paw.markers.label(marker)`: What a marker is called on screen: its name, or its number in the song.
- `paw.markers.lane_row(id)`: The row of the regions' lane that a marker or region is on: 0 for the first row (the top level, and the markers).
- `paw.markers.list()`: Each marker and region, in order of time: { id, beat, name, length, color }. A region has a `length` in beats. A marker has no length.
- `paw.markers.move(id, beat, alone)`: Move a marker or a region so that it starts at `beat`. A region takes the regions and the markers inside it along, in one undo step, unless `alone`. Returns it and how many moved with it.
- `paw.markers.next(beat)`: The first marker after a beat, and the last before it.
- `paw.markers.node(id)`: The node of a region by its id, or nil.
- `paw.markers.parent(id)`: The region around a region (the smallest that holds it), or around a marker (the innermost at its beat). Nil at the top.
- `paw.markers.path(beat)`: The regions around a beat, the outermost first. Where two siblings overlap, the one that starts later is taken.
- `paw.markers.pathname(region)`: A region's names from the top down, joined by `/`: `Chorus 2/Verse A`. `:render range=` and `paw.markers.region` take it when names repeat.
- `paw.markers.prev(beat)`: The last marker before a beat, or nil.
- `paw.markers.region(which)`: A region by number, id, name or path of names (`Chorus 2/Verse A`).
- `paw.markers.regions()`: The regions alone.
- `paw.markers.remove(id, with_inside)`: Remove a marker by id. With `with_inside`, a region's regions inside it go too (never clips, nor markers); without, they move up one level.
- `paw.markers.render_regions(dir, opts)`: Render every region to a file of its own in `dir`, named by its path: `01 Intro.wav`, and inside a region `03 Chorus 2 - 01 Verse A.wav` (each number is the place among its siblings). `opts` is as for `paw.render`, plus `format` ("wav", "flac", "mp3", "ogg" or "opus") and `level`: a number renders the regions of that level only (1 the top), "leaves" the regions with no region inside. Returns the files.
- `paw.markers.set(id, fields)`: Change a marker: `fields` may hold beat, name, length (false makes a region a marker again) and color.
- `paw.markers.tree()`: The regions as a tree: the top-level regions, each a node with `region`, `depth` (1 at the top), `place` (among its siblings), `parent` and `children`, in order of time. Flat regions are a tree of depth 1.
- `paw.markers.walk()`: Every region's node in the order of the tree: each region, then the regions inside it.

## Module paw.media

- `paw.media.clear_edits(clip)`: Take away an audio clip's edit list. Returns how many edits it had.
- `paw.media.collect()`: Copy every file from outside the project's folder into `media` beside it and point the clips at the copies. A file with the same bytes as one the folder has already is not copied again. One undo step. Returns `{ copied, same, missing, dir }`.
- `paw.media.edits(clip)`: An audio clip's edit list: `{ { kind, ... } }`.
- `paw.media.gain_part(clip, from, to, db)`: A gain of `db` on a part of an audio clip, from `from` to `to` seconds of what it plays, in its edit list. Returns how many edits it has.
- `paw.media.glue(clips)`: Join audio clips of one track into one clip that plays a new file: the clips of the list, by id or as clips. A list of one clip joins it and each audio clip that touches or overlaps it. Lua can also give one clip without a list. Returns { id, file, glued }.
- `paw.media.list()`: Every file the project plays: `{ path, missing, inside, on_disk, hash, size }`. `hash` (`b3:` and 64 hexadecimal digits, the BLAKE3 hash of the file's bytes) and `size` are nil until paw has read the file.
- `paw.media.missing()`: Files the project's clips play that are not there, once each.
- `paw.media.normalize(clip, level)`: Bring the loudest sample an audio clip plays to `level` dB (0) by its gain. Returns the new gain.
- `paw.media.pencil(clip, at, values, channel)`: Samples drawn over an audio clip's (a pencil fix), from `at` seconds of what it plays, in one channel (0 or 1) or both, in its edit list. Returns how many edits it has.
- `paw.media.relink(from, to, anyway)`: Make the clips that play `from` play the file `to`, and find the other files that paw cannot find in the folder of `to`. One undo step. Returns `{ clips, found, missing }`. A file with other sound than `from` had is refused, unless `anyway`.
- `paw.media.relink_pick()`: Select a file for a file that paw cannot find, or a directory where paw finds all of them.
- `paw.media.reverse(clip)`: Play an audio clip backwards: a `reverse` in its edit list, which leaves its file as it is (a second reverse takes it away). Returns `{ edits }`.
- `paw.media.search(dir)`: Find in a directory tree each file that paw cannot find. One undo step. Returns `{ found, missing }`.

## Module paw.midifile

- `paw.midifile.encode(file)`: The bytes of a Standard MIDI File from the shape that `parse` returns (`format` 0 or 1, `ppq`, `tracks`, and `tempos`, `signatures` and `markers`, which go in the first track). Ticks can be fractions. paw rounds them.
- `paw.midifile.export(path, opts)`: Write a format 1 MIDI file with the tempo map, time signatures and markers. It contains the whole project, `opts.tracks` (tracks or ids), or only `opts.clips` (ids). Returns the number of notes written.
- `paw.midifile.import(path, opts)`: Import a MIDI file into the project. Its parts go on new tracks below the track of the cursor, at the cursor (or `opts.start`). With `opts.track`, all of it goes as one clip on that track. The tempo map does not change, unless `opts.tempo`. Then the tempo map of the file applies from its start. paw adds the markers of the file. Returns { tracks, clips, notes, skipped }.
- `paw.midifile.import_clip(path, track, start)`: Bring a MIDI 2.0 clip file in as a clip that refers to it, on a track at a beat. The first edit makes it the project's own. Returns the clip.
- `paw.midifile.is_clip_file(path)`: True if a path names a MIDI 2.0 clip file (`.midi2`), from its ending.
- `paw.midifile.is_midi_file(path)`: True if a path names a MIDI file, from its file ending.
- `paw.midifile.lost_text()`: What the last export could not keep, as one line, or nil: MIDI 1.0 has 960 ticks to a beat here, values of 7 bits (14 for the pitch bend), and no controllers of one note but its pressure.
- `paw.midifile.open(path)`: Open a MIDI file as a new project with no file (see the top of this file). Returns { tracks, notes, skipped }. If paw cannot read the file, it raises an error, and the open project does not change.
- `paw.midifile.open_clip(path)`: Open a MIDI 2.0 clip file alone, as a new project with no file: one track that plays it on the default instrument, the clip, and the piano roll on it. `:w` writes the clip back to its file. Returns the clip.
- `paw.midifile.parse(data)`: Read the bytes of a Standard MIDI File. Returns, in ticks (`ppq` for each beat) from the start:

  ```lua
  { format, ppq, length,
    tracks = { { name, instrument, length,
                 notes = { { tick, length, pitch, velocity, channel, lyric, attr } },
                 controls = { { tick, type, value, channel, number, key, program } } } },
    tempos = { { tick, bpm } }, signatures = { { tick, num, den } },
    markers = { { tick, text } }, skipped = { [what] = count } }
  ```

  Channels count from 0. The `type` of a control is "cc" (with `number`), "bend", "pressure" or "program" (with `program`). A bend goes from 0 to 16383, with 8192 in the middle. A pressure has `key` for the pressure of one note.

  Values are as in the file. paw reads format 2 files (independent patterns) as one track after the other. paw reads a file timed in frames of SMPTE time code at 120 beats a minute, because its seconds are then correct. Returns nil and a reason when it is not a MIDI file.
- `paw.midifile.parts(file, merge)`: The data for one track: { name, channel, drums, notes, controls }, in ticks. paw splits the one track of a format 0 file by channel. Each other track with notes is one part. With `merge`, all is one part.
- `paw.midifile.read(path)`: Read a MIDI file from disk: as `parse`, or nil and a reason.
- `paw.midifile.skipped_text(file)`: What was left out of a file, as one line, or nil.
- `paw.midifile.write_clip()`: Write the clip open alone back to its file. Returns its path.

## Module paw.mixer_rows

- `paw.mixer_rows.current()`: The row under the cursor, and the track it is on.
- `paw.mixer_rows.describe_row(id, row)`: What a row is called and holds, for the title bar and `K`.
- `paw.mixer_rows.device()`: The insert under the cursor, for `ge`.
- `paw.mixer_rows.rows(id)`: The rows of a track's strip, top to bottom: { key, kind, index }.
- `paw.mixer_rows.to(i)`: Put the cursor on row `i` (1 for the top) of the cursor track's strip.
- `paw.mixer_rows.to_kind(dir, n)`: Go to the first row of the next (`dir` 1) or previous kind.
- `paw.mixer_rows.to_kind_end(n)`: Move the mixer's cursor to the last row of its kind (or `n` kinds on).

## Module paw.mouse

- `paw.mouse.beat(x, scroll, zoom)`: The beat at the left edge of column `x` of a timeline whose column 0 is beat `scroll`, at `zoom` columns a beat.
- `paw.mouse.done(event)`: Called by `paw.ui.mouse` last: a move over nothing that says what it is under the pointer clears what the status line said.
- `paw.mouse.forget()`: Forget the last press and any gesture under way: the next press is not the second of a double click.
- `paw.mouse.gesture()`: The gesture under way, if any: what was handed to `grab`.
- `paw.mouse.grab(down, handlers)`: Hold the pointer from a press (`down`, as the view got it) until its button is released. Each drag goes to `handlers.drag(e)` and the release to `handlers.up(e)`, at any pointer position. `x` and `y` are relative to the view of the press, and `dx` and `dy` are the cells from the press. `moved` tells if the pointer left the cell of the press. A press of a different button calls `handlers.cancel()` and stops the gesture.
- `paw.mouse.has(event, letter)`: True if the modifiers of an event contain `letter` ("C", "A" or "S").
- `paw.mouse.hint(text, shape)`: Show on the status line what is under the pointer, or what it would do. nil shows nothing. A view calls it while the pointer moves over it. `shape` is the shape a window gives the pointer there: `"resize_h"` over an edge dragged sideways, `"resize_v"` over one dragged up or down.
- `paw.mouse.hint_text()`: What the status line says about the pointer, if anything; and the shape of the pointer, if it has one.
- `paw.mouse.mark_double(event)`: True if a press is the second press of a double click. That is the same button on the same cell soon after the first press, which was not a second press itself. For the pointer of a window, in fractions of a cell, the cell that contains it counts.
- `paw.mouse.mode(event)`: How a click with modifiers chooses: "toggle" with Ctrl, "add" with Shift, else "only".
- `paw.mouse.on_grid(x, scroll, zoom, grid)`: The same, on the grid: the step the column's left edge falls in, which is the one drawn there.
- `paw.mouse.take(event)`: Called by `paw.ui.mouse` first: true when the event was taken here and goes no further.
- `paw.mouse.to_surface(target, event)`: `paw.ui.mouse` calls this for the view that gets an event. Over the pixels that the view shows (`buf:surface`), the event goes to the `pointer` function of the view, in pixels of its drawing. A window gives it the same way (`paw.canvas`). Where the terminal reports the pointer in pixels, the position is exact. In other terminals, it is the middle of the cell. `kind` is "down", "up", "move" (with a button held), "hover", "double" (after the second press) or "wheel" (`dx`, `dy`). The modifiers are `ctrl`, `shift` and `alt`. `col` and `row` are the screen cell under the pointer, where a menu opens. A drag and its release go to the surface of the press, at any pointer position. True when the event went there.
- `paw.mouse.to_view(view, event)`: Give an event in the cells of a view to the view, for a view drawn in a separate window (`paw.canvas.pointer`). A gesture in progress gets it first, as in the terminal.
- `paw.mouse.wheel(event)`: A wheel event as a step: 1 down or right, -1 up or left. The second value tells if it goes to the side.

## Module paw.music

- `paw.music.degree(root, scale, degree)`: Pitch of scale degree `degree` (1 is the root, 8 the octave above).
- `paw.music.is_black(pitch)`: True if a MIDI pitch is a black key.
- `paw.music.name(pitch)`: Name of a MIDI note number: 60 -> "C4".
- `paw.music.pitch(note)`: MIDI note number for a name such as "C4", "f#3" or "Bb2". Numbers pass through.
- `paw.music.pitch_word(text)`: A pitch as typed in a query or an Ex range: `{ pitch = 61 }` for `c#4` or `61`, `{ class = 1 }` for `c#` in any octave; nil when it is not one.

## Module paw.nest

- `paw.nest.blocks(nest)`: Every clip that places subproject `nest`, in order of time.
- `paw.nest.content_key(c)`: A key that changes when what a block plays changes: the stamps of the clips of its subproject, and the block's own place in it.
- `paw.nest.describe(c)`: `K` on a block: `nest Ballad · 6/8 · 8 bars · follows the tempo · 2 tracks · 1 instance · live`. `c` is the clip, in the window's time.
- `paw.nest.get(id)`: The subproject `id`, or nil when there is none.
- `paw.nest.is_open(row)`: Whether a row is open in place.
- `paw.nest.list()`: Every subproject, in the order they were made: { id, name, length, tempo, meter, master, tracks, kind, meta, used }.
- `paw.nest.new(o)`: Make a subproject with a row of its own, as `:nest.new` does (see the top): the subproject over the time given, a return row below the track `below` with one block, the meter in the song's map when one is given; then the window enters it, with one empty track (`paw.opt.nest_track`). Call it in one undo step (a command is one).
- `paw.nest.notes(c, limit)`: The notes that a block plays, from its start, for the small picture inside it: { start, length, pitch } each, at most `limit`.
- `paw.nest.outputs(nest, row, how)`: Give a subproject one row of its own for each of its tracks (`stems`), or one stereo return again (`master`), on its return row `row`. Call it in one undo step. Returns the message.
- `paw.nest.promote(clip, deep)`: Promote the subproject of block `clip` to a view, as `:nest.promote` does: its tracks come back in a group named after it at the place of its return row (`paw.api.nest_promote`); its regions come back as children of a region named after it over the block (made if there is none); its own meter goes into the song's map over the block; and the window that was inside it is now inside a view of the group's tracks over the region's time, at the same place. With `deep`, the subprojects inside it too. Call it in one undo step. Returns the message.
- `paw.nest.shift`: the same as `paw.cursor.shift`.
- `paw.nest.toggle(track)`: `za` on a return row: open its subproject's tracks under it, in the song's time, or close them. On a track shown in place: close its row. False when the track is neither.
- `paw.nest.under`: the same as `paw.groups.under`.

## Module paw.option

- `paw.option.check(name, value)`: Tells if option `name` accepts `value`: true, or nil and an error that tells what it accepts. An option with no default accepts any value.
- `paw.option.define(name, default, spec)`: Give an option a default, for extensions that add their own options. The option then accepts values of the type of the default. `spec` adds more rules:

  ```lua
  paw.option.define("lanes", 4, { min = 1, max = 16, integer = true })
  paw.option.define("look", "plain", { values = { "plain", "fancy" } })
  paw.option.define("size", "auto", { type = { "number", "string" }, min = 1, values = { "auto" } })
  ```

  It gives a handle with the type of the default: `get()` and `set(value)`.
- `paw.option.definitions()`: Each option given a default by `paw.option.define`, by name: what it was given, `{ default, spec }`, the same table until defined again.
- `paw.option.full(name)`: The full name of option `name`: itself, or what its short name stands for.
- `paw.option.list()`: Every option that has a default, by name: { name, default }.
- `paw.option.read(name, text)`: The value typed text stands for in option `name` (`true`, `off`, a number, the text, or a list for an option that takes one: `a,b`), or nil and an error that says what it takes. A value that is not text is checked as it is.
- `paw.option.show(value)`: An option's value as text: a list is its items with commas between.
- `paw.option.spec(name)`: What option `name` takes besides its default's type (`min`, `max`, `integer`, `type`, `values`), or nil.
- `paw.option.undefine(name, was)`: Remove the definition of an option and its value (the extension that defined it unloaded). `paw.opt[name]` is nil again. With `was`, the value that `paw.option.definitions` gave before, that definition returns, and the value stays.

## Module paw.panes

- `paw.panes.area(width, height)`: The size of the main area in pixels, from the frontend: at the start and each time that it changes. The first time that the window of a seat gives it, paw shows the device panel when the tab has its place, closed, as the default start layout has (`paw.layout.default_tree`): a window shows the devices of the selected track next to the timeline unless the user closes them. A start layout of the configuration's own is shown as it is.
- `paw.panes.border(index, x, y)`: A border of the last arrangement (by its place in `state().borders`) dragged to `x, y`: as a border dragged in the terminal, the side that has a size keeps one, in whole cells.
- `paw.panes.cells()`: The main area in cells, with the status line and the command line under it as on a terminal: what the seat's screen is. Nil until the frontend has said.
- `paw.panes.close(id)`: Close a pane's window, as `:close` in it would.
- `paw.panes.focus(id)`: Give a pane's window the keyboard, as a click in it does.
- `paw.panes.pointer(id, event, drawn)`: A pointer event in a pane, in pixels from its corner (as `paw.canvas.pointer` takes them). A press gives it the keyboard first. For a pane drawn in cells, `drawn` tells how: its `cell`, and its size in cells, `cols` and `rows`. It keeps the button held in a drag.
- `paw.panes.state()`: The positions of all items in the main area, for the state of a frontend. `panes` is a list of `{ win, view, kind ("native", "paint", "cells"), title, x, y, w, h, focused, titled }`. `borders` is a list of `{ dir, x, y, length }`. For `dir`, "h" is a rule between panes side by side, and "v" is a rule between panes one above the other. `tabs` is a list of `{ title }`, and `tab` is the current tab. `top` is where the panes start, below the row of tabs. Nil until the frontend gives the size of its area.
- `paw.panes.tab(i)`: A click on tab `i` goes to it.
- `paw.panes.tab_close(i)`: Close tab `i`, as `:tabclose` does (its close button, a middle click).
- `paw.panes.tab_move(from, to)`: Move tab `from` to place `to` among the tabs, as `:tabmove` does (a tab dragged along the row).
- `paw.panes.tab_new()`: A new tab on the start page, after the current one, as `:tabnew` makes.

## Module paw.params

- `paw.params.apply(device, name)`: Set a device to one of the presets of its kind, by name. This is the same as a load with `paw.fx.load` (`:preset`): one undo step, and the device then has that preset.
- `paw.params.format(p, value)`: The value as text, in the parameter's unit.
- `paw.params.fraction(p, value)`: Where the value sits on a slider, 0 to 1.
- `paw.params.from_fraction(p, fraction)`: The value at a slider position, 0 to 1.
- `paw.params.is_log(p)`: True if the parameter moves on a log scale.
- `paw.params.preset_value(p, value)`: A preset's value for a parameter as a number: a choice may be named.
- `paw.params.presets(kind)`: The built-in presets of a device kind: a list of `{ name, params }`.
- `paw.params.read(device, method, data)`: Ask a built-in device for a reading: a list of numbers (`curve`, `spectrum`) or a table of named numbers (`meters`, `pitch`).
- `paw.params.step(p, value, steps)`: The value `steps` key presses away: a hundredth of the slider each, one option at a time for a choice.

## Module paw.pick

- `paw.pick.file(opts)`: Select a file from a tree of directories:

  ```lua
  paw.pick.file({ title = "Import audio", extensions = { "wav", "mp3" },
                  on_choose = function(path) end })
  ```

  Directories come first, and Enter opens them. `..` goes up. The list shows only files with one of `extensions` (all files without it). It starts in `dir`. If not given, it starts in `paw.files.here()`, the folder that relative names go to (`:cd`, else the project's, else where paw started). With `directory = true`, the first item selects the directory that shows, and `on_choose` gets it.
- `paw.pick.filter(query, items, format, primary, mode)`: The items that match `query`, best first, each as { item, text, score }. `mode` is as `paw.pick.match` takes it.

  ```lua
  paw.pick.filter("bass", { "Bass", "Bass Synth", "Drums" })
  ```
- `paw.pick.hear_file(path)`: Hear a file in a picker of files: a sound file on its own, the first bars of a MIDI file through an instrument. The label for the pane.
- `paw.pick.match(query, text, want_positions, mode)`: How well `query` matches `text`: a score, higher is better, and the byte positions of the matched characters in order. Nil when it does not match. Words of the query separated by spaces must each match. `mode` is one of `paw.pick.MODES`, "fuzzy" by default.

  ```lua
  paw.pick.match("bs", "Bass Synth")   --> score, { 1, 6 }
  ```
- `paw.pick.open(given, extra)`: Open a picker. See the top of this file for the fields of `spec`, or pass the name of a source. Returns the picker's state.
- `paw.pick.resume()`: Open the last picker again, as it was: what was typed, the mode, the line selected. Its items are read again.
- `paw.pick.show(where, how)`: Show a location: in place (`how` nil), or in a new window to the side ("vsplit"), below ("split") or in a new tab ("tab"). The view that shows it best moves there. Returns true if there was a place to go.
- `paw.pick.state()`: The open picker, if any: its query, the matches as lines, and the item under the selection. For tests and for frontends.
- `paw.pick.walk(root, limit, depth)`: Project and audio files under `root`, all at once (a test or a script wants the whole list): at most `limit` entries, `depth` folders deep.

## Module paw.plot

- `paw.plot.alpha(colour, alpha)`: A color `#rrggbb` at `alpha` (0 to 1), as `#rrggbbaa`.
- `paw.plot.bars(g, px, opts)`: Bars over time in a strip, one for each of `opts.items`, `{ beat, value, color, bright }`. `value` goes from 0 at the bottom to 1 at the top, and `bright` is for a selected item. Each bar is `opts.width` pixels wide (3), from the bottom, with a head. `from` and `pixels_per_beat` are as for `M.curve`. `color` is for the bars that have no color.
- `paw.plot.bars_cells(buf, opts)`: `M.bars` in cells: a column of eighth blocks for each item.
- `paw.plot.curve(g, px, opts)`: Draw a curve over time in a strip: its grid, the area under it, the line, and its points. `px` is the strip's size as `buf:strip` gives it (`w`, `h`, `cell`). `opts`:

  ```lua
  points            `{ beat, value, shape, tension }` each, in order, as `paw.curves` has them
  from              the beat at the left edge
  pixels_per_beat   the zoom
  frac              `frac(value)` from 0 (bottom) to 1 (top); else `lo` and `hi`
  flat              the value shown when there are no points (else nothing is)
  color             the line's colour, `#rrggbb` (the theme's `dim` by default):
                    a track's own is `paw.draw.track_colour(track)`
  fill              how opaque the area under the line is, 0 to 1 (0.16); false for none
  width             the line's width in pixels (1.5)
  top, bottom       pixels kept clear above 1 and below 0 (2 each)
  grid              bars (and beats, when `beats`) as lines, true by default
  beats             beat lines too (when beats are at least two cells apart, by default)
  guides            faint lines at a quarter, half and three quarters (true)
  markers           a small mark at each point (true)
  background        a colour to fill the strip with first (none: the cells show)
  ```

  Returns `x(beat)` and `y(value)`, where in the strip a beat and a value are.
- `paw.plot.curve_cells(buf, opts)`: `M.curve` in cells: a connected line of sextants (`paw.opt.curve_glyphs`).
- `paw.plot.lines(w, from, ppb, cell_w)`: The bar and beat lines of a plot `w` pixels wide from the beat `from`, at `ppb` pixels for each beat. Each is `{ beat, x, bar }`: `bar` is the number of the bar for a bar line, and `x` is in pixels from the left. `cut` is where paw can cut the drawing for each bar: the nearest edge of a cell of `cell_w` pixels.
- `paw.plot.span(px, step)`: The part of a strip to draw, in pixels from its left. This is the part that shows (`px.view`, all of it when all of it shows) and the width of a piece on each side. It is in whole pieces of `step` pixels from the left edge of the strip. So a piece is the same at each scroll position. Returns the first and the last pixel.
- `paw.plot.wave(g, px, opts)`: A waveform in a strip. For each pixel across, it shows the lowest to the highest sample around the middle, with its RMS as a brighter band in it. A column that reaches full scale is in the clip color. `opts`:

  ```lua
  peaks       `peaks(n)`: `n` `{ min, max, rms }` (-1 to 1) across the
              whole strip, as `api.clip_peaks` gives them; `n` is the
              strip's width in pixels, at most 65536
  color       the wave's colour (the theme's `dim`)
  rms         the RMS band's colour (the wave's, brighter); false for none
  clipped     the colour of a column at full scale (the theme's `red`)
  ```

  Heights obey `paw.opt.wave_scale`, as the cells do.
- `paw.plot.wave_cells(buf, opts)`: `M.wave` in cells: each column from its lowest to its highest sample in eighth blocks (`paw.draw.waveform`), a column at full scale in red. `opts.peaks(n)` is asked for one a column.

## Module paw.plugins

- `paw.plugins.add_dir(dir, name)`: Find CLAP and VST3 plugins in `dir` and in the usual plugin folders, for the rest of the session. Register the plugins in `dir` now. paw makes the devices of these plugins that a project contains and that paw could not make before. The list shows them as from `name` (by default the extension whose directory contains `dir`, or `dir`). It also works with `--no-plugins`. Returns `{ kinds, notes }`: the device kinds found and the files that paw cannot use. Returns nil where paw cannot find plugins.

  ```lua
  paw.plugins.add_dir(here .. "/result/lib/clap")   -- `here`: the extension's directory
  ```
- `paw.plugins.attach(path)`: Load an attachment: a native library that an extension ships, which can take each CLAP plugin that paw makes from now on, and reach the extensions of the plugin (ARA). The library implements `crates/paw-plugins/include/paw_attach.h`. Returns the name of the attachment, or nil and the reason when paw cannot load it.

  ```lua
  paw.plugins.attach(here .. "/lib/paw-ara.so")   -- "ara"
  ```
- `paw.plugins.key_names(track)`: The key names of all the devices of a track. When two devices name a key, the first in the chain wins.
- `paw.plugins.note_names(device)`: What a device calls its keys, by pitch: a plugin that implements CLAP's `note-name` (a drum kit's drums, a sampler's keyswitches), or a built-in device of `M.builtin_names` (the `drums` kit). Empty for the rest. Asked again after `M.names_ttl`.
- `paw.plugins.remove_dir(dir)`: Stop to find plugins in `dir`, and stop to offer the devices found there. The devices that exist continue to work.

## Module paw.profile

- `paw.profile.entries(report)`: The functions of a report as entries of the quickfix list: the share of the samples, the name, the file and the line.
- `paw.profile.running()`: Whether `jit.profile` runs, and the samples it took so far.
- `paw.profile.start(file)`: Start `jit.profile`, which takes a sample of the Lua code each millisecond. With `file`, `stop` writes the folded stacks there. Fails when it runs already.
- `paw.profile.stop()`: Stop `jit.profile`. Returns the samples, the seconds and the functions that took the most time. Writes the folded stacks to the file that `start` was given. Fails when it does not run.

## Module paw.qf

- `paw.qf.cdo(line, opts)`: Run a command line on each entry of the current list of a stack (`:cdo`), all as one undo step. For each entry, the cursor goes to the entry first. The command gets the address as `ctx.target`, and the whole location as `ctx.location`. With `per_track`, it runs one time for each track of the entries (`:cfdo`). Returns how many times it ran.
- `paw.qf.changed(source)`: Tell paw that the entries of a source can be different now.
- `paw.qf.close(loc)`: Close the windows of the tab that show the quickfix list (`loc`: the location list of the current window). Returns true if one closed.
- `paw.qf.count(list)`: How many entries of each level a list has: `{ error, warning, info, hint, total }`.
- `paw.qf.current(stack)`: The current list of a stack (the quickfix lists by default), or nil.
- `paw.qf.diagnostics(opts)`: Put diagnostics in a list, as `vim.diagnostic.setqflist`: `opts` has `target` and `severity` (as `paw.diagnostic.get` takes them), `title` ("Diagnostics"), `win` for a location list, `open` to open its window.
- `paw.qf.entry(e, source)`: An entry as the list keeps it: `{ address, location, text, level, severity, source, fix, data }`.
- `paw.qf.fed(source)`: What a source has in the Problems list now.
- `paw.qf.feed(source, entries)`: The current entries of a source, in the Problems list. These entries replace the old entries of the source (none removes them). Each extension can feed it.

  ```lua
  paw.qf.feed("tuning", { { address = "paw://clip/4", text = "out of tune", level = "warning" } })
  ```
- `paw.qf.first(stack)`: Go to the list's first entry, or its last.
- `paw.qf.fix(entries, opts)`: Do the fixes of entries as one undo step: each entry with a fix in the current list of a stack, or the given entries. Returns how many.
- `paw.qf.fix_title(e)`: The title of an entry's fix, or nil.
- `paw.qf.format(e, list)`: An entry in one line, as said when going to it: `(2 of 7) error: …`.
- `paw.qf.from_diagnostics(target, filter)`: Diagnostics as entries (as `paw.diagnostic.get` takes `target` and `filter`).
- `paw.qf.go(e)`: Put the cursor on the address of an entry, in the view that shows it best, and focus that view. A note goes to the piano roll, and a device or a parameter to the device panel. A clip, a track, a lane or a range of time goes to the arrange view. Returns true if there was a place to go.
- `paw.qf.jump(n, stack)`: Make entry `n` of a stack's current list the current entry and go to it.
- `paw.qf.last(stack)`: Go to the list's last entry.
- `paw.qf.loc_stack(win, make)`: The location lists of a window (of the current window without `win`), made when you ask with `make`. A window that shows a location list uses the list that it shows, as in Neovim.
- `paw.qf.newer(count, stack)`: Go to a newer list in the history (`count` on).
- `paw.qf.older(count, stack)`: Go to an older list in the history (`count` back), or a newer one.
- `paw.qf.open(opts)`: Open the window of the list and give it the keyboard. The quickfix list opens along the bottom of the tab, the whole width (`opts.height` rows, or `paw.opt.qf_height`). A location list opens below its window (`opts.loc`, with `opts.win` the window, the current one by default). If a window of the tab shows the list already, paw goes to it. Returns the window.
- `paw.qf.refresh()`: Read every source of the Problems list again.
- `paw.qf.set(entries, opts)`: Put a list of entries in the quickfix lists (the location lists of a window with `opts.win`, of the current window with `opts.win = true`), with the title `opts.title`, and make it current. A list with the same title in the history is replaced at its place. Its current entry stays. `opts.current = false` keeps a different list current. Returns the list.

  ```lua
  paw.qf.set({ { address = "paw://track/3", text = "too quiet", level = "warning" } }, { title = "Levels" })
  ```
- `paw.qf.severity_of(level)`: A severity from 1 (error) to 4 (hint) from a number or a word. Nil for none.
- `paw.qf.source(source, fn)`: A source that paw asks for its entries when they can change. `fn()` returns them. paw calls it again after `paw.qf.changed(source)`, one time, when a user next looks at the list.
- `paw.qf.stack()`: The quickfix lists.
- `paw.qf.status()`: The part of the status line while the quickfix list has entries: `qf 2/7 E2 W5`, with the position after you go to an entry. Nil when the list is empty.
- `paw.qf.step(count, stack)`: Go `count` entries forward (back, when negative) from the current entry. The first `]q` goes to the first entry. It stops at the ends, as Neovim does.
- `paw.qf.where(e)`: The subject of an entry, in a few words: `Bass 3.1.00`, `Lead › Synth`, `mix.wav`. Empty without an address.

## Module paw.query

- `paw.query.articulations(node)`: A note's articulations: its attribute's (`paw.attr`: the tag, the name and the code, so `pz`, `pizzicato` and `11.A` all find a pizzicato), those the score marks (`meta.notation.art`, a set) and any named in `meta.articulation` (a name or a list of them).
- `paw.query.describe(node)`: A node in a few words, for the quickfix list: `C5 vel 100 at 5.1.00 · Violins pizz`.
- `paw.query.entries(nodes)`: The nodes as quickfix entries.
- `paw.query.field(kind, name, get)`: Add a field to a kind of node: `get(node)` returns its value (a number, text, a boolean, or a list of texts any of which may match).

  ```lua
  paw.query.field("note", "channel", function(node) return node.data.meta.channel end)
  ```
- `paw.query.get(node, name)`: A node's field, or nil.
- `paw.query.location(node)`: A node's location, as the quickfix list and `paw.qf.go` take them.
- `paw.query.parse(q)`: Read a query (text or the table form) once, to run it often. Raises an error that says what is wrong with it.
- `paw.query.run(q)`: Every node a query finds, in the order of the tree (each query of a list of them in turn, none twice).

  ```lua
  for _, n in ipairs(paw.query("note[pitch>=c6]")) do print(n.data.pitch) end
  ```
- `paw.query.select(q, opts)`: Select the items that a query finds, where paw can select them. These are its clips in the arrange view, and its notes in the piano roll (the notes of each clip). Put all found items in the quickfix list (the location list of the window with `opts.loc`). Returns the nodes.

## Module paw.recent

- `paw.recent.clear()`: Forget them all.
- `paw.recent.list()`: The projects opened or saved last, newest first: `{ path, name, time }` (`time` is when, in seconds since 1970). A file that is gone is left out.
- `paw.recent.menu()`: What the window's menu shows: `{ label, path }` each.
- `paw.recent.open(which)`: Open a project from the list, by its place in the list or its path. If it does not open, paw tells you. Returns true if it opened.
- `paw.recent.reopen_last()`: At the start, with no project named: open the newest one when `paw.opt.reopen_last` asks for it. A project that will not open is a message, not the end of the program.
- `paw.recent.use(file)`: Keep the list in `file`, and remember projects for all start options, for tests. `use()` sets all back to the old values.

## Module paw.reconnect

- `paw.reconnect.reconnect()`: Try to open again the device that went away. Returns true if it is open.

## Module paw.regex

- `paw.regex.compile(text, opts)`: Compile an expression so that it is ready to match. If it is not correct, raise an error that tells the problem. `opts.case` true matches case, and false ignores case. By default, an expression in lowercase ignores case.
- `paw.regex.try(text, opts)`: An expression ready to match, or nil and what is wrong with it.

## Module paw.remote

- `paw.remote.closed(client)`: A connection closed: nothing more is sent to it.
- `paw.remote.listeners()`: The listeners: `{ client = { patterns = {...}, watching = bool }, ... }`.
- `paw.remote.push(client)`: Send to a connection the changes of the state of the frontend after the last send. Send nothing when nothing changed.
- `paw.remote.touch()`: A turn had input: a key, the pointer, a call. What the frontends show can be different.
- `paw.remote.turn()`: After each turn of the kernel: push now what its input or its edits changed, at most once in 8 ms.
- `paw.remote.wake()`: Something started to move (the song, a note played): push at the pace from now.

## Module paw.render

- `paw.render.cancel`: the same as `paw.render_cancel`.
- `paw.render.default_path()`: The file a render writes when no file is named: the project's name, in `renders_dir()`.
- `paw.render.render(path, opts)`: Render the project to a file: WAV or FLAC, or MP3, Ogg Vorbis or Opus when ffmpeg is installed (`paw.opt.ffmpeg` says where it is, if not on the PATH), by the file's extension. A lossy file is rendered to a temporary WAV, which ffmpeg then encodes. `opts` (all optional):

  ```lua
  range       "song" (the default), "loop", "selection", or a name in `paw.render_ranges`
  start, end  beats, instead of a range (`end` defaults to the end of the last clip)
  tail        seconds after the end, for reverbs and delays to ring out (1)
  sample_rate (or rate) Hz; the engine's by default
  bits        16, 24 or 32 (float; WAV only); 24 by default
  channels    2 (or "stereo") or 1 (or "mono")
  dither      true to add dither when writing 16 or 24 bits
  quality     for MP3, Ogg Vorbis and Opus: "low", "medium", "high" (the
              default) or "best"; `bitrate` (kbit/s) instead of it for a number
  tags        { title, artist, album, track, year, genre, comment, cover } written into
              the file, over the project's own (`paw.render_tags`); `cover` is a PNG or
              JPEG file (a WAV holds no cover); the title of a lossy file is the project's name by default
  normalize   bring the loudest sample to this level in dB, such as -1
  loudness    bring the integrated loudness to this level in LUFS, such as -14;
              with `normalize` too, the peak level is a ceiling
  tracks      { id, ... }: only these, with what they pass through (a stem)
  master      false to leave out the master track's devices, fader and pan
  threads     threads to render on
  background  true to return at once and render on a thread of its own:
              `render.progress` ({ path, fraction, seconds }) follows now
              and then, and `render.done` (what is returned below),
              `render.failed` ({ path, error }) or `render.cancelled` at the end;
              a render in the foreground emits `render.finished` with what it returns
  ```

  When it is done, it returns `types.RenderResult`. The result has the path, the frames, the seconds, the peak, the gain and the loudness. It also has the format, the bits (nil for a lossy format) and the channels.

  paw emits `render.before` first. Its handlers run before the render starts, so an extension that makes audio of its own can complete it. paw refuses a file that it cannot write before it renders. When a render fails or stops, no file has the name that you gave.
- `paw.render.renders_dir()`: The folder that renders go to when no place is named: `renders/` in the project's folder, apart from the files of the project; the folder of a project kept in one file; nil before the first save.
- `paw.render.status`: the same as `paw.render_status`.
- `paw.render.stems`: the same as `paw.render_stems`.
- `paw.render.tags`: the same as `paw.render_tags`.

## Module paw.roles

- `paw.roles.begin(name, win)`: A view is about to be drawn on the terminal's screen (`win`, the id of its window, if any): its hit regions start afresh.
- `paw.roles.define(name, spec)`: Define a role. `spec.cells(buf, props, ctx)` draws it in cells. It is necessary, because the terminal comes first. `spec.props` names its props and their contents, for documentation and `paw.ui.roles`. `spec.bound` is the props that a frontend takes from the live value when the mark is bound to one. paw does not send these props.
- `paw.roles.finish()`: The view being drawn is done: what it marks after is no hit region.
- `paw.roles.gesture(view, e)`: An event on a hit region (`e.hit`, `e.rect`) to its view: true when it was taken.
- `paw.roles.hit(buf, x, y, w, h, action)`: `buf:hit(x, y, w, h, action)`: make an area a hit region. A press, a move or the wheel there goes to the view's gesture for `action.kind`, in either frontend.
- `paw.roles.input(client, id, view, win, event, held)`: A pointer event from a frontend that gets scenes (paw/scene.tl), in units of its window `id`, over the view `view` (its window of the layout `win`, if any). On a hit region of the scene, the event goes to the gesture of the region, with `x` and `y` in units. A drag that started there continues in units (`held`, which the watcher of the frontend keeps). True when it takes the event.
- `paw.roles.mark(buf, role, x, y, w, h, props)`: `buf:mark(role, x, y, w, h, props)`: mark a role over an area. A terminal draws the cells of the role there. A frontend that knows the role paints it as what it is. `props.hit` makes it a hit region, and `props.bind` ties it to a live value. Returns the buffer of the area.

  ```lua
  buf:mark("fader", 4, 2, 3, 12, { at = 0.8, hit = { kind = "fader", track = id } })
  ```
- `paw.roles.plane(buf, x, y, w, h, opts)`: `buf:plane(x, y, w, h, opts)`: a plane over an area. Each axis of the plane has its own domain, `opts.x` and `opts.y` (`{ domain, from, per }`): `per` is the cells for one unit of the domain, and `from` is the value at the edge of the area. A terminal shows a mark on the cells it rounds to. A window shows it at its exact position.

  ```lua
  local roll = buf:plane(5, 2, 60, 20, { key = "roll", x = { domain = "beat", from = 0, per = 4 },
    y = { domain = "pitch", from = 73, per = -1 }, hit = { kind = "grid" } })
  roll:mark("note", 1.5, 60, 0.5, 1, { label = "C4" })
  ```
- `paw.roles.pointer(view, name, event)`: A mouse event in the terminal, in the cells of the view it is over (as its `on_mouse` takes it, with `view_x`, `view_y`, `win`): to the gesture of the hit region under it. True when it was taken.

## Module paw.roll_clips

- `paw.roll_clips.activate(id)`: Make a clip the active clip. A clip that is not editable yet takes the place of the old active clip in the set. The cursor stays at its position in the song.
- `paw.roll_clips.active()`: The id of the active clip, or nil with no clip open.
- `paw.roll_clips.context()`: The context notes, in the beats of the roll. These are the notes of the other clips of the active clip's track, and of the clips of the shown tracks (not the editable clips), that sound in the range of the editable clips. Each is `{ pitch, start, length, velocity, clip, track, color }`, at most `paw.opt.roll_context_max` of them. paw keeps them until the project, the set of clips or the toggles change.
- `paw.roll_clips.context_at(pitch, beat)`: The context note on `pitch` that sounds at roll beat `beat`, if any.
- `paw.roll_clips.cycle(n)`: Make the clip `n` places after the active one (before it, with a negative `n`) active, the editable clips taken in the order they start.
- `paw.roll_clips.editable(id)`: True if a clip is one of the editable clips.
- `paw.roll_clips.ids()`: The ids of the editable clips, the active one first, then the others in the order they were added. In a narrowed window, only the clips that its scope shows (the active one always).
- `paw.roll_clips.note_at(pitch, beat, parts)`: The note of an editable clip on `pitch` that sounds at roll beat `beat`, the active clip first. Returns the note (in the beats of the roll), its place and its part.
- `paw.roll_clips.notes(range, parts)`: The notes of the editable clips in the roll's beats, in the order they start (lower pitches first in a chord), each with `clip` (its clip's id), `place` (its place among that clip's notes, for `edit_notes`) and `offset`. With one clip they are that clip's notes in its own order. `range` is as for `Clip:notes`, its beats the roll's.
- `paw.roll_clips.offset(id)`: Where a clip's beats are in the roll: add this to them.
- `paw.roll_clips.only()`: Edit the active clip alone. This is what paw does when you open a clip.
- `paw.roll_clips.open(ids, active)`: Edit these clips together. `active` (or the first of them) gets the new notes. paw does not use clips that are not MIDI.
- `paw.roll_clips.parts()`: The editable clips, the active one first: `{ id, clip, offset, start, length, track, name }` each, `clip` a handle (`paw.clip`).
- `paw.roll_clips.pick()`: `:roll.tracks`: a list of the tracks near the roll and of their clips. On a track, Enter shows or hides its notes. On a clip, Enter adds it to the editable set or removes it.
- `paw.roll_clips.rows()`: Each clip near the roll, as rows for a list. Each shown track is a row (`kind` "track", `on` tells if its notes show). Under it are its MIDI clips in the range of the roll (`kind` "clip", `on` tells if it is editable, `active`). The track of the active clip is first, with its clips.
- `paw.roll_clips.show_track(id, on)`: Show the notes of a track behind the notes of the roll, or not. nil returns to the value of `paw.opt.roll_context`.
- `paw.roll_clips.sounding(beat)`: The pitches that sound at roll beat `beat`, in the editable clips and the context, lowest first. The second value is the name of the chord that they make, when `paw.harmony` can tell it.
- `paw.roll_clips.span()`: The stretch of the roll the editable clips cover: from, to. In a scope with time, only its time, as the arrange view (`0` and `$` stop there).
- `paw.roll_clips.step_track(n, wrap)`: Make active the track `n` places after the track of the active clip, in the tracks that the roll shows (before it with a negative `n`). Its clip under the cursor gets the new notes. The notes of the old clip show behind. With `wrap`, it goes round. False when the roll shows no other track.
- `paw.roll_clips.target(beat, parts)`: The editable clip a new note at `beat` goes into: the active one, unless the beat is outside it and inside another. Returns the part.
- `paw.roll_clips.toggle(id)`: Add a clip to the editable set, or remove it. If you remove the active clip, the next clip becomes active. The last clip stays.
- `paw.roll_clips.tracks()`: The tracks whose notes can show behind the notes of the roll. These are the tracks with MIDI clips (of the scope, in a narrowed tab), but not the track of the active clip. `{ id, name, color, drums, on }` each. `on` tells if its notes show.
- `paw.roll_clips.visible()`: The tracks whose notes the roll shows, in the order of the track list: the active clip's and those shown behind it.

## Module paw.roll_draw

- `paw.roll_draw.accidental(semitones)`: `#` or `b` right after `r` and a name: a semitone up or down.
- `paw.roll_draw.active()`: True if you draw a note now: insert mode in the piano roll, the kind that draws.
- `paw.roll_draw.again()`: Keep the notes being drawn and draw them again where they end (`.`), count times.
- `paw.roll_draw.append()`: The next insert mode takes up the note under the cursor at its end, or starts a step on (`a`).
- `paw.roll_draw.articulate()`: Give the notes being drawn an articulation (`a`): asked by name, with the names of the track's instrument to complete.
- `paw.roll_draw.articulation(provider)`: Set where `a` takes articulations from (the articulations extension does): `names(track)` and `apply(track, text, note)`.
- `paw.roll_draw.back()`: Take back the last note kept: it is the one being drawn again.
- `paw.roll_draw.back_all()`: Take back all that this insert drew (`Ctrl-u`): the pencil is where it began.
- `paw.roll_draw.bend(dir)`: Bend the notes being drawn by `dir` steps of `bend_step` semitones (times the count): their own pitch bend rises (or falls) to that at their end, from half of each.
- `paw.roll_draw.bend_of(controls, note)`: The bend of a note of a clip in the clip's beats, or nil: `semis` at its end and where its ramp starts, as a fraction of its length. The piano roll shows it on the note, `K` says it.
- `paw.roll_draw.chord(pitches, name)`: Make the notes being drawn these pitches, the first under the cursor: a chord at the same start and as long.
- `paw.roll_draw.click_step()`: The Step button of the window: step input on or off, from normal mode too.
- `paw.roll_draw.controls_of(id)`: Per-note bends of a clip, read once for each frame that shows it.
- `paw.roll_draw.describe()`: The note being drawn, in words: `C4 · end · 2 steps · 0.5 beats`, or nil.
- `paw.roll_draw.digit(d)`: A digit of the count for the next key, or of a length after `=`.
- `paw.roll_draw.edge(edge)`: Go to the other edge of the note (`o`), or to `edge`.
- `paw.roll_draw.edge_now()`: The edge the cursor is on: "start" or "end", nil when not drawing.
- `paw.roll_draw.erase()`: Erase the notes being drawn (`x`): a clip's note goes when insert mode writes; the pencil stays, with nothing long.
- `paw.roll_draw.expression(what)`: A point of expression at the pencil (`e` then what): `em` the modulation wheel, `ee` expression, `eb` breath, `es` the sustain pedal, `e` and a number any controller. A count first is the value (`100em`); else paw asks it.
- `paw.roll_draw.extend(count)`: Make the notes being drawn `count` steps longer (the pedal pressed while keys are held, in step input).
- `paw.roll_draw.finish()`: End the drawing: write it, and forget it. Returns what it did, in words.
- `paw.roll_draw.grow(steps)`: Move the edge under the cursor `steps` grid steps right, or left with a negative count: at the end, the note grows; at its start, it shrinks. No note grows over the next note of its pitch.
- `paw.roll_draw.hidden(clip)`: The ids of a clip's notes that the pencil holds, which the roll does not draw where they were: they show where the pencil has them.
- `paw.roll_draw.key(lhs, spec)`: A key of the pencil from an extension: `lhs` in the piano roll's insert mode, `spec.run(count, char)` with the count typed before it (and the key typed after it, with `spec.char`). It reads and changes `paw.roll_draw.pen()`, then calls `paw.roll_draw.shown()`.

  ```lua
  paw.roll_draw.key("gs", { desc = "Staccato: half as long", run = function(n) ... end })
  ```
- `paw.roll_draw.label()`: What the piano roll's title says in insert mode.
- `paw.roll_draw.length_key(char)`: Start typing a length (`=`), or add to it: each key that makes one sets the notes being drawn that long at once.
- `paw.roll_draw.mark(kind)`: Put a mark of the song at the pencil's start (`m` then its kind): `k` a key change, `t` a tempo, `s` a time signature from the bar, `'` a marker. Each asks its value, and is in the insert's undo step.
- `paw.roll_draw.name(letter)`: Set the pitch by its name (`r` then a letter): the nearest of that name, the chord with it. `#` and `b` next make it sharp or flat.
- `paw.roll_draw.next(how)`: Keep the notes and go on. "legato" starts the next note at the end, "rest" a step (the note length, or count steps) after it; a note of the clip that starts there is taken up. "chord" draws another note at the same start and as long (`chord`'s count stacks).
- `paw.roll_draw.nudge(steps)`: Move the notes being drawn `steps` grid steps later, or earlier: `>` `<`.
- `paw.roll_draw.pen()`: The notes being drawn now, as `{ pitch, start, length, velocity }` in project beats, the one under the cursor first. An extension's key changes them in place, then calls `paw.roll_draw.shown()`.
- `paw.roll_draw.pick_chord(strum)`: Choose a chord to draw at the pencil (`c`): the diatonic chord on the pencil's pitch first (`4c` its seventh, `5c` its ninth), the others of the key, then common chords on the pitch. Typing searches them; a symbol typed (`V7/V`, `F#m9/C#`, `C4maj7`) is drawn as typed. The chord takes the note's place, its start and length, and the keys shape it as one note until Enter or Escape.
- `paw.roll_draw.pitch(semitones, step)`: Move the notes being drawn by `semitones` (times the count), and hear the new pitch. `step(pitch, n)`, if given, says where `n` such moves go instead: by steps of a scale, say.
- `paw.roll_draw.put_register(name)`: Put the notes of a register at the pencil (`<C-r>` and its name), count times one after another, as `p` pastes them. The pencil goes on where the last one ends. A stretch of time keeps its pitches, and the rest go with their top at the pitch of the pencil. Notes always start from the pencil.
- `paw.roll_draw.shown()`: Show what an extension's key changed in the notes being drawn.
- `paw.roll_draw.snippet()`: Choose a snippet to expand at the pencil (`<Tab>`), count times.
- `paw.roll_draw.start(how)`: Start drawing at the cursor. `how` as `take` has it: "i" or "a"; or "step", step input with a caret (a pen with no length) at the cursor.
- `paw.roll_draw.status()`: What the window says while in insert mode.
- `paw.roll_draw.step_next()`: The next insert mode is step input (`I` in normal mode).
- `paw.roll_draw.stepping()`: True while step input is on: insert mode in the piano roll, with the keys of a MIDI controller entering notes (`I`).
- `paw.roll_draw.suggest(dir)`: Show the next (`dir` 1, `<C-n>`) or the previous (-1, `<C-p>`) suggestion in place of the notes being drawn. Any key that edits takes it; `<C-e>` puts back what was there.
- `paw.roll_draw.text()`: The notes that you drew and kept, as "60@1+0.5 64@1+0.5" in the beats of the roll. The second value is the notes that you draw now, "67@1.5+0".
- `paw.roll_draw.tie()`: Tie the note being drawn to the next note (`~`): its end goes to where the next note of the clips, or the next note kept, starts.
- `paw.roll_draw.toggle_step()`: Step input on or off (`I` in insert mode). The pen stays as it is. Without a MIDI input, paw says why and opens the track's list of inputs.
- `paw.roll_draw.unsuggest()`: Put back the notes that were there before the suggestions (`<C-e>`).
- `paw.roll_draw.value(value)`: Set the step (and the notes being drawn) to a note value, as `=` then `value` does: "8", "8.", "8t". `dot` and `triplet` turn the dot or the triplet of the step on and off.
- `paw.roll_draw.velocity(dir)`: The velocity of the notes being drawn and of the next, by `dir` tens.

## Module paw.routes

- `paw.routes.feeds(from, into)`: True if the sound of `from` goes to `into`.
- `paw.routes.midi_out_text(t)`: Where a track sends MIDI, as text: `Synth · channel 2 · MPE`, or "no MIDI output".
- `paw.routes.outputs(device)`: The output pairs of a device: `{ pair, name, target, target_name }` each, the main pair (pair 1, on its own track) first. Empty for a device with one pair.
- `paw.routes.peers(track)`: The tracks a track may route to: those of its place, the song or its subproject (the tracks of a subproject route only to each other).
- `paw.routes.reached(from)`: The tracks a track's sound reaches, directly or through others, as a set of ids: by outputs, sends and side-chains.
- `paw.routes.reaching(into)`: The tracks whose sound reaches a track, as a set of ids.
- `paw.routes.set_midi_out(track, name, channel, form, members)`: Send the MIDI of a track to the port named `name` (or a part of its name, "none" for none). `channel` is 1 to 16, or nil for the channel of each message. `form` applies where the port does not accept MIDI 2.0 (a key of `M.midi_out_forms`, nil keeps the current form). MPE uses `members` channels (nil for 15).
- `paw.routes.set_output(device, pair, track)`: Play a device's output pair `pair` (2 and on) into a track (a track, its id or name; nil or "none" for nowhere). Errors say why it cannot be.
- `paw.routes.set_sidechain(device, track, pre)`: Set a device's side-chain by a track, a track's id or name ("none" or nil for none), and `pre`. Errors say why it cannot be.
- `paw.routes.setup()`: Define the commands for sends and sidechains. The runtime calls this once at start.
- `paw.routes.sidechain_sources(device)`: The tracks that a device can listen to, `{ id, name }` each, in the order of the track list. Its own track, the master and the tracks that its track feeds are not in the list.
- `paw.routes.sidechain_text(d)`: What a device listens to, as text: the name of the track, with `pre` when it takes the sound before the fader. Nil if it listens to nothing.
- `paw.routes.spread(device)`: Make a track for each output pair of a device that plays nowhere yet, with the name of the pair, and send the pair there. paw puts the new tracks and the track of the device in a group (or in the group of the track of the device). The track of the device cannot be the group, because its pairs feed the new tracks, which would then feed it again. Returns the new tracks.

## Module paw.ruler

- `paw.ruler.add(name, spec)`: Add a part of the bar labels, or put a new one in place of one of that name. It goes into `paw.opt.barlabel` (unless `hidden`).
- `paw.ruler.add_lane(name, spec)`: Add a lane of rows under the bar numbers, or put a new one in place of one of that name.
- `paw.ruler.draw_lanes(buf, x, scroll, span, folds)`: Draw the lanes on `buf`, the rows under the bar numbers, one under the other. `x` is the column of a beat; `scroll` and `span` the beats in sight; `folds` the view's closed time folds (paw/folds.tl), if any.
- `paw.ruler.label(bar, beat, style, cursor_beat, room)`: The pieces of bar `bar`'s label, from the parts in `paw.opt.barlabel` in their order. `bar` is the song's bar: in a scope with time, its label counts from 1 at the scope's start (`paw.scope.bar_offset`). `style` is the style of the bar's number there. `room` is how many columns the label has before the next bar's: each part gets what the parts before it left (`ctx.room`).
- `paw.ruler.lane_rows()`: How many rows the lanes need now, all together.
- `paw.ruler.relative(bar, beat)`: How many `W` (ahead) or `B` (behind) reach bar `bar` from the cursor at `beat`: from inside a bar, the first `B` goes to its own start (paw/defaults/cursor.lua). Nil for the cursor's own bar.
- `paw.ruler.remove(name)`: Take a part away, and its name out of `paw.opt.barlabel`.
- `paw.ruler.remove_lane(name)`: Take a lane away.
- `paw.ruler.set(name, patch)`: Change a part that is there, the built-in `number` too: its `order`, `render`, and the `glyphs` and `styles` it draws with (merged into its own). The part becomes a changed copy, as with `paw.trackcolumn.set`: `paw.ruler.add(name, old)` puts back the table it had before.

  ```lua
  paw.ruler.set("number", { styles = { cursor = "Title" } })
  ```
- `paw.ruler.set_lane(name, patch)`: Change a lane that is there, the built-in `regions` too: its `order`, `rows`, `render`, and the `glyphs` and `styles` it draws with (merged into its own). The lane becomes a changed copy: `paw.ruler.add_lane(name, old)` puts back the table it had before.

## Module paw.scene

- `paw.scene.closed(client)`: A connection closed or stopped to watch. paw keeps no more data for it.
- `paw.scene.live()`: The values that move the bound nodes of a frontend (see the `bind` of crates/paw-scene). These are the playhead, the clock and the load of the engine. For each track id, they are the meter, the recent peak, the clip light and the input. paw rounds them to what a frontend can show. So a program that does nothing has no new data to send (the load is as `paw.audio.load` gives it, as `frontend.watch` sends it). Each call gives the current values.
- `paw.scene.set_pace(ms)`: Tick every `ms` while something moves (`frontend.pace`).
- `paw.scene.turn()`: Call it after a turn of the kernel. paw pushes now, not at the next tick, the windows whose drawing can be different.
- `paw.scene.wake()`: Something started to move (the song, a note played): tick at the pace from now.
- `paw.scene.watchers()`: The watchers: `{ client, windows }` each. `windows` is the names of the windows whose size it gave.

## Module paw.scope

- `paw.scope.apply(s)`: Tell the engine what the rest of the song does for a scope. This is the scope of the tab in front, which the last seat to change tabs (a terminal or a window) selected.
- `paw.scope.at_cursor()`: The scope that `znn` enters at the cursor: the innermost not entered yet. On a closed time fold (paw/folds.tl), its region or its bars; a subproject's clip at the cursor; in a region scope, the region one level inside it at the cursor; else the closed fold of tracks whose row the cursor is on (paw/folds.tl), else the group at the cursor (its header or one of its tracks), else the track. Nil when the window shows that track already.
- `paw.scope.bar_offset(s)`: How many bars of the song come before the first bar of a scope (the current one by default) when its bars are numbered from 1: 0 with no time, or with `scopebars=song`. A scope's bars are the song's (its meter map), counted from the bar its time starts in.
- `paw.scope.breadcrumb(s)`: The path in words: `Song › Bridge › Strings`; a subproject is marked `⧉`: `Song › ⧉Ballad › Strings`.
- `paw.scope.children(s)`: The scopes one level inside a scope (the current one by default): for a region scope, the regions one level inside its region (paw/markers.tl), in order of time; for a group scope, its members (a group or a track), in order. Each has that scope as its parent. Other kinds have none.
- `paw.scope.contains(track, s)`: True if a scope (the current one by default; a group's id is a scope of that group) shows a track: it and every level above it do. With no scope, every track is inside.
- `paw.scope.current(win)`: The scope a window shows, or nil for the song: the window given, else the window being drawn, else the current one. A level whose group, track or region is gone is left out.
- `paw.scope.describe(s)`: What a scope shows, in words: its path, its tracks and its bars.
- `paw.scope.enter(spec, win)`: Enter a scope (`{ kind, id, tracks, from, to, name }`) in a window (the current one by default). In a window that shows a scope, it becomes its child: it shows what both show, and an empty one is refused with the reason. Changes nothing in the project; a jump. Returns the scope.
- `paw.scope.find(which)`: A group by its id, its track, or its name (or part of it).
- `paw.scope.format(beat)`: A place as the scope numbers it: `bar.beat.hundredths`, as `paw.time.format`.
- `paw.scope.group(s)`: The innermost group of a scope's path (the current scope by default): what a narrowed window's tracks are shown under. Nil when no level is a group.
- `paw.scope.group_at(track)`: The group of a track when you narrow: the track itself if it is a group. If not, the group that contains it.
- `paw.scope.held()`: The parts of the rest the engine plays from files now.
- `paw.scope.holder(win)`: The window whose scope and folds an action changes: the one given, else the current one; its stack's keeper.
- `paw.scope.limits_tracks(s)`: True if a scope, or one of the levels above it, limits the tracks.
- `paw.scope.local_bar(song_bar)`: The bar the current scope shows for a bar of the song.
- `paw.scope.name(name, win)`: Name the current scope, so that the picker and `:narrow` find it again. View state, kept with the project's screen. Returns it.
- `paw.scope.named(which)`: A scope by name: a named scope (`:scope.name`), else a group of that name, else a region of that name, else a group or a region whose name starts with it. A number is a group's id.
- `paw.scope.names()`: The named scopes, the latest last.
- `paw.scope.narrow(which)`: Narrow to a group or a region, by its id, its track or its name (see `named`): `enter` of that scope in the current window. Returns the scope.
- `paw.scope.nest(s)`: The innermost subproject of a scope's path (the current scope by default), or nil when the path is in the song: its tracks and its timeline are what the window shows.
- `paw.scope.next(n)`: Go to the scope `n` places beside the current one (`]z`, `3]z`, `[z`), in the same parent. A jump. Returns the scope.
- `paw.scope.of_clip(id)`: The scope of a subproject's clip (`znn` or `<CR>` on it enters it), or nil when the clip places no subproject.
- `paw.scope.of_region(r)`: The scope an operator's region covers (`zn{motion}`, `{Visual}zn`): the region, group or track its text object names (`ar`, `ag`, `it`), else a block of its tracks, with its time when it has some. Nil for the whole of what the window shows (`ie`).
- `paw.scope.of_tab(tab)`: The scope of a tab: that of its current window.
- `paw.scope.open(how, spec)`: Open a scope (the one at the cursor by default) in a new window: `how` is "split", "vsplit" or "tab". The new window starts with the scope of the one it comes from, and enters this one inside it.
- `paw.scope.origin()`: The song's beat of beat 0 of the time the window shows (the window being drawn, else the current one): in a subproject, where its block starts; else 0. `paw.time` adds it, so that a subproject's bars are the song's bars at its place.
- `paw.scope.path(s)`: The levels of a scope's path (the current one by default), from the outermost to it.
- `paw.scope.rest_parts(s)`: The parts of the rest of the song that paw can freeze for a scope. These are the tracks outside it at the top of their branch (a whole group, not its members). They are not the tracks that the sound of the scope goes through (its groups, and a bus that its sends reach). They are not empty.
- `paw.scope.restore(s, win)`: Show a scope in a window as it was (a jump back, `<C-o>`): no jump of its own, no check. Nil is the song.
- `paw.scope.saved_names()`: The named scopes as the project's screen keeps them (paw/layout.tl).
- `paw.scope.sibling(n)`: The scope `n` places after the current one (before it, with a negative `n`), beside it in the same parent: the next region, group or track; a block's next stretch of the same length. Nil and the reason when there is none.
- `paw.scope.song_bar(local_bar)`: The bar of the song for a bar as the current scope shows it.
- `paw.scope.song_beat(beat, s)`: The song's beat of a beat that the current scope shows.
- `paw.scope.song_offset(s)`: The beats to add to a beat of the window to get the song's beat: in a subproject, where the clip it was entered through places its beat 0 (the clip's start less its offset); else 0.
- `paw.scope.span(s)`: The time a scope shows (the current one by default): `from, to` in beats, its own time intersected with its parent's. Nil when it shows all of the song's time. `from` is `to` when the times do not meet.
- `paw.scope.tracks(s)`: The tracks of a scope (the current one by default), in the order of the track list. With no scope, or one that keeps every track, all tracks of the song; in a subproject, its tracks.
- `paw.scope.widen(top, win)`: Leave the scope of a window (the current one by default): up one level, or with `top` to the song. False when it shows the song.
- `paw.scope.window(win)`: The window whose scope and folds a view shows: the one given, else the one being drawn, else the current one; for a view that keeps no stack of its own (the mixer), the arrange window of its tab.

## Module paw.seats

- `paw.seats.close(id, why)`: Let go of a reason for `id`'s seat (or of all of them, with none): the seat closes with its last one.
- `paw.seats.copy(value)`: A deep copy of a value: tables are copied all the way down (their metatables are not), anything else is given back as it is.
- `paw.seats.enter(id)`: Make `id`'s seat the current one: an open seat, else the instance's. Returns the seat entered.
- `paw.seats.fields(name, tbl, keys, start)`: Keep fields of a table (a view's scroll, say) for each seat: `keys` names them, `start` gives what a new seat starts with (nil if absent).

  ```lua
  paw.seats.fields("mixer", view, { "scroll", "geometry" }, { scroll = 0 })
  ```
- `paw.seats.has(id)`: True if `id` has its own seat.
- `paw.seats.keep(name, get, set, fresh)`: Name some state that each seat has its own of. See the top of the file.
- `paw.seats.kind(id)`: What kind of seat `id` is, as a name that stays from one run to the next: "window" for the graphical window, "terminal" for a terminal (the instance's own, or one attached with `paw attach`). The seat of the instance with no terminal is the window that started it.
- `paw.seats.list()`: The seats there are, the instance's first.
- `paw.seats.open(id, why)`: Give connection `id` its own seat, for a reason (`terminal`, `window`). The seat stays while a reason stays.
- `paw.seats.within(id, fn, ...)`: Run `fn` in seat `id` (in the seat of the instance, if that seat closed), then return to the current seat.

## Module paw.shada

- `paw.shada.read()`: Read what is kept: yours, and the current project's.
- `paw.shada.use(file)`: Keep the files in `file` (and the project files where they always are), and keep for all start options, for tests. `use()` sets all back.
- `paw.shada.write()`: Write what is kept: yours, and the current project's.

## Module paw.slices

- `paw.slices.job(name)`: The job `name` while it runs, or nil.
- `paw.slices.run(name, step, opts)`: Call `step(ms)` again and again, each time from a timer of its own, until it returns true. The step works for at most `ms` milliseconds (`opts.ms`, 4) and keeps its place for the next call. The keys that wait run between two calls. `opts.after` is the time before the first call (0). A job of the same name stops first. An error in the step shows as a message and ends the job. Returns the job.
- `paw.slices.running()`: The jobs that run, by name.
- `paw.slices.stop(name)`: Stop the job `name`. Returns true if it was running.

## Module paw.snippet

- `paw.snippet.active()`: The active snippet, or nil. A snippet ends when the project changed other than through it, or the piano roll's cursor left its span.
- `paw.snippet.add(spec)`: Add a snippet, or replace one of the same name. A snippet from an extension never replaces one from the user's configuration.
- `paw.snippet.context(opts)`: The context of an expansion in the piano roll, or nil and why not. `opts`: `at` (project beats, the cursor's when nil), `count`, `values`, `selection` (a region; the visual selection's when nil).
- `paw.snippet.describe_preview(spec, opts, result, why)`: Lines that tell what a snippet would write here.
- `paw.snippet.expand(name, opts)`: Expand a snippet at the cursor of the piano roll (or over its selection): `opts` `count`, `at`, `values` (a choice's value by name). Returns the active snippet, or nil and why nothing was written.
- `paw.snippet.finish()`: Stop the active snippet, and keep the notes that it wrote.
- `paw.snippet.get(name)`: The snippet of a name, or nil.
- `paw.snippet.jump(dir)`: Go to the next choice (`dir` 1) or the previous choice (-1). False when no snippet is active. Then the key can do its usual action.
- `paw.snippet.load_dir(dir, source)`: Load every `*.lua` file of a directory: each calls `paw.snippet.add` or returns a list of snippets. `source` is "config" or "extension".
- `paw.snippet.marks(clip_id)`: The active snippet's notes and span in the clip's beats, for drawing: `{ name, notes, from, to, label }`, or nil.
- `paw.snippet.offered(view)`: The snippets offered in `view` (the focused one when nil), by name.
- `paw.snippet.paint(p)`: Paint the snippet layer of the piano roll (order 40, see `views/pianoroll.lua`). It marks the notes of the active snippet, and shows its range along the bottom with the items of Tab and `<C-n>`. It shows the notes that the picker would write as ghosts.
- `paw.snippet.pick(opts)`: Open the picker of the snippets of the focused view. Enter expands the selected snippet `count` times.
- `paw.snippet.preview(name, opts)`: What a snippet would write here, but does not write: `{ notes, choices, ctx }` or nil and why.
- `paw.snippet.preview_marks(clip_id)`: The notes that the snippet under the selection of the picker would write, in the beats of the clip, to draw them. Nil when no picker of snippets is open.
- `paw.snippet.remove(name)`: Remove a snippet.
- `paw.snippet.step(dir)`: Step the current choice (the first when none is) to its next value (`dir` 1) or the one before (-1), and rewrite the notes.
- `paw.snippet.take_cmdline_selection()`: The selection the command line was opened over, once: what `:snippet` works on.

## Module paw.statusline

- `paw.statusline.component(name, spec)`: Add a component, as an extension does: `paw.statusline.component("pulse", function(ctx) return "♥" end)`, or with the fields of a table (`fn`, `min`, `rank`, `style`, `key`, `cond`).
- `paw.statusline.config()`: The status line's configuration as `setup` made it.
- `paw.statusline.customized()`: True if `setup` changed the line from the line that comes with paw.
- `paw.statusline.draw(buf, which, y, extra)`: Draw the status line along the first row of `buf`.
- `paw.statusline.frontend(width)`: What the window is told: the line as pieces, for the width it has.
