- `paw.statusline.grid_text(grid)`: A grid in beats as a note value: 1 is `1/4`, 0.25 is `1/16`.
- `paw.statusline.line(width, which, extra)`: The line for `width` columns, fitted: `{ left, right }` as `segments` gives them. `text` is for each side, as `{ text, style }` pieces with the separators between them, ready to draw or to send to a window.
- `paw.statusline.reset()`: Back to the line as it comes.
- `paw.statusline.segments(width, which, extra)`: The segments for a screen `width` wide, as `{ left = {...}, right = {...} }`. Each is a list of `{ text, style }` pieces with a `rank` (lower ranks go last) and the `section` that it came from. `pill` is for a colored label. `name` is for the segment that paw cuts before it removes segments.

  ```lua
  which: "status" (default), "winbar", "inactive_winbar" or "tabline"
  ```
- `paw.statusline.setup(opts)`: Change the line: only what is given changes. `sections` replaces the sections it names, `views` and the other bars likewise.
- `paw.statusline.tabline(width)`: What the tab line holds at its right end, as pieces, for `width` columns.
- `paw.statusline.tabline_always()`: True if the tab line shows with one tab.
- `paw.statusline.winbar(view, focused)`: What the window with the keys (or another) adds to its title bar: the text of the `winbar` (or `inactive_winbar`), or nil when there is none.

## Module paw.stems

- `paw.stems.command(ctx, opts)`: What `:render stems` and `:render <group>` do with the command's options.
- `paw.stems.confirm(plan, dir, opts)`: Show a plan and render it on `y`.
- `paw.stems.names_group(word)`: True if `:render <word>` names a group to render alone, and not a file: the name of a group, with no file ending.
- `paw.stems.plan(opts)`: What the stems would be: a list of `{ id, name, file, holds }`, in the order of the track list. `opts`: `dir` (where; `stems` in the renders folder by default, see `paw.render.renders_dir`), `format` ("wav", the default, "flac", "mp3", "ogg", "opus"), `tracks` (one per track, not per group), `group` (that group, or track, alone). In a narrowed tab, the parts of its group.
- `paw.stems.render(plan, opts)`: Write the stems of a plan, with `paw.render`'s options (`background` renders them one after another). Returns the files.

## Module paw.step

- `paw.step.action(name, fn)`: A new action for the controls: `fn(count)` runs in a target that has no action of that name itself.

  ```lua
  paw.step.action("accent", function(count) ... end)
  ```
- `paw.step.action_text(b)`: What a control does, in words: "rest", "keys =8t", "rest, tie while keys are held".
- `paw.step.actions()`: Every action that a control can do: the core's, then the actions of extensions (`M.action`).
- `paw.step.active()`: The name of the target that listens now, or nil.
- `paw.step.ask_input(track)`: Say that step input has no MIDI input for `track`, and why, and open the MIDI part of the track's list of inputs. True if it had to.
- `paw.step.bind(source, action)`: Let a control of the controller do an action while a target listens. `source` is `{ port, channel, note | cc }`; `port` and `channel` may be left out. `action` is a name (`paw.step.actions()`), `{ keys = "=8t" }` (types those keys in the view), or `{ down = "rest", held = "tie" }` (the first with no key held, the second while keys are held). It replaces the control of the same source, for this session: `:step.learn` keeps a control in the file.
- `paw.step.bindings()`: The controls, each `{ source, action, keys, down, held, saved }`.
- `paw.step.held()`: The pitches held now on the controller, in the order they were played.
- `paw.step.held_text()`: The pitches held, in words: "C4 E4".
- `paw.step.input(track)`: What step input listens to for `track`: its MIDI input's port and channel, or every port. Nil and why not when paw hears no MIDI: no port is listed or open, or the track's port is not connected.
- `paw.step.learn(action)`: Wait for the next key, pad or pedal of the controller, and bind it to `action` by its port, channel and note or cc, in the file of the controls.
- `paw.step.learn_cancel()`: Stop the wait of `:step.learn`.
- `paw.step.load()`: Read the file of the controls again: what it keeps replaces what it kept before. With no file, the default of the pedal. The controls from Lua (`M.bind`) stay as they are.
- `paw.step.paused()`: Why the keys only sound now: "playing" or "recording", or nil.
- `paw.step.refresh()`: Look again at which target listens: its track plays the controller, and with none the held keys are forgotten. A target calls it when it starts or stops listening.
- `paw.step.said()`: What a control did a moment ago ("rest", "back"), for the title; nil after a moment.
- `paw.step.source(track)`: The port that step input listens to for `track`, in a few words: `"Keystation 49"`, `"Keystation 49 · ch 2"`, `"all ports"`, or nil with no input.
- `paw.step.source_text(s)`: A control in words: "Test Pads C2 (note 36)", "cc 64 (pedal)".
- `paw.step.target(name, spec)`: Let a view take step input: `spec` as `paw.contracts.StepTarget` says. The first target whose `active()` is true listens. A second call with the same name replaces the target.
- `paw.step.unbind(source)`: Take away the control of `source`: `paw.step.unbind({ cc = 64 })` lets the pedal sustain again. True if there was one.
- `paw.step.untarget(name)`: Remove the target of a view (its extension unloaded).
- `paw.step.use(file)`: Keep the controls in `file`, for tests; with no file, where paw keeps them (nowhere with --clean). Then read them from there.
- `paw.step.velocity()`: The velocity of the notes entered, in words: "key", or a number.

## Module paw.stretch

- `paw.stretch.badge(c)`: The stretch, shift and loop of a clip in a few characters, for its label: "×1.5 +3st ↻". `stretching…` shows while paw makes its sound. Nil for a clip with none of these.
- `paw.stretch.carry(c, snap, by)`: Give `snap` the playback values of `c`. `snap` is the snapshot of a piece of clip `c` that starts `by` beats into it. The values are its stretch, shift and timebase, and its loop from the start of the piece. Returns `M.moved(c, by)`.
- `paw.stretch.file_at(c, by)`: The time in the file of an audio clip that plays `by` beats after its start. It obeys the stretch, the warp markers and the bend of the clip along the tempo (`clip.bent`, when it follows a tempo that changes in it).
- `paw.stretch.file_seconds(c, beats, at)`: Seconds of an audio clip's file that `beats` beats of it from beat `at` (its start when left out) play.
- `paw.stretch.fit(id, from, to)`: Stretch an audio clip over beats `from` to `to`. It starts at `from`, continues until `to`, and plays its current sound.
- `paw.stretch.follow(id, bpm)`: Make an audio clip follow the tempo, with its sound at `bpm`. If `bpm` is not given, it is the tempo at the start of the clip, for its current stretch. With `bpm` false, the clip keeps its time again. Its length changes with its stretch, so it plays the same sound.
- `paw.stretch.lead(c)`: The seconds of its file that an audio clip would play before its start, if it were longer at the start. This is the part of the first `offset` seconds of the file that plays.
- `paw.stretch.loop(id, on, beats)`: Loop a clip (`on` true), or stop its loop (false). `beats`, when given, is the length of the part that repeats.
- `paw.stretch.markers(c)`: A clip's warp markers as they are saved (`{ source, target }` each), nil for none.
- `paw.stretch.move_content(id, by)`: Move what a looped clip plays as `M.moved` says, in the project: its offset or notes (and other takes' notes), and where its loop begins.
- `paw.stretch.moved(c, by)`: The play position of a clip after its start moves `by` beats later (earlier below 0), while its sound stays at the same time. For sound, it is `offset`. For a looped clip, it is also `loop_start`, kept in one repeat. `shift` is how far its notes move (counted from the new start).
- `paw.stretch.pitch(id, semitones)`: Shift an audio clip's pitch to `semitones` (fractions allowed) above its file's.
- `paw.stretch.repeats(c, limit)`: Where a looped clip's repeats begin, in beats from its start, past the first: where its notches are drawn. At most `limit` (256) of them.
- `paw.stretch.reset(id)`: Play an audio clip's file at its own speed again, at its own length, without warp markers.
- `paw.stretch.set(id, ratio)`: Stretch an audio clip to play its file `ratio` times as long, with the same sound. It becomes longer or shorter from its start by the same ratio.
- `paw.stretch.sounding(c, notes, limit)`: The `notes` of a MIDI clip as they sound, counted from its start. For a looped clip, these are the notes of its repeated range again and again, each cut at the end of its repeat. At most `limit` of them.
- `paw.stretch.to(id, beats)`: Stretch an audio clip. Its current sound then lasts `beats` beats.
- `paw.stretch.warp_add(id, beat)`: Put a warp marker on an audio clip at `beat`. It pins the time of its file that plays there (nothing moves). Returns its index.
- `paw.stretch.warp_move(id, index, beat)`: Move warp marker `index` of a clip to play at `beat`. The sound between it and the markers next to it stretches, and the start and the end of the clip do not move. The stretch on each side stays between 0.25 and 4. Returns its index, which can be different.
- `paw.stretch.warp_near(c, beat)`: The index of a clip's warp marker nearest `beat`, and how far it is.
- `paw.stretch.warp_remove(id, index)`: Take warp marker `index` off a clip.
- `paw.stretch.warp_snap(id, step)`: Move every warp marker of a clip onto the nearest line of a grid of `step` beats (`paw.opt.grid` when left out), from the first on.

## Module paw.takes

- `paw.takes.badge(c)`: A clip's takes in a few characters, for its label: "2/4", or nil.
- `paw.takes.choose_at(track, take, beat)`: Make take `take` play in the piece of a track at `beat`, and join it to the pieces next to it where that is exact. Returns the clip, or nil if no piece there has such a take.
- `paw.takes.comp(track, take, from, to)`: Make take `take` play on a track from beat `from` to `to`. paw cuts each clip there with that number of takes at the two ends where it goes across them. paw selects take `take` for each piece between them. Then it joins again the adjacent pieces that play the same take, where that is exact (`M.join_pieces`). Clips without takes do not change. Returns the number of pieces that got the take, or 0 when no clip there has it. A piece named after its recording or its take is named after the take that it plays.
- `paw.takes.content(clip, index)`: What take `index` of a clip plays, as the clip would have it if that take were selected. For sound, it is `{ file, offset, gain }`, with the offset of the start of the clip in the file. For notes, it is `{ notes, controls }`, counted from the start of the clip. The take that plays is the content of the clip.
- `paw.takes.count(clip)`: How many takes a clip has (1 without any others), and which plays.
- `paw.takes.explode(id)`: Each take as a separate clip, on new tracks below the track of the clip, one take on each track. The clip keeps the take that plays. Returns the tracks.
- `paw.takes.join_pieces(track, from, to)`: Join the pieces of a track that continue exactly from one another (see `continues`). This applies to the pieces from beat `from` to `to`, with the pieces that touch each end. Returns the number of joins.
- `paw.takes.keep(id)`: Throw away every take but the one that plays.
- `paw.takes.lane_count(track)`: The number of take lanes that a track shows: the highest number of takes of its clips. None while they are hidden or when no clip has takes.
- `paw.takes.lanes_shown(track)`: True if a track shows its take lanes.
- `paw.takes.named_by_take(c, takes)`: True if the name of a clip comes from its takes: the name of the take that plays, or of the recording ("take 1" for "take 1.2").
- `paw.takes.new(id, name)`: Keep the sound of the clip as a take, and continue in a copy of it. The copy becomes the take that plays. Use it to try a variation. Returns its number.
- `paw.takes.of(clip)`: The takes of a clip: { active, list = { { name }, ... } }, or nil for a clip that has only what it plays.
- `paw.takes.piece(c, from, to, shift)`: The takes of a piece of a clip, from beat `from` to `to` of the timeline: what a cut gives to each side. Sound keeps its entries as they are (the offset of the piece tells where it is in them). Notes are those of the range, counted from the start of the piece. Nil for a clip without takes. All notes of a looped clip go with each piece, moved by `shift` as the notes of the piece are (see `paw.stretch.moved`).
- `paw.takes.record_over(id)`: Make a new audio recording, clip `id`, the newest take of the audio clips under it on its track, instead of a clip on top of them. paw cuts those clips where the recording starts and ends. Each piece gets all the takes of the recording, lined up, and plays the take that the recording plays. What the piece played before stays as a take. The part of the recording where no clip was stays a clip. Returns the number of clips that got takes.
- `paw.takes.remove(id, index)`: Discard a take: by default the take that plays. Then the take before it plays. With one take left, the clip becomes a clip without takes again.
- `paw.takes.select(id, index)`: Play take `index` of a clip. One undo step. Returns the take's name.
- `paw.takes.shift(id, by)`: Move the notes of a clip's other takes by `by` beats, as its own are moved when its start is trimmed or its content slipped.
- `paw.takes.show_lanes(track, on)`: Show a track's take lanes, or hide them (`on` false).
- `paw.takes.step(id, by)`: Step through a clip's takes, round and round.
- `paw.takes.toggle_lanes(track)`: Show the take lanes of a track, or hide them. Returns true if they show.

## Module paw.tempo

- `paw.tempo.at(beat)`: The tempo at a beat (the start if left out).
- `paw.tempo.bar_of(beat)`: The bar that contains a beat, counted from 1.
- `paw.tempo.bar_start(n)`: Where bar `n` (the first bar is 1) starts, in beats.
- `paw.tempo.beats_to_seconds`: the same as `paw.api.tempo_seconds`.
- `paw.tempo.commands(command)`: Define the tempo and time signature commands with `command`.
- `paw.tempo.describe()`: The whole map as text, for example "120 bpm 4/4 at bar 1, 90 bpm from bar 3 with a ramp, ...".
- `paw.tempo.is_bar_line(beat)`: Whether a bar starts at this beat of the window's time.
- `paw.tempo.label(point)`: What a tempo change reads as on a ruler: "96" or "120>" for a ramp.
- `paw.tempo.lines(from, to, limit)`: The bar and beat lines from one beat to another: { beat, bar, index }, `index` 0 on a bar line (bars count from 1).
- `paw.tempo.marks(from, to)`: Tempo and signature changes from one beat to another, for a ruler to mark: { beat, text, kind = "tempo" | "signature" }, the start's left out.
- `paw.tempo.place(text)`: A place given to a command: a bar (`17`), a bar and beat (`17.3`), a bar of the song (`@19`), or `cursor` / `here`. The beat of the cursor when nothing is given. In a scope with time (`paw.scope`), bars are its own, from 1 at its start; `@19` is bar 19 of the song all the same. The beat is of the window's time (in a subproject, from its start).
- `paw.tempo.point_at(beat)`: The tempo point in effect at a beat.
- `paw.tempo.points()`: Every tempo point, the start's first: { beat, bpm, ramp }.
- `paw.tempo.remove(beat)`: Remove the tempo change at `beat`.
- `paw.tempo.remove_signature(bar)`: Remove the signature change that starts bar `bar`.
- `paw.tempo.seconds_between(from, to)`: Seconds from beat `from` to beat `to`.
- `paw.tempo.seconds_to_beats`: the same as `paw.api.tempo_beat`.
- `paw.tempo.set(beat, bpm, opts)`: Set the tempo from `beat`. With `opts.ramp`, ramp from here to the tempo of the next point, and do not hold. Without it, a point keeps its value.
- `paw.tempo.set_points(tempos, signatures)`: Replace the whole map: `set_points({ { beat = 0, bpm = 120 } }, { { beat = 0, num = 4, den = 4 } })`.
- `paw.tempo.set_signature(bar, num, den)`: Start bar `bar` (the first bar is 1) in `num`/`den`, up to the next change.
- `paw.tempo.signature_at(beat)`: The signature at a beat, as two numbers.
- `paw.tempo.signatures()`: Every signature point, the start's first: `{ beat, bar, num, den }`.

## Module paw.tempolane

- `paw.tempolane.add(beat, bpm)`: A tempo change at a beat, which holds. If a change is there, it gets the tempo.
- `paw.tempolane.bpm(fraction)`: The tempo at a height in the row (a fraction, 0 at the bottom), to a whole beat a minute and never below 20.
- `paw.tempolane.commands(command)`: Define the tempo lane's commands with `command`.
- `paw.tempolane.draw(points, step)`: A stroke of the pencil: `points` are `{ beat, bpm }` as they were drawn. They replace the changes over the stretch drawn across (the start's stays, with its tempo taken from the stroke if it reaches it), each a slope to the next, at most one to `step` beats.
- `paw.tempolane.fraction(bpm)`: Where a tempo is in the row, 0 at the bottom, 1 at the top.
- `paw.tempolane.move(beat, to, bpm)`: The change at `beat` to another beat and tempo. The start's change keeps its beat and changes its tempo.
- `paw.tempolane.ramp(beat, on)`: Make the change at `beat` ramp to the next, or hold again.
- `paw.tempolane.range()`: The tempo at the bottom and at the top of the row. The range keeps a small space around the slowest and the fastest tempo of the map, in tens of beats a minute. The range is at least 80 and centered. So a steady song does not show as a wall.
- `paw.tempolane.remove(beat)`: Remove the change at `beat`. You cannot remove the change at the start.
- `paw.tempolane.show(on)`: Show the row, or hide it (`on` false).
- `paw.tempolane.shown()`: True if the row shows.
- `paw.tempolane.toggle()`: Show the tempo lane, or hide it. Returns true if it shows.

## Module paw.textbuf

- `paw.textbuf.add_number(text, col, n, limit)`: Add `n` to the number at or after column `col` of a text, up to column `limit`. A sign before it counts. Decimals also count, and paw keeps them. Returns the new text and the column of the last character of the number.
- `paw.textbuf.align(rows)`: Put cells in columns. Each column is as wide as its widest cell, with two spaces between columns. paw removes the spaces at the end.
- `paw.textbuf.apply(buf, steps)`: Apply steps as one undo step, then read the buffer again. A step that fails takes back what the steps before it did, and the buffer keeps its changes.
- `paw.textbuf.buf()`: The buffer shown in the keyboard's window, if it is a text buffer.
- `paw.textbuf.cells(text)`: The cells of a line: the stretches between runs of two spaces or more (or a tab), each with the column it starts at.
- `paw.textbuf.changes(buf)`: The changes that the lines ask for, compared with the data that paw read. These are the lines that paw cannot read, and the items deleted, changed (with the fields that changed), copied and added. It also tells if the kept items are in a different order.
- `paw.textbuf.copy_lines(lines)`: A copy of lines (`{ text, id }`).
- `paw.textbuf.current()`: The text buffer window the keyboard is in.
- `paw.textbuf.exec(line)`: Run a line typed after `:` in a text buffer. Returns true when it was the buffer's to run.
- `paw.textbuf.here()`: The window, its buffer, the buffer's text and the window's cursor.
- `paw.textbuf.increment(n)`: Add `n` to the number at or after the cursor (`Ctrl-a`, `Ctrl-x`).
- `paw.textbuf.insert(how, opts)`: Start insert mode at the cursor of the current window. `how` is "i" before the cursor, "a" after it, or "I" at the first character that is not a space. It is "A" at the end, "o" on a new line below, or "O" above.
- `paw.textbuf.join(ctx)`: Join lines (`J`).
- `paw.textbuf.kind(name, spec)`: Make a kind of text buffer. It shows for the names that its `pattern` matches (`paw://` and the others). See `docs/reference/lua-views.md`. A kind with `readonly` (the message for a change) cannot change. `gutter = false` removes the line numbers. paw does not read a `static` kind again when the project changes. `paint(canvas, x, y, text, kind, width, row, buf)` draws a line in place of the usual colors.

  ```lua
  paw.textbuf.kind("clips", { pattern = "^paw://clips$", read = ..., format = ..., parse = ..., plan = ... })
  ```

  A kind also has the fields of a buffer type, next to the text: `keymaps`, `motions`, `textobjects` and `operators` (see `paw.layout.powers`. Their `ctx` has `buf`, `kind`, `args` and `target`). `describe(ctx)` is for `K`, and `status(ctx, line)` is for the `view` component of the status line. Its keys are in key scope `textbuf.<name>`, before the keys of the text.
- `paw.textbuf.kind_of(target)`: The kind a buffer name is of, and what its pattern took from it.
- `paw.textbuf.open(name, opts)`: Show a text buffer: in this window (`opts.here`), split below (beside with `opts.vertical`), or in a graphical frontend's window of its own (`opts.window`). Returns the window.
- `paw.textbuf.plan(buf)`: The plan a buffer's changes make: `{ text, run }` steps, or nil and why (and the line that does not read).
- `paw.textbuf.put(before, register, count)`: Put a register's text after the cursor, or before it (`p`, `P`).
- `paw.textbuf.quote(name)`: A name as a cell: quoted when it would not read back as itself.
- `paw.textbuf.reload(buf)`: Read the buffer again from the project: the text, what it was read from, and its undo list.
- `paw.textbuf.replace(ctx)`: Replace the characters under the cursor with the one typed (`r`).
- `paw.textbuf.same(a, b)`: True if the values of two fields are the same: numbers within a small tolerance, and tables field by field.
- `paw.textbuf.sync(buf)`: Call it after the project changed. paw reads an unmodified buffer again. paw marks a modified buffer as older than the project.
- `paw.textbuf.text(lines)`: A text of lines (`{ text, id }`) that keeps its own undo, as a buffer's `state.text`.
- `paw.textbuf.tilde(ctx)`: Swap the case of the characters under the cursor (`~`).
- `paw.textbuf.undo(redo, n)`: Undo `n` changes of the text, or redo them.
- `paw.textbuf.unquote(cell)`: A cell's text without the quotes `quote` put round it.
- `paw.textbuf.width(s)`: How many characters a string has (UTF-8).
- `paw.textbuf.write(buf, force)`: `:w` in a text buffer: the plan, to confirm. With `force`, also when the project changed after paw read the buffer.

## Module paw.track_kinds

- `paw.track_kinds.add(name, opts)`: A new track of the kind `name`. `opts.name` is its name (if not given, the title of the kind without "track"), and `opts.index` its place. The other options go to `create`.
- `paw.track_kinds.clear(which)`: Make a track an ordinary one again, as far as its kind goes: what the kind made (its devices) stays, for the extension to take away.
- `paw.track_kinds.define(name, spec)`: Define a kind of track (see above). `name` is a word: what is typed after `:track.add` and kept in the track's `meta.kind`.
- `paw.track_kinds.describe(which)`: A few words on a track's kind, for `K` and the track header: `Vocal track · Kitane`, "vocal (no extension here defines it)", or nil.
- `paw.track_kinds.known_words()`: ": there are vocal, drums", for messages.
- `paw.track_kinds.list()`: The defined kinds, in the order they were defined.
- `paw.track_kinds.of(which)`: The name of the kind of a track: the kind that it keeps. If not, a kind whose `is` claims it. Nil for a usual track.
- `paw.track_kinds.open(clip)`: Open a clip in its track's kind's editor. True when it did.
- `paw.track_kinds.remove(name)`: Forget a kind: no longer offered, nor in the menus. Tracks that keep it are ordinary tracks again until something defines it.
- `paw.track_kinds.set(which, name, args)`: Make a track of `name`'s kind: keep the kind on it, then let the kind make it what it is. `args` go to `create`.
- `paw.track_kinds.spec(which)`: A track's kind as defined, or nil (an ordinary track, or a kind that no loaded extension defines).

## Module paw.trackcolumn

- `paw.trackcolumn.add(name, spec)`: Add a component, or put a new one in place of one of that name. It goes into `paw.opt.trackcolumn` (unless `hidden`), so it shows at once.
- `paw.trackcolumn.click(L, x, track, ctx)`: A click at column `x` of the column on a line of `track`: the component there does what its `click` says. True if one had a `click`.
- `paw.trackcolumn.describe(track)`: What the components shown say of `track` for `K` (their `describe`), a line each, in their order.
- `paw.trackcolumn.draw(buf, L, y, track, ctx)`: Draw one line of the column for `track` at line `y` of `buf` (the column's own part of the view), with what `ctx` says of the line.
- `paw.trackcolumn.layout(frame, room)`: The column for one draw over the tracks of `frame`, at most `room` columns wide: the components named in `paw.opt.trackcolumn`, in their order, each as wide as it says. A component that fails takes no room.
- `paw.trackcolumn.remove(name)`: Take a component away, and its name out of `paw.opt.trackcolumn`.
- `paw.trackcolumn.set(name, patch)`: Change a component that is there, the built-in ones too: its `order` (to put it elsewhere), `width`, `render`, `click`, `describe`, and the `glyphs` and `styles` it draws with (merged into its own). The component becomes a changed copy: `paw.trackcolumn.add(name, old)` with the table it had before puts that back.

  ```lua
  paw.trackcolumn.set("fold", { order = 5, glyphs = { open = "-", closed = "+" } })
  paw.trackcolumn.set("number", { width = 4, styles = { cursor = "Title" } })
  ```
- `paw.trackcolumn.set_sign(name, patch)`: Change a sign that is there, as `set` changes a component: its `priority`, `render`, `describe`, `glyphs` and `styles`.

  ```lua
  paw.trackcolumn.set_sign("diagnostics", { glyphs = { error = "E", warn = "W" } })
  ```
- `paw.trackcolumn.shows(name)`: True if component `name` is shown: added and named in `paw.opt.trackcolumn`.
- `paw.trackcolumn.sign(name, spec)`: Add a sign to the `signs` component: `render(track, ctx)` gives one character, or nothing. Where several give one, the highest `priority` shows. `nil` for `spec` takes the sign away.

## Module paw.ui

- `paw.ui.active()`: True if something moves on its own now: the song plays, a track listens to its input, or a moment after activity (`poke`), while meters fall.
- `paw.ui.arrange(width, height)`: The position of each visible view on a screen of the current size: a list of `{ name, win, x, y, w, h }`. The tab line is along the top when there is more than one tab. `.borders` contains the borders between windows, and `.nodes` the position of each node of the tree, to resize them.
- `paw.ui.ask_value(opts, set)`: Ask for an exact value on the command line: a number is the value, with its sign (`-6` is -6 dB), and `+=2` and `-=3` change the current value by a step.

  ```lua
  paw.ui.ask_value({ label = "Volume", now = -8, unit = "dB", min = -60, max = 12 }, function(v) ... end)
  ```

  The options are `show(value)`, which writes the current value, `parse(text)`, which reads one absolute value, and `min` and `max`, the limits of the value.
- `paw.ui.box(buf, title, style)`: Draw a box around a buffer's edge and return a buffer for the inside.
- `paw.ui.close()`: Close the float that has the keys, or the window of a view.
- `paw.ui.dock(name, opts)`: Add a view to the layout along one side of the screen.

  ```lua
  paw.ui.dock("clock", { side = "top", size = 5 })
  ```

  `side` is "top", "bottom" (above the status line), "left" or "right" (next to the arrange view). Without `size`, the view shares the space that is left. To dock a view that is already in the layout moves it. Other tabs put it in the same place when they show it.
- `paw.ui.draw_hints(buf)`: List the keys that can follow a half-typed command, in a box along the bottom of the screen.
- `paw.ui.draw_menu(buf)`: Draw the menus over the screen. Called last by `paw.ui.render`.
- `paw.ui.draw_popup(buf)`: The list of candidates, over the bottom of the screen immediately above the command line. It starts below the word that they complete.
- `paw.ui.focus(name)`: Give a view the keyboard, and show it first if it is hidden. The window that contains it gets the keys, and paw goes to the tab of that window.
- `paw.ui.focus_next(step)`: Focus the next (or with -1 the previous) window that takes the keyboard.
- `paw.ui.frame_ms()`: How many milliseconds at least go between two frames while something moves: 1000 / `paw.opt.fps`, as the option is now.
- `paw.ui.go(location)`: Go to a location in the view that shows it best, and focus that view. The piano roll shows notes, the device panel shows devices and parameters, and the arrange view shows tracks and time.
- `paw.ui.hide(name)`: Close the window of a view, in each tab. The view keeps its place for the next time. The last window of a tab does not close: it goes on showing the view, as `Ctrl-w c` leaves it.
- `paw.ui.hl(name, def)`: Define a highlight group: a table of `fg`, `bg`, `bold`, `dim`, `italic`, `underline`, `reverse`, `strike`, or the name of a group to follow. Colors are `#rrggbb`, or a number for one of the 256 colors of the terminal. On a terminal without 24-bit color, each `#rrggbb` shows as the nearest of the 256.
- `paw.ui.input(opts, on_submit)`: Ask for a line of text on the command line.

  ```lua
  paw.ui.input({ prompt = "Name: ", text = "Bass" }, function(text) ... end)
  ```

  paw does not call the callback when the user cancels the prompt. The options are those of the command line (`paw.views.cmdline.open`): `complete`, `history`, `on_change` (live preview), `anchor` (draw it next to its subject), `on_key`, `still` (the preview asks for a whole frame itself when it changes another view).
- `paw.ui.layer(view, part, name, order, paint)`: Draw `paint(ctx)` as a layer of a part of a view (`"arrange", "header"`). It replaces a layer with the same name (nil removes it). The view tells what `ctx` contains where it calls `paw.ui.paint`.
- `paw.ui.live(buf, draw_part)`: Draw a live part on `buf`: `draw(buf)` draws it, now and each time it is drawn again by itself.
- `paw.ui.live_drawing()`: True if a live part drawn now is one of the terminal's screen.
- `paw.ui.live_value(bind, props)`: While a live part is drawn again: set the props of a mark bound to `bind` (`position`, `meter:<id>`, or a value that a view's `live_values()` gives) to the values of now.
- `paw.ui.location(view, win)`: The location under the cursor of the focused view (or `view`). With `win`, the cursor of that window: each window of a view has its own.
- `paw.ui.locator(view, spec)`: Say how a view places locations (`{ uri, selector }`):

  ```lua
  at()            the location under its cursor, or nil
  position()      where its cursor is, as a list of numbers to sort by
  place(location) where a location is in it, the same way, or nil when it does not show it
  go(location)    put its cursor there
  ```
- `paw.ui.menu(items, opts)`: Open a menu of `items` at `opts.x`, `opts.y` on the screen. See the top of the file.
- `paw.ui.mouse(event)`: Send a mouse event to the view under the pointer, with coordinates relative to that view (and `view_x`, `view_y`, `w`, `h`, the position of the view). First, the floats over the views and a gesture in progress get it (`paw.mouse`).
- `paw.ui.notify`: the same as `paw.notify`.
- `paw.ui.open(name, opts)`: Open a view in a float over the other views. It takes the keyboard until `paw.ui.close()`.

  ```lua
  paw.ui.open("help", { title = "Keys", width = 80, height = 30 })
  ```
- `paw.ui.page(title, lines, opts)`: Show lines of text in a float. Each line is a string or `{ text = ..., style = ... }`. With `opts.bottom`, it opens at the end. `opts.width` and `opts.height` give its size (100 by 30).
- `paw.ui.paint(view, part, ctx)`: Draw the layers of a part of a view: views call this where the part is drawn.
- `paw.ui.place(root, x, y, w, h)`: Lay a tree of windows out over a rectangle, as `arrange` lays out a tab's: in whatever unit its sizes are in (a graphical frontend's pixels).
- `paw.ui.poke(ms)`: Keep the screen animated for some time, for example after paw plays a note.
- `paw.ui.recolour()`: Set each group again. Call it after `paw.opt.termcolors` changes.
- `paw.ui.redraw`: the same as `paw.api.ui_redraw`.
- `paw.ui.render(buf)`: Draw the whole screen. Called by the kernel.
- `paw.ui.render_live(buf)`: Draw the live parts of the screen again, on the frame drawn last. Called by the kernel (`paw.api.ui_redraw_live`). False when the screen must be drawn whole instead.
- `paw.ui.render_scene(name, w, h, cell, win)`: Draw one view alone as a scene for a graphical frontend (see crates/paw-scene). The scene is `w` by `h` units (fractions are permitted). `cell` is the cell `{ w, h }` of the frontend in pixels, and `win` is the window of the layout that it shows in, if any.

  The text that `render_view` writes in whole cells becomes the runs and fills of the scene. The strips that the view keeps under them become its pictures. A view that paints is one picture of the whole area. The kernel keeps the scene, and `paw.api.scene_end` tells what changed in it.
- `paw.ui.render_screen(buf)`: Draw the whole screen into `buf`: the tab's windows, floats, the status and command lines.
- `paw.ui.render_view(name, buf)`: Draw one view alone on a buffer of its own. A window of a graphical frontend shows the result (see `paw.canvas.open_view`). A pane of its main area also shows a window of the layout this way (`M.view_win`, while paw draws it). Braille shows there as dots (`paw.canvas`), because the font has no braille.
- `paw.ui.role`: the same as `paw.roles.define`.
- `paw.ui.show(name)`: Show a view: in its window if it has one in this tab, else where it was docked. A view has one window at a time: one on screen in another tab moves here.
- `paw.ui.size()`: The size of the screen in cells. This is the size of the terminal. For the seat of a graphical frontend that told the size of its main area, it is the size of that area (`paw.panes`). So paw measures a split there on what it shows.
- `paw.ui.start_ticker()`: Draw what moves while the song plays: from when it starts.
- `paw.ui.strip(buf, x, y, w, h, opts)`: Keep an area of a buffer for pixels: see `Buf:strip`. Where it is kept is in `paw.ui.rects.surfaces`: `{ key, name, win, x, y, w, h, cell = { w, h }, under, draw, paint }` each, in cells of the screen (`name` the view that kept it, `win` the id of its window, `paint` for a view's whole drawing, `buf:surface`).
- `paw.ui.surface(buf, x, y, w, h, name)`: Keep an area of a buffer for a view's pixels: see `Buf:surface`. A strip, kept for the view's window, whose drawing is the view's `paint`.
- `paw.ui.theme(groups)`: Define many highlight groups at once.
- `paw.ui.titlebar(buf, opts)`: Draw a title bar of one row along the top of a docked panel, and return a buffer for the rest of it. `opts`: `name`, `pill` (`{ text, group }`, before the name), `context` (after the name), `right` (state, at the right end), `reserve` (columns to keep free at the right end, for the view's own items), `focused`. When the panel has focus, the whole bar is in the accent color, inverted.

  ```lua
  local body = paw.ui.titlebar(buf, { name = "Mixer", context = "5 tracks", focused = ctx.focused })
  ```
- `paw.ui.toggle(name)`: Show the view `name` in its window, or hide it if it shows now.
- `paw.ui.transport()`: The transport as `paw.api.transport_get` gives it. While a frame is drawn, the one read first in that frame: the status line, the ruler and the views read it once between them.
- `paw.ui.view(name, def)`: Register a view. It replaces a view with the same name.

  ```lua
  paw.ui.view("clock", { render = function(self, buf) buf:text(0, 0, os.date()) end })
  ```

  Optional fields: `focusable` (default true), `on_key(self, key)` for keys with no mapping, `modal` (each key goes to `on_key`), `on_mouse(self, event)`, `on_show(self)`, `on_hide(self)`. A view is a buffer type with one buffer, with the name of the view or the name from `bufname`.

  `window_state` names the fields of the view's table that are each window's own (the cursor, the scroll, the open clip). Then any number of windows show the view, and the table holds the state of the window that draws or acts (`paw.layout.bind`). `window_fresh` names the fields a new window starts without, such as caches. Without `window_state`, the view shows in one window at a time. `open_target(self, target)` opens a thing by name in the window (`:e roll://7`), and `window_target(self)` gives that name back for a saved layout. `share` says what part of the room the view keeps where windows share it: `{ column, least, most }`.
- `paw.ui.visible(name)`: True if a view is on the screen now.
- `paw.ui.wake()`: Start the frames of what moves, unless they run: nothing happens when nothing moves.

## Module paw.ui.Buf

- `paw.ui.Buf.columns(self, widths, gap)`: Buffers side by side across this buffer, each with a width from the left, with `gap` columns between them (0 by default). A width of "*" takes the space that the others leave. paw does not make the buffers that do not fit.

  ```lua
  local name, body = buf:columns({ 12, "*" })
  ```
- `paw.ui.Buf.fill(self, x, y, w, h, char, style)`: Fill a `w` by `h` area at `x`, `y` with `char` in `style`, clipped.
- `paw.ui.Buf.hit`: the same as `paw.roles.hit`.
- `paw.ui.Buf.image(self, x, y, w, h, key)`: Show the picture of pixels `key` (`paw.canvas.image`) stretched over the cells `x, y, w, h`: as an image where the terminal or the window shows images, else in half blocks, two pixels a cell. Returns true where it is an image, as `buf:strip` does. A key that paw does not keep (any more) shows nothing.

  ```lua
  local key = paw.canvas.image(png_bytes)
  buf:image(0, 0, buf.width, buf.height, key)
  ```
- `paw.ui.Buf.keep(self, key, x, y, w, h)`: Keep the cells drawn in the area `x, y, w, h` as they are now, under `key`, to put back on a later frame with `buf:put_kept` instead of drawing them again. The caller knows when what they show is the same. A change of a highlight group forgets every kept area.
- `paw.ui.Buf.mark`: the same as `paw.roles.mark`.
- `paw.ui.Buf.plane`: the same as `paw.roles.plane`.
- `paw.ui.Buf.put_kept(self, key, x, y, w, h)`: Put back the cells kept under `key` (`buf:keep`), if they were kept from the same place on the screen: true when they were.
- `paw.ui.Buf.root(width, height)`: The buffer that covers a whole screen of the given size.
- `paw.ui.Buf.strip(self, x, y, w, h, opts)`: Keep an area for pixels that `opts.draw(g, px)` draws, where the terminal shows images. `g` is a painter of `paw.canvas`. `px` is `{ w, h, cell = { w, h }, fg, bg, view }`: the size of the strip, the cell of the terminal in pixels, and its colors. For a strip that is partly off its window, `view` is the part that shows (x, y, w, h). paw calls it after it draws the screen. `opts.key` names the strip, and paw keeps images by this name. For a view that can be in two windows, put the id of the window in it. The default is the view and its window. With `opts.under`, the cells that the view draws there stay above the picture (its cursor, labels, the playhead). If not, they are blank. False where there are no pixels (`paw.opt.graphics` off, a terminal without images, tmux, or a terminal that cannot put text over an image). Then the view draws cells there:

  ```lua
  local pictured = plot:strip(0, 0, plot.width, plot.height, {
    key = "curve:" .. win.id, under = true,
    draw = function(g, px) paw.plot.curve(g, px, { ... }) end,
  })
  ```
- `paw.ui.Buf.sub(self, x, y, w, h)`: A buffer for the area `x`, `y`, `w` by `h` of this one, clipped to it.
- `paw.ui.Buf.surface(self, x, y, w, h, name)`: Keep an area for the pixels of a view that paints (`name`, by default the view that paw draws), where the terminal shows images. Its `paint` draws there at the cell size of the terminal, after paw draws the screen. The cells stay blank. False where the terminal shows only cells. Then the view draws them:

  ```lua
  if buf:surface(0, 1, buf.width, buf.height - 1) then return end
  ```
- `paw.ui.Buf.text(self, x, y, text, style)`: Write `text` at column `x`, row `y` of this buffer in highlight group `style`, clipped to the buffer. Returns the number of columns written.

## Module paw.ui.keybar

- `paw.ui.keybar.check()`: The keys shown that nothing is mapped to, as `view mode key` strings: empty when every line tells the truth.
- `paw.ui.keybar.entries()`: The entries for what has the keyboard now, as `{ shown key, text }`.
- `paw.ui.keybar.set(view, mode, entries)`: Set the keys shown for a view in a mode ("n", "x", "i").
- `paw.ui.keybar.show(lhs)`: A key as a person reads it: `<leader>mm` is `Space mm`, `<C-w>c` is `Ctrl-w c`.

## Module paw.undofile

- `paw.undofile.dir(path)`: The undo folder of the project at `path`, or nil when paw keeps none.

## Module paw.util

- `paw.util.clamp(v, lo, hi)`: `v`, kept between `lo` and `hi`.
- `paw.util.copy`: the same as `paw.seats.copy`.
- `paw.util.expand_path(path)`: A path as typed, with `~` at its start for the home folder, as a shell reads it: `~/mix.wav`. Every command that takes a file name reads it so.
- `paw.util.fader_db(now, want, lo, hi)`: The level a fader goes to from `now` when it is moved to `want`: in its travel (`lo` to `hi`, the fader's when not given), but never back past where it is. A track at +10 dB that is turned down goes to +9, not to the top of the travel.
- `paw.util.fit(text, width)`: Cut or pad text to exactly `width` columns.
- `paw.util.inspect`: the same as `paw.inspect`.
- `paw.util.merge(base, extra)`: Shallow copy with the fields of `extra` laid over it.
- `paw.util.round(v, step)`: `v` rounded to the nearest multiple of `step` (1).

## Module paw.vca

- `paw.vca.assign(track, vca)`: Put a track under a VCA.
- `paw.vca.dissolve(vca)`: Take a VCA away: its tracks stay, at their own faders.
- `paw.vca.is_vca(track)`: True if a track is a VCA.
- `paw.vca.list()`: Every VCA, in the order of the track list.
- `paw.vca.make(tracks, name)`: A new VCA over `tracks` (ids or tracks), after the last track. Returns its track.
- `paw.vca.members(vca)`: The tracks in a VCA, in the order of the track list.
- `paw.vca.of(track)`: The VCAs of a track (their ids), in the order in which paw put the track in them.
- `paw.vca.unassign(track, vca)`: Take a track out of a VCA, or out of all of them without `vca`.

## Module paw.xml

- `paw.xml.child(el, name)`: The first child of an element with a name, or nil.
- `paw.xml.children(el, name)`: Every child of an element with a name (every child without one).
- `paw.xml.decode(text, opts)`: The root element of an XML text, or nil and what is wrong. `opts.spans` keeps where each element is in the text, for `encode` with `opts.source` (see `paw.api.xml_decode`).
- `paw.xml.element(name, attr, order)`: A new element: `paw.xml.element("Track", { id = "t1", name = "Bass" })`. Its attributes are written in the order of `order`, then the others by name.
- `paw.xml.encode(root, opts)`: The XML text of an element: see `paw.api.xml_encode` for `opts`.
- `paw.xml.escape(text)`: Text made safe for XML, in text and in an attribute's quotes.
- `paw.xml.number(el, name)`: The text of a child as a number, or nil.
- `paw.xml.text(el, name)`: The text of a child, trimmed; nil when there is no such child.

## Module paw.zip

- `paw.zip.read(data)`: The entries of an archive: a table of name to contents, and the list of names in the order of the archive (folders left out). Nil and why when it is not a ZIP archive or an entry cannot be read.
- `paw.zip.write(entries)`: An archive of `entries` (`{ name = , data = }` each, in order), stored without compression.

## Module paw.api

- `paw.api.audio_devices()`: The audio devices the system offers, and which are open.
- `paw.api.audio_reconnect()`: Try to open again the device that went away. Returns true when it is open.
- `paw.api.audio_test_device(opts)`: The simulated device of the `test` backend. `{ present = false }` disconnects it. `fail_after = n` disconnects it after n blocks of the next stream. `back_after = ms` connects it again `ms` after it goes.
- `paw.api.audio_use(opts)`: Open other devices, and remember them for the next run.
- `paw.api.audio_watch(opts)`: With `{ auto = false }`, paw does not open again a device that returns by itself. `period` is the interval between checks, in milliseconds.
- `paw.api.automation_hold(track, target, device, param, on)`: A control is held (a fader under the pointer) or let go: in touch mode it writes automation for as long as it is held. The control is named as a lane's target is.
- `paw.api.base64_decode(text)`: The bytes of base64 text, either alphabet, with or without its padding; spaces and line ends are left out. Nil and the reason when it is not base64.
- `paw.api.base64_encode(data, opts)`: Base64 of bytes. `opts.url` uses the URL alphabet (`-_`), and `opts.pad = false` leaves out the `=` at the end.
- `paw.api.blocks(device)`: The number of audio blocks that the engine finished since it started. With a device id, the number of blocks that this device ran: the blocks that it slept through do not count. A change sent to the engine is in effect in the block after the next one that finishes, so wait until the count is two more (the test helper `T.next_block` does this). Nil for a device that the engine does not have.
- `paw.api.canvas_export(path, format, pages, scale)`: Write drawings (the operations of `paw.canvas.paint`) to a file: `format` "pdf" (one page for each drawing), "svg" or "png" (the first). Each page is `{ ops, width, height }` in pixels. `scale` is the points for one pixel in a PDF (0.75: 96 pixels to the inch).
- `paw.api.canvas_image(bytes, w, h, format)`: Keep a picture of pixels for drawings to name (`paw.canvas.image`): `bytes` a PNG file, or straight RGBA `w` by `h` pixels row by row; `format` `"png"` or `"rgba"` (a PNG file is known without it). Returns its content key, its width and its height.
- `paw.api.canvas_pixels(key)`: A picture of pixels kept under `key`, as a window is sent it: its size and its pixels as straight RGBA in base64. Nil for a key not kept (any more).
- `paw.api.chain_write(track, file)`: Write a track's devices as a chain file: `file` (a `devices.json`) and the `.state` files of the plugins beside it. Returns the files.
- `paw.api.checkpoint_delete(file)`
- `paw.api.checkpoint_dir()`
- `paw.api.checkpoint_list()`
- `paw.api.checkpoint_restore(file)`
- `paw.api.checkpoint_write(name, id)`
- `paw.api.clip_add(track, opts)`: A clip of a defined kind: `kind` is its name, with `data` and `length`, and `version`, `timeline`, `offset`, `media`, `sound` and `signals` as `clip_custom` gives them.
- `paw.api.clip_add_notes(id, notes)`
- `paw.api.clip_collect()`: Make every clip that refers to a MIDI clip file outside the project the project's own. Returns how many.
- `paw.api.clip_controls(id)`: Controller, pitch wheel and pressure moves of a MIDI clip: { start, type = "cc" | "bend" | "pressure", number, value }.
- `paw.api.clip_custom(id)`: The content of a clip of a defined kind, as the project saves it: `{ type, version?, timeline?, offset?, data, media?, sound?, signals? }`. `data` is `{ json = value }`, a plain value (tables, strings, numbers, booleans; a JSON null reads as nil), or `{ text = { ext, text } }`, UTF-8 text in the kind's own format.
- `paw.api.clip_edit_add(id, edit)`: Add an edit to an audio clip's edit list (`edits.rs`): `{ kind = "gain", from, to, db }` or `{ kind = "pencil", at, channel, values }`, in seconds from where the clip starts in its sound. Returns how many edits it has.
- `paw.api.clip_edits(id)`: An audio clip's edit list, as `clip_edit_add` takes its edits (with times in seconds of its sound).
- `paw.api.clip_edits_clear(id)`: Take away an audio clip's edit list. Returns how many edits it had.
- `paw.api.clip_get(id)`
- `paw.api.clip_glue(ids)`
- `paw.api.clip_kind_define(name)`: Let `clip_add` make clips of the kind `name`: a lowercase word that is not `midi`, `audio` or another built-in. `paw.clip_kinds.define` calls it.
- `paw.api.clip_kind_remove(name)`: Stop making clips of the kind `name`. Clips of it that the project has stay.
- `paw.api.clip_kinds()`: The kinds of clip that extensions defined, by name (sorted).
- `paw.api.clip_list(track, from, to)`: --- clips --- The clips of a track, in timeline order. With `from` and `to` (beats), only those that overlap that stretch: a view that shows part of the song asks for what it shows.
- `paw.api.clip_normalize(id, level)`
- `paw.api.clip_note_add(id, note)`: One note at a time, by its place in the notes of the clip (from 1). The functions that add and change a note return its new place, because the notes stay in the order of their start.
- `paw.api.clip_note_at(id, pitch, beat)`: The note on `pitch` that sounds at `beat`, and its place in the notes of the clip. Nothing when there is no such note.
- `paw.api.clip_note_remove(id, index)`
- `paw.api.clip_note_set(id, index, fields)`
- `paw.api.clip_notes(id, range)`: The notes of a MIDI clip, in the order of their start. With a range `{ from, to, low, high }` (beats in the clip, pitches), only the notes that sound in it. The second value is then the place of each note in the whole list.
- `paw.api.clip_notes_edit(id, edit)`: Several at once, as one edit: `{ set = { { index = 3, start = 1 } }, remove = { 5, 6 }, add = { note, ... } }`. Every index is a note's place before the call.
- `paw.api.clip_peaks(id, n)`: `n` { min, max } pairs for all of the sound that an audio clip plays.
- `paw.api.clip_remove(id)`
- `paw.api.clip_reverse(id)`: Audio clip operations that leave the source file alone (session/clipops.rs).
- `paw.api.clip_set(id, key, value)`: Change a clip: a table of the entries to change, as `clip_get` gives them, or one `key` and its value. Only the key form clears an entry (`nil`).
- `paw.api.clip_set_controls(id, controls)`
- `paw.api.clip_set_custom(id, set)`: Replace what a custom clip's kind compiled, as one undo step: `data` (required), `media`, `sound` (a MIDI or audio content) and `signals` are all replaced (absent: none); `version`, `timeline` and `offset` stay as they are when absent. The data and the signals' bodies are plain values: a function, `userdata`, `cdata`, a table that holds itself, NaN, an infinite number or a string that is not UTF-8 is refused with where it is (`.frames[3]: a function is not data`), and so is data over 1 MB. Binary or big data goes in a media file.
- `paw.api.clip_set_notes(id, notes)`
- `paw.api.clip_source_length(id)`: Beats of sound left in an audio clip's file from where the clip starts in it.
- `paw.api.clip_to_cues(id, track)`: Copy a clip, with its `meta`, off the timeline of a track. Returns the copy's id.
- `paw.api.clip_warp_add(id, beat)`: Warp markers of an audio clip (`session/stretching.rs`), counted from 1.
- `paw.api.clip_warp_move(id, index, beat)`
- `paw.api.clip_warp_remove(id, index)`
- `paw.api.crc32(data)`: The CRC-32 of bytes, as zip and gzip use it.
- `paw.api.cue(list)`: `{ { track =, clip = id }, { track =, stop = true }, { track =, timeline = true }, ... }`, each with `quantize` (`bar` when not given: off 1/16 1/8 1/4 beat bar 2bars 4bars), `legato` and `from`: all on their boundary, timed together by the engine.
- `paw.api.cue_list(track)`: --- cues (session/cues.rs) --- A clip goes off the timeline with `clip_add(track, { cue = true, ... })`: it starts at 0, loops over its length, and plays only when cued. You edit it as a usual clip; `clip_set(id, "track", other)` moves it.
- `paw.api.cue_state()`: What each track plays and has in its queue, in the last report of the engine.
- `paw.api.deflate(data, format)`: Compress `data` with deflate, as `format` says: "raw", "zlib" or "gzip".
- `paw.api.device_add(track, kind, opts)`
- `paw.api.device_alias(old, new)`: Devices of `old`, a kind that was renamed, are made as `new`.
- `paw.api.device_call(id, method, data)`: A request to a device that accepts data from scripts. Bytes in, bytes out.
- `paw.api.device_editor(id, open)`: Show or hide the window of a plugin. With no second argument, toggle it.
- `paw.api.device_find(query)`: The kind of device installed that answers `query`, `{ kind, format, id, name, vendor }` (each optional), as an entry of `device_types`; nil when none does. It looks by `kind` (an old name too), else by the plugin's own `id` (a CLAP id, a VST3 class id in either case, an LV2 URI), else by `name` with the `vendor` (a kind without a vendor answers any), else by `name` in any case; `format` ("clap", "vst3", "lv2", "builtin") keeps to one format. The list of all kinds is not made, so it is quick with many plugins. `device_find_all` gives all that answer.
- `paw.api.device_find_all(query)`: Each kind of device installed that answers `query` (see `device_find`): all that answer the first test that finds one.
- `paw.api.device_get(id)`
- `paw.api.device_load(id, load)`: Load a preset into a device, as one undo step: `{ name =, state =, params =, factory =, call = }`. `call = { method =, data = }` is a `device_call` that changes the state of the plugin (`property.set` of an LV2 plugin). The state after it is kept.
- `paw.api.device_move(id, track, index)`
- `paw.api.device_note_names(id)`: What a plugin calls its keys, `{ [pitch] = name }` (CLAP `note-name`).
- `paw.api.device_param(id, name)`: One parameter of a device, named by its key, the device's own id for it or its name: its entry of `param_info`, with `value` (now) and `text` (that value as the device writes it).
- `paw.api.device_param_parse(id, name, text)`: The value that a text stands for, for a parameter, as the device reads it. An error when the device cannot read the text.
- `paw.api.device_param_text(id, name, value)`: A value of a parameter as text, as the device writes it ("440 Hz"). Without a value, the value now.
- `paw.api.device_post(kind, topic, data)`: Data for all devices of a kind, now and in the future (also the devices of a render). nil removes the topic. Returns `{ { device, error } }` for the devices that refused it.
- `paw.api.device_remove(id)`
- `paw.api.device_restart(id)`: Start again a device that stopped (a plugin that crashed).
- `paw.api.device_set(id, key, value)`: Change a device: a table of the entries to change, as `device_get` gives them, or one `key` and its value. Only the key form clears an entry (`nil`).
- `paw.api.device_set_param(id, name, value)`: Set a parameter of a device, named by its key, the device's own id for it or its name. The value is a number, or text as the device reads it ("440 Hz", "Saw").
- `paw.api.device_state(id)`: The state of a plugin. Give it as `state` when you add a copy of the device.
- `paw.api.device_types()`: --- devices ---
- `paw.api.engine_audible(tracks)`: Only these tracks heard for now, as a solo would, or all with nil.
- `paw.api.engine_follow(track)`: The track that plays MIDI input while no track is armed, as if monitored, or none with nil (`paw.opt.midi_follows_selection`).
- `paw.api.engine_follow_always(track)`: The track that plays MIDI input as if monitored, also while another track is armed, or none with nil. While set, it takes the place of `engine_follow`'s track. Step input sets it to the track of the clip it enters into, so that the controller sounds there.
- `paw.api.engine_get()`: --- engine ---
- `paw.api.engine_held()`
- `paw.api.engine_hold(track, file)`: Play a track from a sound file for now, as if it is frozen, or live again with nil. The project does not change (see `freeze.rs`).
- `paw.api.engine_midi_filter(name, rules)`: Controls of MIDI input that tracks do not get: they neither sound nor record. Scripts still hear them, as `midi.in` events with `filtered = true`. Each `name` (`"step"`, `"learn"`) keeps its own list beside the others; nil or an empty list removes it.
- `paw.api.engine_reset_stats()`: Forget the process times that `engine_get().blocks` recorded until now.
- `paw.api.engine_restart(opts)`
- `paw.api.engine_set_sleep(sleep)`: With true, devices at rest sleep through silence: a reverb after its tail, a synth with no note that sounds. When the song is stopped and nothing sounds, the whole engine rests. The sound is the same with false. `engine_get().device_sleeps` counts the blocks that devices slept through, and `engine_get().engine_rests` the blocks that the engine rested.
- `paw.api.engine_set_threads(threads)`: The number of threads that process tracks, with the audio thread. 0 lets paw select the number. `engine_get().threads` gives the number in use.
- `paw.api.env()`
- `paw.api.events_take()`
- `paw.api.fs_copy(from, to)`: Copy a file, or a directory with all it holds, to where there is nothing.
- `paw.api.fs_create(path)`: Make an empty file where there is none.
- `paw.api.fs_exists(path)`: True when a file or directory is there (a link that leads nowhere is not).
- `paw.api.fs_mkdir(path)`: Make a directory and the ones above it that are missing.
- `paw.api.fs_move(from, to)`: Move a file or directory; it is refused where `to` is there already.
- `paw.api.fs_remove(path)`: Remove a file, or a directory with all it holds: only for what paw or an extension made for itself, a cache or a temporary folder. The files of the user go to the trash (`fs_trash`) instead. Nothing there is no error.
- `paw.api.fs_sound(path)`: The format a sound file's header says: `{ rate, channels, seconds }` (`seconds` nil when the header does not say); an error for a file that is not one.
- `paw.api.fs_space(path)`: The space of the disk that holds a path: `{ free, total }` in bytes (free: what a program that is not root can use).
- `paw.api.fs_stat(path)`: `{ kind = "file" | "dir" | "link", dir, size, mtime }`, or nil when nothing is there. A link is looked at, not followed, for its kind, and `dir` is true if it leads to a directory.
- `paw.api.fs_trash(path)`: Put a file or directory in the freedesktop trash; returns where it is.
- `paw.api.grid_fill(x, y, w, h, fill, style, cx, cy, cw, ch)`: Restyle the area `(x, y, w, h)`, clipped to `(cx, cy, cw, ch)`, in `style` as `grid_text` takes it, and overwrite its characters when `fill` is given.
- `paw.api.grid_image(key, x, y, w, h, cx, cy, cw, ch)`: Draw the picture of pixels kept under `key` over the cells `(x, y, w, h)`, clipped to `(cx, cy, cw, ch)`, two pixels a cell in half blocks (`▀`): what a terminal that shows no images shows of it. False for a key not kept (any more).
- `paw.api.grid_keep(key, x, y, w, h, cx, cy, cw, ch)`: Keep the cells of the area `(x, y, w, h)`, clipped to `(cx, cy, cw, ch)`, under `key`, to put back on a later frame with `grid_put` when what they were drawn from has not changed.
- `paw.api.grid_live_begin(x, y, w, h, cx, cy, cw, ch)`: A live part of the screen is drawn over the cells `(x, y, w, h)`, clipped to `(cx, cy, cw, ch)`: what is under them is kept, to draw it again by itself (`paw.ui.render_live`). Returns its number for `grid_live_end`, or nil when no part of it is on the screen.
- `paw.api.grid_live_end(index)`
- `paw.api.grid_live_restore()`: Take the live parts off the frame drawn last, to draw them again. Returns how many there were.
- `paw.api.grid_live_seal()`: The frame is drawn: what is over the live parts now stays over them.
- `paw.api.grid_put(key, x, y, w, h, cx, cy, cw, ch)`: Put the cells kept under `key` back, if they were kept from the same area: true when they were. Nothing is drawn else.
- `paw.api.grid_surface(key, x, y, w, h, cx, cy, cw, ch, under)`: Keep the cells `(x, y, w, h)`, clipped to `(cx, cy, cw, ch)`, for pixels under the name `key` (`buf:strip`), over the text or `under` it. Returns the number of the surface for `grid_surface_ops`, or nil when no part of it is on the screen.
- `paw.api.grid_surface_ops(index, ops)`: The drawing a surface shows: the operations of `paw.canvas.paint`.
- `paw.api.grid_surfaces_seal()`: The view being drawn is done with the surfaces it kept: what is drawn over them from now on covers them.
- `paw.api.grid_text(x, y, text, style, cx, cy, cw, ch)`: Draw text at `(x, y)`, clipped to the rectangle `(cx, cy, cw, ch)`, in `style`: the number of a highlight group (`hl_id`), its name, a table of attributes, or nil. Returns the number of columns the text takes.
- `paw.api.hl_id(name)`: The number of the highlight group `name`, for the style of `grid_text` and `grid_fill`: a frame passes numbers, not names. The number stays the same for as long as paw runs, and follows the group when it changes. A group not defined yet has one too.
- `paw.api.hl_set(name, def, full)`
- `paw.api.inflate(data, format)`: The bytes `data` holds compressed as `format` says ("raw", "zlib" or "gzip"), and the number of bytes of `data` the compressed stream took (what follows is not part of it). Nil and the reason when they are not compressed so.
- `paw.api.input_levels()`: The level of each input channel of the device, as linear gain, whatever takes it.
- `paw.api.json_array(t)`: Mark a table (a new one without `t`) as a JSON array, so that `json_encode` writes it as `[]` when it is empty. Returns it.
- `paw.api.json_decode(text)`: Nil and the reason, when the text is not JSON.
- `paw.api.json_encode(value, pretty)`: JSON text of a value; `pretty` lays it out on lines, indented.
- `paw.api.lane_add(track, opts)`
- `paw.api.lane_add_point(id, beat, value)`
- `paw.api.lane_add_state(id, state)`: Add a state to a state lane, or replace the one of its name, as one undo step. Returns its index, from 0.
- `paw.api.lane_get(id)`
- `paw.api.lane_list(track)`: --- automation ---
- `paw.api.lane_points(id)`
- `paw.api.lane_remove(id)`
- `paw.api.lane_set(id, key, value)`: Change a lane: a table of the entries to change, as `lane_get` gives them, or one `key` and its value. Only the key form clears an entry (`nil`).
- `paw.api.lane_set_points(id, points)`
- `paw.api.lane_set_shapes(id, shapes)`
- `paw.api.lane_set_states(id, states)`: Replace the states of a state lane, as one undo step. A point that names a state no longer there names the last.
- `paw.api.lane_shapes(id)`: The shapes of the stretches that are not straight, `{ beat, shape, tension }` each by the beat of the point they leave: "hold" or "smooth".
- `paw.api.lane_states(id)`: The states of a state lane, whole: `{ name, state, params, call = { method, data }, program, bank }` each. A point's value is the index of one, from 0.
- `paw.api.lane_value_at(id, beat)`
- `paw.api.limit_hook(func)`: The time limit on Lua (`paw.limit`). The arguments are the function to call when a callback runs too long, and the time when the current callback must return (on the clock of `now`, nil when it returned). `limit_async` tells if paw finds an overrun inside compiled code too.
- `paw.api.limit_watch(deadline)`
- `paw.api.load_apart(on)`: Make plugins apart from the main loop (true), or wait for each as it is added (false, what scripts start with). Returns what it was.
- `paw.api.log(line)`
- `paw.api.log_get()`
- `paw.api.lua_devices()`: Every script found: `{ kind, path, name, category, error, active }`, `active` false for one hidden by a script of the same name in a directory of a higher rank.
- `paw.api.lua_devices_add(dir, rank)`: Look for devices in `dir` from now on; a script there wins over one of the same name in a directory of a lower `rank` (0 by default). Returns `{ added, changed, errors }`: kinds, kinds, and `{ kind, path, error }` for scripts that did not load.
- `paw.api.lua_devices_remove(dir)`: Look in `dir` no more: a script of the same name elsewhere makes its scripts' kinds from now on, or nothing does. Returns the kinds of the scripts that were there.
- `paw.api.lua_devices_rescan()`: Look at every script again, loading those that changed. Same answer as `lua_devices_add`; `changed` are the kinds whose devices are now behind their file.
- `paw.api.measure(opts)`
- `paw.api.measure_cancel(id)`
- `paw.api.measure_poll(id)`
- `paw.api.measure_start(opts)`
- `paw.api.media_adopt(file)`
- `paw.api.media_collect()`
- `paw.api.media_dir()`: Where new recordings and bounces go: `media` beside the project file, or the user's data directory before the project has one.
- `paw.api.media_list()`: The sound files of the project (session/media.rs): the files that paw cannot find, links to new paths, and copies into the folder of the project.
- `paw.api.media_missing()`
- `paw.api.media_peaks(file, offset, seconds, n)`: `n` { min, max, rms } for `seconds` of a sound file from `offset` seconds: the sound that the other takes of a clip would play.
- `paw.api.media_relink(from, to, anyway)`: A file with other bytes than `from` had is refused, unless `anyway`.
- `paw.api.media_search(dir)`
- `paw.api.media_store(megabytes, keep)`: Long files are played from the disk: past how many megabytes of decoded sound (0: never), and how many gigabytes of it are kept between runs. With no arguments, what is set: megabytes, directory.
- `paw.api.midi2_read(path)`: A MIDI 2.0 clip file (`.midi2`): `{ notes, controls, length, skipped }`, with times in beats; `skipped` says what the file held that a clip has no place for.
- `paw.api.midi2_text(path)`: A MIDI 2.0 clip file as text, one note or controller move to a line, as `paw clip cat` prints it.
- `paw.api.midi2_write(path, clip)`: Write notes and controller moves (`{ notes, controls, length }`) as a MIDI 2.0 clip file, all or nothing.
- `paw.api.midi_close_output(name)`
- `paw.api.midi_close_port(name)`
- `paw.api.midi_inject(event)`: With `port`, as if from the port of that name.
- `paw.api.midi_inject_ump(words)`: A Universal MIDI Packet (one or two 32-bit words), as if from a MIDI 2.0 port. Returns true if the engine plays that message.
- `paw.api.midi_inputs()`: --- MIDI input ---
- `paw.api.midi_open_output(name)`: A port of paw that other programs can read MIDI from. `midi_close_output` returns true if there was such a port to remove.
- `paw.api.midi_open_port(name)`: A port of paw that other programs can send MIDI to. `midi_close_port` returns true if there was such a port to remove.
- `paw.api.midi_outputs()`: --- MIDI output ---
- `paw.api.midi_select(which)`: Open only the ports that match these ids or names, or all of them with nil.
- `paw.api.midi_send(track, event)`: Send a MIDI message to one track's devices right now, outside the timeline.
- `paw.api.midi_test_ports(ports)`: The MIDI ports the null backend lists, as if plugged in.
- `paw.api.midi_ump(event)`: What an event is as a MIDI 2.0 packet: two 32-bit words.
- `paw.api.nest_add(opts)`: Make a subproject with its master track and no other track, as one undo step, for example `{ name = "Bridge", length = 32 }`. The length is in beats, and 32 when you leave it out. Add its tracks with `track_add({ nest = id })`. Returns its id.
- `paw.api.nest_get(id, key)`: A subproject as a table: its fields, `tracks` (its tracks in order, without its master) and `used` (whether the song plays it). With `key`, only that field of its own (`name`, `length`, `master`...): this is quicker.
- `paw.api.nest_list()`: --- nests (subprojects): tracks with a timeline of their own --- The ids of the subprojects, in the order they were made.
- `paw.api.nest_promote(clip)`: Promote the subproject of a block (`clip`) to song data, as one undo step: its tracks come back in a group named after it at the place of its return row, their clips at the row's beats, cut at the block. The group track gets the master's devices and then the row's, the sum of their faders in dB, the row's pan and sends, and their lanes (two volume lanes added in dB). The row, the master and the subproject go. Returns `group`, `tracks`, `from`, `to`, `zero` (the song's beat of the subproject's beat 0) and `combined` (the targets of the lanes made one). `paw.nest.promote` does the rest: regions, the meter, the view.
- `paw.api.nest_set(id, key, value)`: Change a subproject: a table of the entries to change (`name`, `length`, `tempo`, `meter`, `kind`, `meta`), as `nest_get` gives them, or one `key` and its value.
- `paw.api.note_off(track, pitch)`
- `paw.api.note_on(track, pitch, velocity, attr)`: Play a note on a track, with a MIDI 2.0 attribute if one is given.
- `paw.api.now()`
- `paw.api.plugins_add_dir(dir)`: Find CLAP and VST3 plugins in one more directory from now on (the directory of an extension), and register the plugins in it. Returns `{ kinds, notes }`: the device kinds found there and the files that paw cannot use. Returns nil where paw cannot find plugins.
- `paw.api.plugins_attach(path)`: Load an attachment: a native library that an extension ships, which paw offers each CLAP plugin that it makes from now on (see `crates/paw-plugins/include/paw_attach.h`). Returns the name of the attachment.
- `paw.api.plugins_remove_dir(dir, kinds)`: Stop to find plugins in a directory added with `plugins_add_dir`, and make no more devices of `kinds`, the kinds found there. Devices that exist continue to work.
- `paw.api.plugins_rescan(name)`: Examine the plugin files again (all, or those that `name` matches). This includes the files that failed before. Returns notes on the files that paw cannot use, or nil without plugins.
- `paw.api.preview_get()`
- `paw.api.preview_level(db)`
- `paw.api.preview_play(file)`: A sound file heard on its own over everything, outside the project.
- `paw.api.preview_stop()`
- `paw.api.proc_close_input(id)`
- `paw.api.proc_kill(id)`
- `paw.api.proc_read(id, max)`: A process started with `pipe = true`: what it wrote ("" when nothing, nil once it closed its output). `proc_write` writes to it. A `proc.output` event says when there is something to read.
- `paw.api.proc_spawn(argv, opts)`: --- helper processes and sockets ---
- `paw.api.proc_status(id)`
- `paw.api.proc_stop(id)`: Ask it to finish and let it: `proc_status` says when it has.
- `paw.api.proc_write(id, data)`
- `paw.api.project_backup(path, note)`: Write the project as it is now to a different file. The path of the project and its modified flag do not change. The file keeps `note` under `recovery`.
- `paw.api.project_changed_files()`: The files of the open project that changed outside paw and are not acted on yet: paths in its folder, or full paths outside it.
- `paw.api.project_file_text(value)`
- `paw.api.project_files()`: The files of a project kept in a folder, with what each holds and if it differs from the disk (see `:ls`).
- `paw.api.project_get(key)`: --- project --- The project as a table. With `key`, only that entry of the table: this is quicker (`edits`, which goes up with each change, is asked for on each key and each edit).
- `paw.api.project_keep_changes()`: Keep the project as paw has it: forget the changes made outside.
- `paw.api.project_load(path, opts)`: `opts.plugins_offline` opens it with all plugins offline. `opts.offline` is a list of devices (by id) to open offline.
- `paw.api.project_mark_saved()`: Count the project as it is now as saved, for a script that wrote what it holds somewhere itself (a clip opened alone, written back to its file).
- `paw.api.project_new()`
- `paw.api.project_recover(path, opts)`: Open a file written by `project_backup` as the project it was a copy of: under that project's own file name, and as changed. `opts`: `as_path` opens it under that file name instead (for a `.bak`, which has no note), and what `project_load` takes.
- `paw.api.project_reload()`: Read a project kept in a folder again, as one undo step.
- `paw.api.project_save(path)`
- `paw.api.project_save_files(paths)`: Save only these files of a project kept in a folder, by their path in it. Returns the paths written.
- `paw.api.project_screen()`: The tabs and windows that the project file keeps, as plain data, or nil. They are not part of the song: setting them is not an edit, and the next save writes them (paw/layout.tl).
- `paw.api.project_screen_set(value)`
- `paw.api.project_set(key, value)`: Change the project: a table of the entries to change, as `project_get` gives them (`{ name = "Song", tempo = 96 }`), or one `key` and its value. Only the key form clears an entry (`nil`).
- `paw.api.project_shelve()`: Put the open project aside, with its undo history, and open an empty project. `project_unshelve` brings the first project back exactly as it was. For checks that need their own tracks (extensions/doctor).
- `paw.api.project_shelved()`
- `paw.api.project_unshelve()`
- `paw.api.quit(code)`: --- kernel ---
- `paw.api.read_dir(path)`
- `paw.api.redo()`
- `paw.api.reload()`
- `paw.api.render(path, opts)`
- `paw.api.render_cancel()`
- `paw.api.render_check(path, ffmpeg)`: Nothing when a render can write `path`, or why not.
- `paw.api.render_formats(ffmpeg)`: What a render can write: `{ { name = "WAV", extensions = { "wav" } } }`.
- `paw.api.render_start(path, opts)`: Start a render on a separate thread. Then the events `render.progress` and `render.done`, `render.failed` or `render.cancelled` come.
- `paw.api.render_status()`: The render that runs now, `{ path, fraction, seconds, cancelling }`, or nil.
- `paw.api.rpc_clients()`
- `paw.api.rpc_push(client, event, payload)`: Connections on the control socket (crates/paw-core/src/rpc.rs). Push an event to one (false when it closed), list them, and tell the terminal of the input that paw handles now (0 for the terminal of paw). Also release the terminal of a connection.
- `paw.api.rpc_version()`
- `paw.api.runtime_file(path)`: The text of a file of the runtime that is built into the program, by its path under `runtime`: a module (`lua/paw/util.tl`) or a declaration of Teal (`types/paw.d.tl`). Nil when the program has no such file. The loader checks the types of a file in Teal with these.
- `paw.api.scene_begin(w, h)`: Start a scene `w` by `h` units big, for `scene_draw` and `scene_picture` to put nodes in.
- `paw.api.scene_blob(client, key)`: A drawing that `client` got from paw, by its content key.
- `paw.api.scene_cells(client, id)`: What `client` has of the window `id`, lowered to cells: as `ui_view_snapshot` gives a view, rows of runs of one style.
- `paw.api.scene_close()`
- `paw.api.scene_draw(name, cols, rows)`: Draw a view by itself, `cols` by `rows` cells, as a window shows it: its writes are the scene's runs and fills, its cursor and its theme's colors the scene's.
- `paw.api.scene_end(client, id)`: The scene made, kept as what `client` has of the window `id`: the patch (JSON) that brings what it had up to it, pushed to it as a `scene.patch` event (unless it is 0, the instance's own); nil when nothing changed. A second result false: the connection is gone.
- `paw.api.scene_forget(client, id)`: Forget what `client` was sent of the window `id`, or of all of them: its next scene of one is sent whole.
- `paw.api.scene_hit(client, id, x, y)`: What is under the point `x, y` (units) of what `client` has of the window `id`: `{ key, hit, at = { x, y }, rect = { x, y, w, h } }` (see `paw_scene::Scene::hit`), or nil.
- `paw.api.scene_open(rect, opts)`: While a view is drawn for a scene: a node over a rectangle of it, in units of the scene, that what is written until `scene_close` goes into. `opts`: `role` (a group without), `props`, `hit` (a press on it is on that), `bind` (`meter:4`), `key` (its name; the role and where it is without), `clip` (the part that shows). With `plane` (`{ x = axis, y = axis }`, each `{ domain, from, per }`, see `paw_scene::Axis`) it is a plane, whose kids are placed in its domain; with `into` (the key a plane was made with) it goes into that plane, `rect` in the plane's domain. False when paw draws no scene now, or there is no such plane, with nothing to close.
- `paw.api.scene_picture(rect, opts)`: A drawing (`paw.canvas` operations) over a rectangle of the scene: `opts` `ops`, `px` (`{ w, h }` it was drawn at), `under` (the cells drawn there go over it), `clip` (the part that shows).
- `paw.api.scene_roles(client, roles)`: The roles `client` draws itself: in what it is sent from now on, such a role goes without the cells that draw it for a terminal.
- `paw.api.signature_remove(beat)`
- `paw.api.signature_set(beat, num, den)`
- `paw.api.sleep(ms)`
- `paw.api.smufl(font)`: A music font's SMuFL metadata (`Leland`, the default, `Bravura` or `Petaluma`): `engravingDefaults`, `glyphBBoxes`, `glyphsWithAnchors` and `glyphs` (every glyph name with its code point). Nil for a font there is none of.
- `paw.api.smufl_outline(font, codepoint)`: A music font's glyph as path commands in staff spaces from its origin, y down (`{ "M", x, y, "C", ... }`), for a frontend that cannot draw the font. Nil for a glyph or font there is none of.
- `paw.api.sock_accept(id)`
- `paw.api.sock_close(id)`
- `paw.api.sock_connect(path)`
- `paw.api.sock_listen(path)`
- `paw.api.sock_read(id, max)`: The bytes that came, "" when none came, nil after the peer closed.
- `paw.api.sock_write(id, data)`
- `paw.api.sound_envelope(path)`: The levels of a sound file, any format the engine plays: `{ rate, channels, frames, seconds, peaks, peak, onset, blocks }`, levels as linear gain. `peaks` holds the loudest sample of each channel, `peak` the loudest of all. `onset(level, from)` gives the time in seconds of the first frame, at `from` seconds or later, where a channel is louder than `level` (nil when none is). `blocks(from, to, ms)` gives the loudest sample of each block of `ms` milliseconds (default 1) between two times in seconds.
- `paw.api.sound_write(path, opts, samples)`: Write a WAV file: `opts` is `{ rate, channels (2), bits (16, 24, or 32 for float) }`. `samples` is the interleaved samples as bytes of 32-bit floats in the order of the machine (`ffi.string` of a `float[?]`), or a function `(frame, count)` that gives them one piece at a time and nil at the end. Returns the number of frames.
- `paw.api.startup_enter()`: Open an item of the start that `paw --startuptime` times: a module, an extension, the configuration. `startup_leave` closes it with its line. Nothing happens when the start is not timed.
- `paw.api.startup_leave(label)`: Close the item `startup_enter` opened last: its line in the file of `--startuptime` gives its time with and without the items opened in it.
- `paw.api.startup_timed()`: True while `paw --startuptime` times the start.
- `paw.api.state_get(key)`
- `paw.api.state_set(key, value)`
- `paw.api.str_width(text)`
- `paw.api.tempo_at(beat)`
- `paw.api.tempo_bar_length(beat)`
- `paw.api.tempo_bar_of(beat)`: Bars count from 0 here; `paw.tempo` and `paw.time` count from 1.
- `paw.api.tempo_bar_signature(bar)`
- `paw.api.tempo_bar_start(bar)`
- `paw.api.tempo_bbt(beat)`
- `paw.api.tempo_beat(seconds)`
- `paw.api.tempo_from_bbt(bar, beat, fraction)`
- `paw.api.tempo_from_seconds(tempos, signatures)`: A tempo map from points placed in seconds, as other programs keep them: `tempos` is `{ { seconds, bpm, ramp } }`, `signatures` is `{ { seconds, num, den } }`. Each point's beat follows from the stretch before it, held, or ramped linearly in time. Returns `{ tempos, signatures, beat, seconds }`: the points in beats, as `tempo_set_points` takes them, and two functions that convert with this map, `beat(seconds)` and `seconds(beat)`.
- `paw.api.tempo_is_bar_line(beat)`
- `paw.api.tempo_lines(from, to, limit)`: The bar and beat lines from one beat to another: { beat, bar, index } each, `index` 0 on a bar line. At most `limit` of them (default 10000).
- `paw.api.tempo_points()`: Every point: `{ tempos = { { beat, bpm, ramp } }, signatures = { { beat, num, den, bar } } }`.
- `paw.api.tempo_remove(beat)`
- `paw.api.tempo_seconds(beat)`
- `paw.api.tempo_set(beat, bpm, ramp)`
- `paw.api.tempo_set_points(tempos, sigs)`: Replace the whole map: `tempo_set_points({ { beat, bpm, ramp } }, { { beat, num, den } })`.
