- `paw.api.tempo_signature(beat)`
- `paw.api.test_devices()`: Add devices that fail on purpose (`test.panic`, `test.nan`). Tests use them to see what a bad device does to the other devices.
- `paw.api.test_panic(why)`: Panic, as a bug in the program does. Tests use it to see what paw keeps.
- `paw.api.timer_start(ms, repeat, func)`: --- timers ---
- `paw.api.timer_stop(id)`
- `paw.api.toml_decode(text)`: The table of a TOML text, or nil and what is wrong (`line 4: ...`). Each table keeps the order of its keys in its metatable, `getmetatable(t).__keys`. A date or a time is its text.
- `paw.api.toml_encode(value, inline)`: The TOML text of a table; with `inline`, of any value on one line (`{ a = 1, b = "x" }`). The keys of a table come in the order of its metatable's `__keys`, then the others by name. A list of tables is an array of tables.
- `paw.api.track_add(opts)`
- `paw.api.track_attr_delay(id, attr)`: The milliseconds that the attribute map of the track moves a note with `attr` (below 0: earlier). 0 when the track has no attribute map.
- `paw.api.track_chain_file(track, file, refer)`: Give a track the devices of a chain file (a `devices.json`). With `refer`, the track refers to the file until the chain's first edit. Returns how many devices.
- `paw.api.track_collect()`: Make every track read from a folder outside the project, and every chain of devices read from a file outside it, the project's own. Returns how many tracks and how many chains.
- `paw.api.track_get(id, key)`: A track as a table. With `key`, only that entry of the table: this is quicker, because the table lists each clip of the track.
- `paw.api.track_import_folder(folder, index)`: Add the track of a track folder outside the project (a folder with a `track.json`) at `index` (from 1; the end when nil). The project refers to the folder until the track's first edit. Returns its id.
- `paw.api.track_list(opts)`: --- tracks --- The ids of the song's tracks, in their order. `{ nest = id }` gives the tracks of that subproject instead (without its master), and `{ all = true }` every track: the song's and each subproject's. Views list the tracks of their scope with `paw.scope.tracks()`.
- `paw.api.track_meter(id)`
- `paw.api.track_move(id, index)`
- `paw.api.track_remove(id)`
- `paw.api.track_set(id, key, value)`: Change a track: a table of the entries to change, as `track_get` gives them (`{ name = "Bass", volume = -6 }`), or one `key` and its value. Only the key form clears an entry (`track_set(id, "output", nil)`). An entry that is as it was is no change.
- `paw.api.transport_get()`: --- transport ---
- `paw.api.transport_play()`
- `paw.api.transport_record()`
- `paw.api.transport_seek(beats)`
- `paw.api.transport_set(key, value)`: Change the transport: a table of the entries to change, as `transport_get` gives them (`{ loop_enabled = true }`), or one `key` and its value. Only the key form clears an entry (`nil`).
- `paw.api.transport_stop()`
- `paw.api.trial_active()`
- `paw.api.trial_begin()`: --- audition (session/audition.rs) --- `trial_end(false)` discards the edits made after `trial_begin`. The project is then as it was and the undo history does not change. `trial_end(true)` keeps the edits as one step.
- `paw.api.trial_end(keep)`
- `paw.api.ui_attached()`
- `paw.api.ui_caps()`: What the terminal of the seat whose turn it is can show besides cells: `{ graphics, pixels, cell = { w, h }, pixel_mouse, fg, bg }`, `pixels` when a view can be shown in pixels there.
- `paw.api.ui_caps_set(caps)`: Say what that terminal can show, in the same form: its frontend does when it starts, and tests do.
- `paw.api.ui_client()`
- `paw.api.ui_cursor(x, y)`
- `paw.api.ui_detach(client)`
- `paw.api.ui_frame_snapshot(width, height, live)`: A frame drawn off screen as a terminal is drawn, for tests: whole, or with `live` only its live parts again on the frame this drew last (nil when the runtime says it must be drawn whole). Each row as its text and as its cells with their styles.
- `paw.api.ui_frames()`: The frames drawn so far: `{ full, live, unchanged }`: whole frames, frames of the live parts only, and of those the ones that changed no cell, which were not sent.
- `paw.api.ui_line_redraws()`: How many of the redraws (`ui_redraws`) were `ui_redraw_line`.
- `paw.api.ui_mouse(on)`: True if the terminal reports the pointer (`paw.opt.mouse`), for the screen that paw draws now.
- `paw.api.ui_redraw()`: --- screen ---
- `paw.api.ui_redraw_line()`: The prompt on the command line changed: draw its live parts again (the line and the list), on the frame drawn last, and tell the windows that show state that something moved. Cheaper than `ui_redraw`: the views under it are not drawn again.
- `paw.api.ui_redraw_live()`: Draw only the live parts of the screen again (the playhead, the meters, the status line), on the frame drawn last; a whole frame when one is asked for too, or the runtime says it is needed.
- `paw.api.ui_redraws()`
- `paw.api.ui_seat(seat)`
- `paw.api.ui_size()`
- `paw.api.ui_snapshot(width, height)`
- `paw.api.ui_view_snapshot(name, width, height)`
- `paw.api.undo()`: --- undo ---
- `paw.api.undo_adjust(before, label)`: Put the project back as it was before the last step, so that a command runs again and its edits take the step's place: `paw.commands.adjust`. `before` is the state the command started from, and `label` the step's new name.
- `paw.api.undo_adjust_cancel()`: Put the step back as it was, when the command run again failed.
- `paw.api.undo_checkpoint()`
- `paw.api.undo_current()`
- `paw.api.undo_diff(a, b)`
- `paw.api.undo_discard()`
- `paw.api.undo_file_open(dir)`: Read the undo file in the folder `dir` for the project that just opened. Gives `states`, the number of states that came back, or `stale` when the project's files changed after the undo file was written.
- `paw.api.undo_file_wait()`: Wait until the undo file that is being written is complete.
- `paw.api.undo_file_write(dir, bytes)`: Write the undo file in the folder `dir` after a save, in about `bytes` bytes at most. The write runs on a thread of its own.
- `paw.api.undo_goto(id)`
- `paw.api.undo_join(id)`: The edits of this turn join undo state `id`, the current one, and do not make a step of their own. For example, a snippet changed its choice.
- `paw.api.undo_keep(id, keep)`
- `paw.api.undo_keys(text)`
- `paw.api.undo_label(text)`: Give a name to the open step. The first name wins. nil removes a name given while the step changed nothing.
- `paw.api.undo_limits(steps, bytes)`: How many steps the history keeps, and about how many bytes of what they changed: `paw.opt.undo_steps` and `undo_memory` set these.
- `paw.api.undo_name(name, id)`
- `paw.api.undo_pending()`: `undo_pending` is true if the edits of this turn will close as a step. `undo_discard` puts back what they changed, and no step closes (`edit.before`, paw/hooks.tl).
- `paw.api.undo_project(id)`: A state's project as a project file holds it (the current state's by default), and the text of a project file for a project given as data: see extensions/projdiff.
- `paw.api.undo_reset()`: Make the project as it is now the start of its undo history, and unchanged: a MIDI file opened as a project (paw/midifile.tl).
- `paw.api.undo_step(n)`
- `paw.api.undo_travel(seconds)`
- `paw.api.undo_tree()`: The undo tree and checkpoints: crate::history, session/undo.rs.
- `paw.api.wait(ms)`: Let `ms` milliseconds pass. Timers fire and events come, as between the key presses of a person. `sleep` stops all of that. A script that waits for the result of a timer uses `wait`.
- `paw.api.warnings()`
- `paw.api.which(program)`: Where a program is on `PATH`, as `command -v` says; nil when it is not there. A name with a `/` is checked as it is.
- `paw.api.xml_decode(text, opts)`: The root element of an XML text, or nil and what is wrong (with the byte). An element is `{ name, attr, order, children, text }`: `attr` maps each attribute to its text, `order` lists them as written, `children` holds the child elements, `text` the text and CDATA directly in it (nil when there is none). References are read; an entity a DTD defines is kept as it is written. UTF-16 with a byte order mark is read too. `opts.spans` gives each element `span = { from, open, close, to, lead, tail }`, the bytes it takes in the text, so that `xml_encode` can write what is not changed byte for byte. `opts.meta` is set as the metatable of each element.
- `paw.api.xml_encode(root, opts)`: The XML text of an element (as `xml_decode` gives them, or made with the same fields). Attributes are written in `order`, then the others by name; numbers as the shortest text that reads back the same, or with at most `opts.digits` digits after the point. `opts.indent` puts each element on a line, indented by it. `opts.declaration` is written first (true: the usual one). `opts.source` is the text the tree was read from with `spans`: what did not change is written as it was, byte for byte, and the text around the root element too.
